publication.desc: Publications (articles, reports, book chapters) reporting empirical or theoretical work on public attitudes, perceptions, opinions and discourse about refugees and asylum seekers in Germany, Europe, or comparative contexts.
publication.narr: Include publications that present surveys, qualitative studies, media analyses or policy research explicitly about attitudes toward refugees/asylum seekers, acceptance, integration preferences, perceived threat, xenophobia, support for refugee-related policies, or changes in public opinion over time. Include works that analyse determinants (contact, political ideology, media exposure), subgroup differences, and longitudinal trends. Exclude publications that only address migration in general without specific attention to refugees/asylum seekers, studies solely about migration policy mechanics without public opinion, or historical/descriptive pieces that do not address attitudes or opinions.

research_data.desc: Survey and observational datasets containing measures of opinions, attitudes or behavioral intentions regarding refugees and asylum seekers (national or comparative public opinion surveys, panel data, targeted refugee attitude modules).
research_data.narr: Include datasets that contain items or scales measuring attitudes toward refugees/asylum seekers (e.g., willingness to accept refugees, perceived cultural/economic threat, policy preferences, social distance), contact with refugees, or modules on migration where refugee-specific items are present. Include cross-sectional and longitudinal survey data (national polls, ESS, Eurobarometer, SOEP modules, specialised refugee attitude surveys). Exclude datasets that do not contain any refugee-specific attitude items or only administrative records about asylum applications without attitudinal measures.

variables.desc: Variables and variable-level metadata capturing attitudes toward refugees/asylum seekers (single items and scales), related constructs (xenophobia, perceived threat, social distance, contact), and relevant sociodemographic controls.
variables.narr: Include variable descriptions and codes for items asking about opinions on refugees (e.g., 'Do you support accepting refugees?', 'Would you accept a refugee as a neighbor?'), scales measuring xenophobia or refugee acceptance, and variables on contact, media consumption, political ideology, age, education and region used as covariates. Exclude variables that only record migration status of respondents without any attitudinal content or variables about migration flows/policies without linking to public opinion.

instruments_tools.desc: Questionnaires, survey modules, validated scales and coding schemes used to measure public opinion and attitudes toward refugees and related constructs.
instruments_tools.narr: Include full questionnaires or modules that contain refugee-attitude items, validated scales for measuring xenophobia/social distance, vignette instruments about refugee scenarios, interviewer guidelines and codebooks, and instruments for measuring contact or media exposure relevant to refugee attitudes. Exclude instruments focused exclusively on administrative registration of refugees, technical asylum procedures, or instruments measuring migration policy capacity without attitudinal components.

publication.desc: Publications addressing general life satisfaction or global subjective well‑being, including measurement, determinants, cross‑national comparisons, and longitudinal changes.
publication.narr: Include empirical and theoretical studies that explicitly measure or analyse overall life satisfaction (single‑item global measures or validated scales), their correlates (income, health, social relations, employment), measurement properties, and population-level trends. Include comparative work using ESS, WVS, SOEP or other survey data. Exclude publications focused solely on domain-specific satisfaction (e.g., job satisfaction, marital satisfaction) unless they include a global life satisfaction measure or directly compare domain and global measures.

research_data.desc: Datasets containing measures of general life satisfaction or global subjective well‑being (single items or multi‑item scales) from national, cross‑national and panel surveys.
research_data.narr: Include datasets that provide the standard global life satisfaction items (e.g., 'All things considered, how satisfied are you with your life as a whole?') or validated scales (e.g., SWLS), with accompanying sociodemographic and contextual variables for analysis. Typical sources include SOEP, ESS, WVS, Eurobarometer, and other national surveys. Exclude datasets that only contain domain‑specific satisfaction measures without any global life satisfaction item.

variables.desc: Variable metadata for items and scales measuring general life satisfaction and related subjective well‑being indicators (item wording, response scales, scoring rules).
variables.narr: Include variables representing single‑item life satisfaction measures (with response ranges), composite scores from validated scales (e.g., SWLS total score), indicators for affective well‑being if used alongside life satisfaction, and standard demographic covariates. Provide coding information, missing value handling, and scale reliability where available. Exclude variables limited to domain satisfaction only unless accompanied by a global life satisfaction variable.

instruments_tools.desc: Survey instruments and psychometric tools used to measure global life satisfaction and subjective well‑being (questionnaire modules, SWLS, translation/validation documents, scoring manuals).
instruments_tools.narr: Include validated instruments (Satisfaction With Life Scale, single‑item global measures used in ESS/WVS), questionnaire modules containing life satisfaction items, translation and cultural adaptation reports, and documentation on administration and scoring. Exclude instruments that only measure domain‑specific satisfaction or affect without a global life satisfaction component.

publication.desc: Publications on general self‑efficacy (self‑perceived competence to cope with life’s demands), including psychometric studies, validations, correlational and intervention research.
publication.narr: Include empirical and theoretical work that uses or evaluates general self‑efficacy constructs (e.g., General Self‑Efficacy Scale), cross‑cultural validations, associations with health, education, employment and wellbeing, and interventions aimed at changing general self‑efficacy. Exclude studies focused exclusively on domain‑specific self‑efficacy (academic, health, occupational) unless a general self‑efficacy measure is also included.

research_data.desc: Datasets that include measures of general self‑efficacy (e.g., GSES items or equivalent scales) collected in surveys, panels or intervention studies.
research_data.narr: Include datasets with item‑level or scale scores for general self‑efficacy, longitudinal data tracking change in self‑efficacy, and trials that measure pre/post general self‑efficacy. Provide documentation on scale items and scoring. Exclude datasets containing only domain‑specific self‑efficacy measures without a general self‑efficacy instrument.

variables.desc: Variables and metadata for items and scales measuring general self‑efficacy (item text, response categories, total scores, reliability statistics).
variables.narr: Include variable descriptions for each GSES item (or equivalent), computed total or mean scores for general self‑efficacy, reverse‑coding rules, and reliability (Cronbach’s alpha). Also include demographic covariates commonly used in analyses. Exclude variables that only reflect domain‑specific self‑efficacy constructs unless accompanied by a general self‑efficacy variable.

instruments_tools.desc: Validated instruments and administration materials for measuring general self‑efficacy (e.g., General Self‑Efficacy Scale by Schwarzer and Jerusalem), translations, scoring guidelines and psychometric evaluations.
instruments_tools.narr: Include scale instruments (full item lists), scoring manuals, normative data, translation/adaptation reports, and guidance for use in surveys or interventions. Exclude instruments that exclusively measure domain‑specific self‑efficacy (e.g., academic self‑efficacy) when no general self‑efficacy instrument is present.

publication.desc: Publications examining antisemitism: prevalence, attitudes, stereotypes, conspiracy beliefs, historical and contemporary manifestations, hate crimes and policy responses.
publication.narr: Include empirical studies, surveys, qualitative analyses and reports that explicitly measure or theorize antisemitic attitudes, incidents, discourse, causes and consequences. Include research on measurement (scales), demographic correlates, intergroup dynamics, and evaluations of interventions or policies addressing antisemitism. Exclude general prejudice research that does not include antisemitic-specific measures or analyses, and works that only discuss Jewish history without linking to contemporary antisemitic attitudes or incidents.

research_data.desc: Datasets containing items or modules that measure antisemitic attitudes, beliefs, incident records or complaint datasets documenting antisemitic events.
research_data.narr: Include survey data with antisemitism items (stereotypes, social distance, Holocaust denial, conspiracy beliefs), incident databases (police/NGO records of antisemitic crimes), and longitudinal surveys tracking antisemitic attitudes. Include datasets with contextual variables enabling analysis (region, demographics, media exposure). Exclude datasets lacking any antisemitism‑specific measures or those limited to unrelated forms of prejudice without antisemitic indicators.

variables.desc: Variables capturing antisemitic attitudes and behaviours: items on stereotypes, social distance, conspiracy beliefs, Holocaust denial, experiences of antisemitic incidents, and related demographic/contextual covariates.
variables.narr: Include variable labels and item wording for antisemitism measures (e.g., agreement with antisemitic statements), coding for incident types, frequency counts, perpetrator/victim descriptors, and standard sociodemographic controls. Exclude variables that only measure general prejudice without items targeting antisemitic content.

instruments_tools.desc: Survey scales, questionnaires, codebooks and coding schemes used to measure antisemitism and to record antisemitic incidents (measurement instruments, vignette protocols, incident classification schemas).
instruments_tools.narr: Include validated antisemitism scales, questionnaire modules used in national/international surveys, coding manuals for incident databases, and methodological documentation on administering sensitive items. Exclude generic prejudice instruments that do not include antisemitism items and technical police systems unrelated to research classification.

publication.desc: Publications on work and employment: labor market participation, job quality, unemployment, employment transitions, workplace conditions and labour market policy evaluations.
publication.narr: Include empirical and theoretical studies that focus on employment status, job characteristics (hours, contract type, sector), unemployment/incidence, underemployment, labor market integration, returns to work, and policy impacts (active labour market programmes, minimum wage). Include research on subpopulations (youth, migrants, disabled) if employment is the central focus. Exclude publications that concern education, training, or retirement solely in non‑employment contexts unless linked to employment outcomes.

research_data.desc: Datasets with labour market and employment information: household and labour force surveys, administrative employment records, panel data and employer surveys.
research_data.narr: Include datasets containing employment status, occupation and industry codes, hours worked, contract type, earnings/wages, unemployment spells, job search behaviour, and employer-level variables. Typical sources: labor force surveys, SOEP, microcensus, IAB, administrative unemployment records. Exclude datasets without employment-related variables or those purely focused on education without employment linkage.

variables.desc: Variables describing employment and work: employment status, occupation, industry, working hours, contract type, wages, unemployment duration, job search and job quality indicators.
variables.narr: Include variable metadata for standard labour market items (employed/unemployed/out of labour force), ISCO/ISCO-88/ISCO-08/ISCO-08 mappings, NACE industry codes, hourly/daily/weekly hours, contract permanence, earnings (gross/net), unemployment spells and reasons for job separation. Also include variables on training, commuting, multipart job holdings and workplace characteristics. Exclude variables unrelated to labour market outcomes (purely educational test scores) unless used to analyse employment.

instruments_tools.desc: Survey modules, questionnaires, coding schemes and analytic tools for measuring employment and work (labour force modules, occupational/industry coding manuals, job quality indices).
instruments_tools.narr: Include standard labour force questionnaires, interviewer instructions, occupational/industry coding manuals (ISCO, NACE), job classification concordances, job quality measurement tools, and documentation for administrative employment registers. Exclude instruments that measure only non‑work constructs or that are irrelevant to measuring employment (e.g., medical assessment tools without occupational linkage).

publication.desc: Publications addressing occupational load, work-related stress, psychosocial and physical burdens at work, and their effects on health, safety, performance, and absenteeism.
publication.narr: Include empirical studies, reviews, and theoretical work that focus on workload, job strain, psychosocial risk factors (e.g. demands, control, effort-reward imbalance), occupational stress, burnout related to paid work, and interventions to reduce work-related burden. Include workplace health and safety reports, epidemiological studies linking work exposures to health outcomes, and policy analyses about occupational risk. Exclude publications on non-work-related stress (purely family or general life stress without workplace linkage), student academic workload unless explicitly framed as employment, and purely economic analyses of labor markets that do not address occupational burden or psychosocial/physical working conditions.

research_data.desc: Survey datasets, cohort studies and administrative data that measure work-related stressors, workload, exposures to physical/psychosocial hazards, and related health or absence outcomes.
research_data.narr: Include datasets containing measures of job demands, job control, effort-reward imbalance, working hours, shift work, ergonomic exposures, sickness absence, mental health indicators, and biomarkers linked to occupational burden. Include longitudinal employer or workforce panels, occupational health surveillance, and national working conditions surveys that enable analysis of exposure-outcome relationships. Exclude datasets that do not contain workplace-specific exposure or outcome variables (e.g. general population health datasets without occupational information) or datasets focused exclusively on non-occupational stressors.

variables.desc: Variables capturing workload and occupational burden such as job demands, working hours, physical workload, psychosocial risk scales, absenteeism, and health outcomes related to work.
variables.narr: Include variables measuring perceived workload, quantitative and qualitative job demands, time pressure, overtime, shift patterns, ergonomic strain, exposure to hazards, job control/decision latitude, effort-reward balance, burnout scales, stress, mental health symptoms, and sickness absence. Also include objective measures like recorded overtime hours, injury reports, and physiological stress markers if linked to work. Exclude generic stress variables with no linkage to occupational context.

instruments_tools.desc: Validated questionnaires and measurement tools for assessing occupational workload and psychosocial/physical burdens at work (e.g. JCQ, COPSOQ, ERI, burnout inventories).
instruments_tools.narr: Include descriptions and use of validated instruments for measuring job demands and occupational stress such as the Job Content Questionnaire (JCQ), Copenhagen Psychosocial Questionnaire (COPSOQ), Effort-Reward Imbalance (ERI) questionnaire, Maslach Burnout Inventory (MBI), Perceived Stress Scale (when used in occupational context), and workplace exposure assessment protocols. Also include time-use diaries, ergonomic assessment checklists, and employer absence records used to quantify burden. Exclude management tools or organizational audits that do not produce measures of workload or psychosocial/physical burden.

publication.desc: Publications on job satisfaction, employee attitudes toward work, facets of satisfaction (pay, supervision, tasks), and links with performance, turnover, and well‑being.
publication.narr: Include empirical studies, theoretical papers, and reviews that investigate overall job satisfaction or its components, determinants (e.g. job characteristics, rewards, leadership), outcomes (e.g. commitment, turnover intentions, productivity), and interventions to improve satisfaction. Include cross-national and sector-specific studies of satisfaction and measurement research about satisfaction scales. Exclude studies focused solely on customer satisfaction, student satisfaction unrelated to employment, or organizational climate papers that do not report job satisfaction measures.

research_data.desc: Datasets and surveys containing measures of job satisfaction and related employee attitude variables across occupations, sectors, and time.
research_data.narr: Include workplace surveys, employee panels, national labour force or working conditions surveys, and longitudinal studies that include single-item or multi-item job satisfaction measures and related covariates (e.g. pay, autonomy, working hours). Include employer-level datasets that record employee engagement or satisfaction metrics. Exclude datasets lacking explicit job satisfaction indicators or those focused on non-employee populations.

variables.desc: Variables representing global or facet-specific job satisfaction, affective and cognitive components of job attitudes, and related outcomes such as turnover intentions and organizational commitment.
variables.narr: Include variables for overall job satisfaction, satisfaction with pay, promotion opportunities, supervision, colleagues, work tasks, working conditions, and work-life balance; also include job engagement, commitment, turnover intention, and intention to stay. Include both single-item satisfaction measures and validated multi-item scales. Exclude variables that measure only organizational outcomes without an employee-reported satisfaction component.

instruments_tools.desc: Standardized instruments and scales to measure job satisfaction and related constructs (e.g. JSS, MSQ, single-item measures, engagement scales).
instruments_tools.narr: Include established instruments such as the Job Satisfaction Survey (JSS), Minnesota Satisfaction Questionnaire (MSQ), single-item global satisfaction questions, and related engagement or commitment instruments (e.g. Utrecht Work Engagement Scale where relevant). Include survey modules and questionnaires used in labour and working conditions surveys to assess satisfaction. Exclude instruments that measure only managerial performance or customer satisfaction without employee-reported satisfaction.

publication.desc: Publications on work in the context of enterprises and firms: workplace organization, industrial relations, employment practices, production processes, and company-level working conditions.
publication.narr: Include studies and reports that examine the relationship between work and the employing organization such as organizational structure, HR practices, workplace governance, industrial relations, occupational safety at the firm level, production organization, and case studies of companies. Include comparative studies of establishments, employer surveys, and policy analyses concerning workplace and firm practices. Exclude macroeconomic labor market analyses that do not address firm- or establishment-level work processes, and purely consumer-focused business research unrelated to employee work.

research_data.desc: Enterprise- and establishment-level datasets capturing workplace practices, employment structure, working conditions, and company-level outcomes.
research_data.narr: Include establishment surveys, employer panels, workplace audits, HR administrative records, and matched employer-employee datasets that record management practices, working hours, shift organization, collective bargaining coverage, occupational health interventions, and productivity measures. Include datasets enabling analysis at the firm or plant level. Exclude individual-level surveys without linkage to establishment identifiers or datasets that only report macroeconomic aggregates.

variables.desc: Variables describing firm/establishment characteristics and workplace arrangements such as firm size, sector, ownership, management practices, collective bargaining, shift systems, and workplace safety policies.
variables.narr: Include variables measuring establishment size, industry classification, ownership structure, presence of works councils or unions, HR practices (e.g. training, recruitment), shift organization, workplace safety measures, production technology, and employee composition by occupation. Include organizational outcome variables like productivity, absenteeism, and turnover at the firm level. Exclude variables that concern only individual attitudes without contextual linkage to the employing organization.

instruments_tools.desc: Instruments for assessing workplace organization and company-level practices such as employer questionnaires, organizational audits, and workplace assessment protocols.
instruments_tools.narr: Include employer survey instruments, organizational climate audits, management practice indexes, workplace risk assessment tools, and standardized establishment survey modules used to measure company-level working conditions and HR practices. Include protocols for matched employer-employee data collection. Exclude business tools focused solely on market performance or customer analytics that do not assess employee work or workplace organization.

publication.desc: Publications about work–life relations: work–family balance, reconciliation of employment and private life, flexible work arrangements, and effects on well‑being and family outcomes.
publication.narr: Include empirical and theoretical studies that investigate work–life balance, work–family conflict and enrichment, flexible working time, parental leave, telework and its effects on family life, and policies to reconcile work and private life. Include comparative policy analyses, interventions, and qualitative studies of lived experience. Exclude publications focusing exclusively on family dynamics without connection to employment, or on retirement and leisure that do not consider work–life interaction.

research_data.desc: Datasets measuring time allocation, work–family conflict, caregiving responsibilities, flexible work arrangements, and related outcomes such as well‑being and family functioning.
research_data.narr: Include time-use surveys, family and household panels, working conditions surveys with work–life modules, employer datasets on flexible work usage, and longitudinal studies tracking work and family outcomes. Include data capturing childcare arrangements, unpaid caregiving, commuting time, telework frequency, and leave uptake. Exclude datasets lacking indicators that link employment arrangements to family or private life domains.

variables.desc: Variables capturing work–life balance dimensions: work–family conflict/enrichment, flexible hours, telework, caregiving duties, commuting time, and perceptions of reconciliation between work and private life.
variables.narr: Include measures of work-to-family and family-to-work conflict, work–life balance satisfaction, number of hours in paid and unpaid work, schedule flexibility, telecommuting frequency, childcare use, caregiving time, and uptake of family leave. Include outcomes like mental health, relationship quality, and job retention as they relate to work–life integration. Exclude variables unrelated to family or private life (purely occupational variables without linkage to non-work responsibilities).

instruments_tools.desc: Measurement tools for assessing work–life balance and related constructs such as work–family conflict scales, time-use diaries, and flexible work use modules.
instruments_tools.narr: Include validated scales like the Work–Family Conflict Scale (Netemeyer et al.), Work–Life Balance questionnaires, time-use diary methodologies, survey modules on telework and flexible scheduling (e.g. EWCS modules), and instruments measuring caregiving burden. Include employer policies inventories that record leave entitlements and flexible arrangements. Exclude general well‑being instruments that do not include work–life items or tools measuring only organizational performance.

publication.desc: Publications covering employment, work organisation, occupations, labour relations, job quality, occupational health, and the sociology/economics of work.
publication.narr: Include broad empirical studies, reviews, and theoretical work about paid work and employment: labor market participation, occupational structure, working conditions, job quality, employment relations, skills and training, occupational health and safety, and policy interventions affecting work. Include sectoral, cross-national, and historical perspectives on work. Exclude content unrelated to employment (e.g. volunteer activities unless explicitly analyzed as work) and publications that do not address work or employment dimensions.

research_data.desc: General labour and employment datasets such as labour force surveys, panel studies, occupational statistics, and working conditions surveys that provide data on employment and work characteristics.
research_data.narr: Include national and international labour force surveys, panel datasets (e.g. labor panels), occupational classifications, employer-employee linked datasets, administrative employment records, and working conditions or occupational health datasets that capture employment status, occupation, industry, wages, and working hours. Exclude datasets without employment-related variables or those focused solely on non-labor domains.

variables.desc: Core employment and work variables including employment status, occupation and industry codes, working hours, wages, contract type, job tenure, and measures of job quality and working conditions.
variables.narr: Include variables for employment/unemployment status, full-/part-time, temporary vs. permanent contracts, occupation (ISCO), industry classification, hourly/weekly earnings, working hours, shift work, job tenure, training, and measures of job satisfaction and health as they relate to work. Also include standard demographic covariates used in labor research. Exclude variables that do not pertain to employment or the nature of work.

instruments_tools.desc: Standard instruments and classification systems used in work and employment research such as labour force questionnaires, ISCO occupational coding, industry classifications, and working conditions survey modules.
instruments_tools.narr: Include tools used to measure employment and work characteristics: labour force survey questionnaires, time-use diaries for work, occupational and industry classification systems (ISCO, NACE/WZ), standardized working conditions and occupational health survey modules (e.g. EWCS items), and administrative record linkage protocols. Include validated scales for job quality and work-related health. Exclude instruments unrelated to measuring work or employment.

publication.desc: Publications analyzing the changing nature of work and employment over time, including causes, patterns and consequences of structural, technological and organizational change.
publication.narr: Relevant publications: empirical and theoretical studies, review articles and policy reports that address transformations in work (e.g. digitalization, automation, platform work, flexibilization, demographic change), longitudinal analyses of occupational change, comparative/historical accounts of labor market restructuring, and evaluations of policies responding to change. Include works at micro (worker, firm), meso (occupation, sector) and macro (national, cross-national) levels. Exclude: publications that only mention the phrase without analysing change; narrow technical papers on specific technologies that do not address effects on work or employment; purely clinical or medical case reports unrelated to labor-market transformation.

research_data.desc: Datasets and data collections that capture changes in work and employment over time, including longitudinal panel surveys, repeated cross-sections and registries relevant to occupational transformation.
research_data.narr: Relevant data: longitudinal panel datasets (e.g. national panels), repeated cross-sectional surveys and time-series that measure employment patterns, job tasks, telework, skill requirements, contract types, occupational mobility, and firm-level restructuring; administrative registers on employment, industry/occupation matrices, and cross-national surveys tracking work conditions over time (e.g. EWCS, SOEP). Include documentation, codebooks and harmonised time-series. Exclude: datasets that only contain unrelated demographic data without variables on work change, single-company datasets with no information about structural change, or raw technical datasets about equipment with no labor-focus.

variables.desc: Variables that measure aspects of occupational change and the evolving nature of work, including employment type, job tasks, skills and mobility indicators.
variables.narr: Relevant variables: occupational codes and classifications over time (ISCO, national codes), job tenure, job-to-job mobility, incidence of temporary/atypical contracts, teleworking/remote work indicators, automation/technology-exposure measures, skill requirements/skill use scales, task content measures, part-time/full-time status, firm restructuring indicators. Exclude: variables that only measure generic demographics with no link to work change and variables limited to a single point in time without temporal comparability when the query concerns change.

instruments_tools.desc: Questionnaires, coding schemes and measurement instruments used to assess changes in work, occupations and job tasks.
instruments_tools.narr: Relevant instruments: survey modules and questionnaires on job tasks and task routineness, measures of digitalisation and platform work, occupational history calendars, instruments for coding occupations (ISCO concordances, national mappings), workplace change assessment tools, employer survey modules on restructuring and technology adoption, and validated scales for measuring skill use and task content. Exclude: technical engineering tools unrelated to labor outcomes, clinical assessment instruments not designed for workplace research.

publication.desc: Publications on work and occupations covering job characteristics, occupational choice, career development, vocational training and the labour market role of occupations.
publication.narr: Relevant publications: empirical studies, theoretical analyses and reviews that address occupations, career trajectories, vocational education and training, job characteristics, occupational segregation, sectoral differences, and labour market outcomes by profession. Include cross-sectional and longitudinal research, policy analyses and comparative studies. Exclude: papers solely about leisure or unrelated personal activities; studies that use 'occupation' only as a demographic label without substantive analysis of work or occupational processes.

research_data.desc: Datasets containing information on occupations, job histories, career development and vocational training suitable for research on work and professions.
research_data.narr: Relevant data: labour force surveys, occupation-coded microdata (with ISCO or national coding), employment registries, career history panels, vocational training modules, employer surveys capturing occupational structure, and harmonised cross-national datasets. Include metadata and codebooks that enable occupational analysis. Exclude: datasets lacking occupational or job-related variables, or datasets focused exclusively on non-work domains (e.g. purely health or housing surveys) unless they include substantive job information.

variables.desc: Variables that describe occupational status, job characteristics, career trajectories and vocational qualifications.
variables.narr: Relevant variables: occupation codes (ISCO, KldB), industry sector, job title, employment status (employee/self-employed), occupational prestige and skill level measures, vocational qualifications/training indicators, career path indicators (promotions, lateral moves), job tenure, full-/part-time status, and wage linked to occupation. Exclude: variables unrelated to employment or that only record employer identifiers without occupational detail.

instruments_tools.desc: Instruments and tools used to measure and classify occupations, career histories and vocational competences.
instruments_tools.narr: Relevant instruments: occupational classification manuals (ISCO, national classifications), job history calendars, questionnaires on vocational training and career development, coding tools and concordances between classification systems, career trajectory mapping tools, and competency assessment instruments. Exclude: measurement tools unrelated to occupational analysis (e.g. clinical psychometrics not adapted to workplace contexts).

publication.desc: Publications investigating work and job satisfaction, including determinants, consequences, measurement and cross-group comparisons of occupational well-being.
publication.narr: Relevant publications: empirical studies, theoretical papers, meta-analyses and policy reports on job/organizational satisfaction, its antecedents (job characteristics, working conditions, leadership, pay), consequences (health, turnover, productivity), and measurement approaches. Include research on intrinsic/extrinsic satisfaction, cross-national comparisons and sectoral studies. Exclude: works that only mention satisfaction in passing without measurement or analysis, and studies focused on life satisfaction without connection to job-related satisfaction.

research_data.desc: Datasets containing measures of job or work satisfaction and related work-context variables suitable for analysis of determinants and outcomes of job satisfaction.
research_data.narr: Relevant data: surveys and panels that include job satisfaction items (e.g. single-item or multi-item scales), workplace surveys, longitudinal datasets tracking satisfaction over time (SOEP, EWCS, ESS modules where applicable), and employer surveys with employee well‑being measures. Include data documentation and scales. Exclude: datasets lacking any job satisfaction or workplace-wellbeing indicators.

variables.desc: Variables measuring job satisfaction, facets of satisfaction, and related predictors/outcomes (work conditions, pay, autonomy, health).
variables.narr: Relevant variables: overall job satisfaction scores, facet-specific satisfaction (pay, supervision, tasks), Likert-scale items or validated composite scores (e.g. MSQ, JSS), variables on working conditions (hours, autonomy, demands), psychosocial risk factors, turnover intentions, absenteeism and mental/physical health indicators. Exclude: generic happiness variables without explicit reference to work, and variables that only capture employer-side satisfaction (management satisfaction with workforce) unless linked to employee outcomes.

instruments_tools.desc: Validated questionnaires and measurement tools for assessing job satisfaction and related workplace well‑being constructs.
instruments_tools.narr: Relevant instruments: standard job satisfaction measures (Minnesota Satisfaction Questionnaire, Job Satisfaction Survey, single-item measures used in large surveys), scales assessing facets of job satisfaction, psychosocial workplace instruments (e.g. COPSOQ, Job Content Questionnaire, Effort–Reward Imbalance), and survey modules capturing satisfaction-related constructs. Include translations and psychometric documentation. Exclude: instruments not targeted at job-related satisfaction or those without psychometric validation.

publication.desc: Publications on working conditions, including physical, psychosocial, contractual and temporal aspects of work and their impacts on health, safety and well-being.
publication.narr: Relevant publications: empirical research, reviews and policy analyses addressing occupational health and safety, psychosocial risks, work organisation, shift work, working hours, job control, workplace hazards, precarious contracts, and their effects on workers. Include intervention and evaluation studies, sector-specific analyses, and cross-national comparisons. Exclude: publications that only use the term superficially without analysing working conditions, and papers exclusively about non-work settings.

research_data.desc: Datasets that measure various dimensions of working conditions, such as physical exposures, psychosocial factors, schedules, and contract types.
research_data.narr: Relevant data: workplace and employee surveys (e.g. European Working Conditions Survey), occupational health surveillance data, employer records on work schedules and hazards, panel data with work-condition modules, and administrative inspections data. Include variable documentation, exposure metrics and health outcome linkages. Exclude: datasets without items on work environment, exposures or contractual/temporal conditions.

variables.desc: Variables capturing aspects of working conditions: physical demands, psychosocial factors, hours and scheduling, employment contract and safety exposures.
variables.narr: Relevant variables: physical workload, ergonomic risk factors, exposure to hazards (noise, chemicals), psychosocial measures (demands, control, social support), working time (hours, shift/night work, overtime), contractual form (temporary, permanent, agency), occupational safety incidents, and workplace accommodations. Exclude: variables that only identify occupation without information on the conditions of work, or variables limited to non-work environmental exposures.

instruments_tools.desc: Assessment instruments and tools for measuring working conditions, occupational hazards, health and psychosocial work environment.
instruments_tools.narr: Relevant instruments: COPSOQ, Job Content Questionnaire (demand-control-support), Effort–Reward Imbalance scale, EWCS survey modules, workplace risk assessment checklists, ergonomic assessment tools, shift-work questionnaires, safety reporting systems, and structured observational tools. Include translations, validation studies and guidance for application. Exclude: clinical diagnostic instruments unrelated to workplace exposures or tools solely for industrial engineering design without occupational-health focus.

publication.desc: Publications on unemployment, including its causes, duration, socio-economic consequences and policy responses at individual and population levels.
publication.narr: Relevant publications: empirical analyses, theoretical studies, policy reports and reviews addressing unemployment incidence, long-term unemployment, youth unemployment, unemployment duration and transitions, unemployment benefits and active labour market policies, and the socio-economic and health impacts of joblessness. Include cross-national comparisons and administrative-data based studies. Exclude: studies that only mention unemployment tangentially (e.g. as a control variable) without substantive analysis.

research_data.desc: Datasets and administrative registers containing unemployment measures, spells, benefit receipt and job-search behaviour for analysis of labour-market non-employment.
research_data.narr: Relevant data: labour force surveys with unemployment modules, panel datasets recording employment spells and transitions, unemployment registers and administrative benefit records, job-search surveys and youth transition studies. Include documentation on unemployment definitions, spell start/end dates and linkage to demographic and health data. Exclude: datasets without clear unemployment indicators or that only capture informal non-employment without unemployment measures.

variables.desc: Variables that define and measure unemployment status, duration, transitions, benefit receipt and job-search activities.
variables.narr: Relevant variables: unemployment status (according to ILO definition), start and end dates of unemployment spells, duration of unemployment, prior employment history, receipt and type of unemployment benefits, job-search intensity and methods, reason for job loss, re-employment indicators, and demographic correlates (age, education). Exclude: variables that only measure inactivity without distinguishing unemployment (unless clearly coded), and economic indicators at aggregate level without microdata linkage when individual-level analysis is intended.

instruments_tools.desc: Instruments, register systems and survey modules used to measure unemployment, job-search behaviour and programme participation.
instruments_tools.narr: Relevant instruments: labour force survey questionnaires (unemployment modules), administrative unemployment registers, benefit payment and caseworker databases, job-search and unemployment spell calendars, standardized coding for labour-status categories, and evaluation tools for active labour-market programmes. Exclude: tools not designed to capture unemployment or those focused exclusively on underemployment without unemployment measures.

publication.desc: Publications that study commuting/to-work journeys (Arbeitsweg), including travel time, mode choice, distance, congestion, active commuting, and health or wellbeing consequences of commuting.
publication.narr: Include empirical articles, reports and reviews that focus on the daily journey to and from work: determinants of commute mode, commute duration, spatial distance, multimodal trips, peak-hour dynamics, commuting-related stress, injury or exposure en route, and links between commuting and health, productivity or work–life balance. Also include urban planning and transport policy evaluations that target commuting. Exclude publications that treat non-work travel in general without distinguishing trips to/from workplace, or publications that only mention commuting peripherally without measured or analyzed commuting variables.

research_data.desc: Datasets and surveys containing commute-specific measures: travel time, distance, mode, frequency, route, departure/arrival times, and commute-related exposures (noise, pollution).
research_data.narr: Include travel and mobility surveys, time-use surveys with commute modules, household travel surveys, employer travel plans, GPS/transport sensor datasets, national transport or labour force surveys with commute variables, and longitudinal datasets that track changes in commuting. Exclude datasets lacking explicit measures identifying journeys to/from work (e.g., only general mobility without purpose) or datasets that only record workplace location without travel measures.

variables.desc: Variables that capture aspects of commuting: commute time, distance, travel mode, number of transfers, departure/arrival times, cost, congestion measures, and subjective commute satisfaction or stress.
variables.narr: Include measured or derived variables such as one-way travel time to work, round-trip commute duration, home–work distance, primary mode (car, public transport, bicycle, walking), multimodality indicators, peak/off-peak flags, route characteristics, commuting frequency, perceived commute stress, and exposures (air pollution, noise). Exclude variables that do not specify travel purpose or are aggregated mobility indices without work-specific attribution.

instruments_tools.desc: Measurement instruments used for commute assessment: travel diaries, GPS/accelerometer trackers, map-based route collection tools, commute modules in surveys, and validated scales for commuting stress.
instruments_tools.narr: Include survey modules and questionnaires asking about usual mode, travel time and distance to work; travel diaries and day reconstruction methods specifying work-trip entries; GPS tracking and smartphone apps that record routes and times; transport modelling tools for commute distance/time estimation; and psychometric scales specifically assessing commuting stress or satisfaction. Exclude instruments that record mobility only at an aggregate level without trip purpose or those unrelated to travel-to-work measurement.

publication.desc: Publications on working time (Arbeitszeit): hours of work, schedules, shift work, overtime, flexible hours, part-time/full-time distinctions, and related policy and health outcomes.
publication.narr: Include empirical studies, policy analyses and reviews examining contractual and actual working hours, temporal organization of work (shifts, night work, irregular schedules), overtime and unpaid hours, effects on health, wellbeing and family life, productivity, and legal/regulatory frameworks for working time. Exclude publications that focus solely on non-labour temporal measures (e.g., leisure time only) or that mention hours worked without analysis or measurement.

research_data.desc: Datasets and registers that record working-time information: employment surveys, time-use studies, payroll records, employer scheduling data, and longitudinal labour market datasets.
research_data.narr: Include national labour force surveys, enterprise payroll/administrative time records, working-time modules in social surveys (e.g., EWCS), time-use diaries capturing paid work episodes, and longitudinal panels measuring changes in hours or schedules. Prefer datasets with both contractual and actual hours, plus shift/roster indicators. Exclude datasets that lack explicit working-time measures or only contain aggregated employment counts without hours or schedule detail.

variables.desc: Variables describing working time: weekly/annual hours, contractual vs actual hours, overtime, shift type, start/end times, irregularity, part-time/full-time status, and schedule control.
variables.narr: Include numeric measures (paid hours per week/day, overtime hours), categorical indicators (shift work, night work, weekend work, flexible schedule), timing variables (typical start and end times), measures of schedule variability and predictability, and subjective items on satisfaction with working hours and perceived work–life balance. Exclude variables that only indicate employment status without any temporal detail.

instruments_tools.desc: Tools for measuring working time: time-use diaries, payroll and electronic time-stamp systems, employer scheduling software extracts, and standardized survey modules on working hours.
instruments_tools.narr: Include validated instruments and administrative sources used to measure hours and schedules: diary-based time-use instruments (with paid-work episodes), employer payroll registers and clock-in/clock-out logs, roster/schedule exports, and standard survey items from sources like the European Working Conditions Survey or Working Time Survey. Exclude general employment questionnaires lacking detailed time or schedule items.

publication.desc: Publications addressing foreigners/immigrants (Ausländer): migration status, integration, labour market outcomes, health disparities, discrimination, and demographic studies of foreign-born populations.
publication.narr: Include empirical and theoretical works that explicitly study foreign-born persons, migrants, or persons with migration background: labor market integration, educational attainment, health and wellbeing among migrants, social inclusion/exclusion, legal and policy analysis of immigration, and statistical descriptions of foreign populations. Include studies that use the term 'Ausländer' in context of nationality, citizenship or migration background. Exclude works that use the term only in passing, studies focused solely on tourists or short-term visitors, or publications that do not disaggregate by migration status or country of origin.

research_data.desc: Datasets with migration-related variables: population registers, migration surveys, labour force surveys with country-of-birth or citizenship variables, asylum registers, and longitudinal migration panels.
research_data.narr: Include administrative population registers that record nationality, country of birth and residency status, specialized migration and integration surveys, household surveys with migration modules, labour market datasets that allow comparison by migration status, and health surveys with migrant identifiers. Exclude datasets lacking any marker of migration/foreign origin or those that only capture temporary visitors/tourists without immigrant status.

variables.desc: Variables indicating foreign or migrant status: country of birth, citizenship/nationality, migration background, year of arrival, residence permit type, language proficiency, and naturalization status.
variables.narr: Include primary identifiers (country of birth, citizenship, nationality), derived measures (first/second generation, length of stay, age at arrival), legal status descriptors (refugee/asylum seeker, permanent/temporary permit), and integration-related measures (host-language skills, employment in host-country jobs). Exclude variables that only approximate migration indirectly (e.g., surname) unless linked to validated migration markers.

instruments_tools.desc: Instruments to measure migration status and integration: migration questionnaires/modules, administrative registers, language proficiency tests, and acculturation/integration scales.
instruments_tools.narr: Include standard survey modules asking about birthplace, citizenship, year of immigration, reason for migration, and residence status; administrative data linkages with registries; validated instruments for language assessment; and scales measuring integration, discrimination or acculturation. Exclude instruments that do not collect clear migration identifiers or that only offer informal proxies for foreign status.

publication.desc: Publications on burdens arising from work (Belastung von Arbeit), including psychosocial stressors, workload, physical load, occupational hazards, burnout and health consequences of work demands.
publication.narr: Include empirical and review studies that analyze how aspects of work create burden—psychosocial demands (workload, time pressure, emotional demands), physical strain (ergonomic load, repetitive movements), exposure to hazards, and resulting outcomes such as stress, burnout, musculoskeletal disorders, sickness absence or reduced well‑being. Include occupational health interventions addressing reduction of work-related burden. Exclude studies concerning non-work stressors unless they explicitly connect to or confound work-related burden.

research_data.desc: Datasets capturing job demands and work-related burdens: occupational health surveys, workplace assessments, longitudinal panels with psychosocial measures, and administrative sickness/absence records.
research_data.narr: Include surveys and datasets that measure job demands, control, effort-reward balance, physical exposures, incidence of work-related illness or injury, and absence records. Examples include workplace health monitoring, national working conditions surveys, and cohort studies linking job exposures to health outcomes. Exclude datasets that measure general stress without specifying work as the source.

variables.desc: Variables that quantify work-related burden: job demands, job control, effort-reward imbalance, physical load measures, exposure to hazards, perceived stress at work, and sickness absence related to work.
variables.narr: Include validated scales and items (e.g., demand, control, support scores), numeric measures of physical workload (lifting weight, repetition rates), records of occupational injury, frequency/duration of sick leave, and subjective measures of burnout or exhaustion attributable to work. Exclude variables that capture generic psychological distress without attributing cause to work contexts.

instruments_tools.desc: Measurement instruments for work-related burden: Job Content Questionnaire, Effort–Reward Imbalance instrument, Copenhagen Psychosocial Questionnaire, Maslach Burnout Inventory, ergonomic assessment tools and workplace exposure checklists.
instruments_tools.narr: Include validated psychometric instruments for psychosocial work factors (JCQ, ERI, COPSOQ), burnout measures (MBI), standardized ergonomic observation tools, workplace exposure assessment protocols, and administrative tools for recording occupational incidents and sick leave. Exclude generic stress scales not tied to workplace conditions or ad hoc measures lacking validation for occupational research.

publication.desc: Publications exploring the relationship between burden/stress (Belastung) and work (Arbeit): how work produces burden and how burden affects work performance, health and employment outcomes.
publication.narr: Include research examining causal or associative links between work conditions and burdens (physical, mental, psychosocial), effects of burden on productivity, absenteeism and career trajectories, and interventions to mitigate work-related burden. Accept interdisciplinary studies (occupational health, psychology, sociology, labour economics) that explicitly analyze the interplay between burden and work. Exclude literature that treats burden or work independently without analysis of their connection.

research_data.desc: Datasets that allow joint analysis of work characteristics and burden: combined measures of job exposures and health/stress outcomes, employer records linking workload to performance or absence, and panel data tracking both work conditions and burden over time.
research_data.narr: Include integrated datasets (working conditions surveys with health modules, longitudinal panels with job and health measures, company HR data linking workload and sick leave) that permit analysis of how work relates to burden and vice versa. Exclude datasets that contain only work attributes or only health/burden measures without the ability to link the two at individual or group level.

variables.desc: Variables capturing both work attributes and burden outcomes: job demands/control/support, physical exposures, work hours, plus stress, burnout, sickness absence, and performance metrics.
variables.narr: Include paired variables such as measures of workload and corresponding stress/burnout scores, objective workload indicators (hours, caseload) with health outcomes (sick days, mental health diagnoses), and organizational performance indicators linked to employee burden. Exclude isolated variables that do not permit connecting work characteristics to burden outcomes.

instruments_tools.desc: Tools for assessing the work–burden relationship: combined survey modules (work conditions + health), validated psychosocial instruments (JCQ, COPSOQ, ERI), burnout inventories, and HR analytics linking workload and absence.
instruments_tools.narr: Include instruments and protocols designed to measure both sides of the equation: standard workplace psychosocial questionnaires combined with health and absence records, ergonomics and exposure assessment tools alongside symptom checklists, and employer data extraction methods that align work metrics with individual health/performance. Exclude tools that measure only job attributes or only health outcomes without integration capability.

publication.desc: Publications addressing physical, ergonomic, psychosocial and organizational workplace burdens, exposures and their health or productivity consequences.
publication.narr: Include empirical studies, reviews and reports that examine workplace stressors, ergonomic loads, psychosocial demands (e.g., job strain, effort-reward imbalance), physical hazards (noise, chemicals, manual handling), injury and sickness absence related to work. Include intervention and evaluation studies that aim to reduce workplace burdens. Exclude studies that focus on non-workplace stress (domestic or community stress) unless explicitly linked to occupational exposures, and exclude purely clinical case reports not situated in workplace contexts.

research_data.desc: Datasets and survey modules that capture workplace exposures, psychosocial demands, physical/chemical hazards, injury and absenteeism data.
research_data.narr: Include cohort studies, cross-sectional surveys and administrative data containing measures of workplace burdens (self-reported demands, COPSOQ/JCQ items, occupational exposure records, accident/compensation registers, sick-leave and disability records), workplace monitoring data and occupational cohort follow-ups. Exclude datasets without workplace-specific exposure or outcome variables and laboratory-only stress measurements not tied to real work settings.

variables.desc: Variables measuring types and intensity of workplace burdens, associated health outcomes and work-related consequences.
variables.narr: Include variables such as physical demands (lifting, repetitive movements), ergonomic risk scores, noise/chemical exposure levels, psychosocial demand/control/support scores, effort-reward imbalance, working hours/shift work, perceived workload, stress symptoms, burnout, musculoskeletal complaints, injury events, sick leave and absenteeism. Exclude generic mental health variables that lack linkage to workplace exposure or context unless usable as work-related outcomes.

instruments_tools.desc: Validated questionnaires, observational checklists and measurement tools for assessing workplace burdens and exposures.
instruments_tools.narr: Include instruments such as the Copenhagen Psychosocial Questionnaire (COPSOQ), Job Content Questionnaire (JCQ), Effort-Reward Imbalance (ERI) questionnaire, Maslach Burnout Inventory when used for work stress, ergonomic assessment tools (RULA, REBA), noise dosimeters, exposure measurement protocols and workplace observation checklists. Exclude tools that measure general life stress without workplace items.

publication.desc: Publications concerned with occupations, occupational classification, employment status and labor market roles.
publication.narr: Include studies, reports and analyses addressing job titles, occupational status, occupational stratification and their links to socioeconomic outcomes, health or mobility. Include methodological papers on occupation coding and classification. Exclude publications that do not pertain to occupational roles (e.g., unrelated uses of the word) or that treat employment only as a peripheral demographic variable without substantive occupational detail.

research_data.desc: Datasets that record occupation, job titles, occupational codes, employment histories and related labor market variables.
research_data.narr: Include census, labor force surveys, longitudinal panels and administrative datasets containing occupation fields (ISCO/SOC codes), industry, employment status, contract type and detailed job histories. Exclude datasets lacking occupation information or those focused exclusively on non-occupational constructs.

variables.desc: Core variables describing occupation, job classification and employment characteristics.
variables.narr: Include variables such as job title, occupational code (ISCO/SOC), industry code, employment status (employed, unemployed, self-employed), contract type (permanent/temporary), working hours, occupational class, occupational prestige and sector. Exclude variables that do not refer to the job/occupation dimension.

instruments_tools.desc: Classification manuals, coding tools and survey modules used to record and categorize occupations.
instruments_tools.narr: Include ISCO and other occupational classification manuals, coding schemes (e.g., ISCO-08), occupation coding software and crosswalks, survey question wordings for occupation and employment, and guidance materials for coding free-text job titles. Exclude instruments unrelated to occupational coding or that measure other constructs only tangentially.

publication.desc: Publications examining the relationship between educational attainment, qualifications and occupational outcomes or career development.
publication.narr: Include empirical and theoretical studies on how education influences occupational status, job matching, returns to education, vocational training, skill formation and social mobility. Include research on educational-occupational mismatch and transitions from education to employment. Exclude works that deal only with educational pedagogy without linking to occupational destinations or labor market outcomes.

research_data.desc: Datasets combining detailed measures of educational qualification, field of study and occupational outcomes.
research_data.narr: Include longitudinal and cross-sectional datasets (e.g., labor force panels, education-to-work cohorts, microcensus) that record highest educational level, vocational qualifications, field of study, training history and subsequent occupational codes, earnings and employment status. Exclude datasets lacking either meaningful education or occupation variables.

variables.desc: Variables capturing educational attainment, qualifications and their mapping to occupations and career outcomes.
variables.narr: Include variables such as years of schooling, highest degree, ISCED/qualification codes, vocational certificates, field of study, training type, occupational code, job level, earnings, skill mismatch indicators and employment stability. Exclude generic academic performance measures that do not connect to occupational outcomes.

instruments_tools.desc: Coding schemes, questionnaires and tools that link education information to occupational classification and skill measurement.
instruments_tools.narr: Include ISCED and national qualification classification manuals, tools mapping qualifications to occupations, survey modules on educational history and vocational training, measures of skill mismatch, and instruments for assessing returns to education. Exclude classroom-level teaching instruments not relevant to labor market placement.

publication.desc: Publications on job satisfaction, workplace well-being and their determinants and consequences.
publication.narr: Include empirical studies, reviews and reports that measure overall and facet-specific job satisfaction, examine predictors (work conditions, pay, supervision, autonomy) and outcomes (turnover, health, productivity). Include cross-national comparisons and longitudinal analyses of job satisfaction. Exclude studies that only address general life satisfaction without linking responses to employment or that use job satisfaction as a minor control variable without substantive analysis.

research_data.desc: Datasets and survey modules that include measures of job satisfaction and related workplace attitudinal variables.
research_data.narr: Include large-scale surveys and panel datasets (e.g., national social surveys, European Working Conditions Survey, SOEP, ALLBUS) that contain single-item or multi-item measures of job satisfaction and facet-specific satisfaction (pay, tasks, colleagues). Exclude datasets without job satisfaction or without identifiable workplace context for satisfaction measures.

variables.desc: Variables measuring overall and facet-specific job satisfaction, and related attitudes and outcomes.
variables.narr: Include variables such as overall job satisfaction score, satisfaction with pay, tasks, supervision/co-workers, work-life balance, intrinsic/extrinsic satisfaction facets, turnover intention, organizational commitment and absenteeism. Exclude non-work-related well-being measures unless explicitly tied to occupational context.

instruments_tools.desc: Validated scales and survey items for assessing job satisfaction and its facets.
instruments_tools.narr: Include instruments such as the Job Satisfaction Survey (JSS), Minnesota Satisfaction Questionnaire (MSQ), single-item global job satisfaction questions used in large surveys, facet scales for pay/supervision/tasks, and guidance on scoring and interpretation. Exclude clinical diagnostic tools that do not specifically measure job-related satisfaction.

publication.desc: Publications on employment activity, types of work tasks, labor force participation and occupational engagement.
publication.narr: Include studies and reports that describe patterns of occupational activity (full-time/part-time, task composition), employment participation across groups, job task analyses, and the relationship between ability/health and work activity. Include investigations of occupational roles over the life course and occupational transitions. Exclude studies focusing on non-occupational activities (leisure, household tasks) unless linked to paid employment.

research_data.desc: Datasets containing employment activity measures, task-level job information, work hours and employment spell histories.
research_data.narr: Include labor force surveys, employment registers, time-use surveys and panel data with variables on employment status, hours worked, job tasks, occupational codes, and employment spells. Include job exposure matrices and datasets with task-based measures. Exclude datasets that do not record actual work activity or that only contain high-level employment indicators without activity detail.

variables.desc: Variables capturing employment participation, job tasks, working time and occupational activity characteristics.
variables.narr: Include variables such as employment status, hours worked, part-time/full-time indicator, primary job tasks, task complexity, occupational code, sector, employment spells, commuting and activity limitations at work. Exclude variables that only refer to non-work activities or general lifestyle measures.

instruments_tools.desc: Instruments and tools for measuring job tasks, time use and employment histories.
instruments_tools.narr: Include time-use diaries, work diary instruments, task inventories and taxonomies (e.g., O*NET mappings), employment history modules, job exposure matrices (JEMs) and survey question modules for recording employment activity. Exclude clinical functional assessments that do not specify workplace activities.

publication.desc: Scholarly publications, reports and book chapters discussing occupational mobility, career mobility, job-to-job transitions, vertical/horizontal mobility and labor market mobility processes in individual life courses or across groups.
publication.narr: Relevant documents describe empirical or theoretical work on occupational mobility (intra- and inter-occupational moves), measurement and determinants of job changes, promotion/demotion, sectoral mobility, geographic mobility for work, career trajectories and labor market segmentation. Include comparative, longitudinal and life-course studies, policy analyses of mobility barriers, and methodological papers on mobility measurement (e.g., mobility matrices, status scales). Exclude works focused solely on general migration without link to employment, macroeconomic mobility of firms, purely economic mobility concepts not tied to individual careers, or pieces that only mention mobility tangentially without substantive treatment.

research_data.desc: Datasets capturing employment histories, job transitions, promotions, occupational codes and timing of job changes (longitudinal or retrospective life-history data), employer/sector information and related socio-demographic variables.
research_data.narr: Relevant datasets include panel or retrospective surveys and administrative records that record sequences of jobs, dates of job start/stop, occupational codes (e.g., ISCO), job status (employee/self-employed), tenure, promotions, wages, reasons for leaving/entering jobs, and geographic moves for work. Include data enabling analysis of vertical/horizontal mobility and career trajectories. Exclude datasets limited to cross-sectional snapshots without any employment history or datasets about firms rather than individuals, and datasets where job-change information is incidental or unavailable.

variables.desc: Variables that operationalize occupational mobility and career change: number/timing of job changes, change in occupational status, promotion/demotion indicators, tenure, sector change, occupational class codes, transition reasons and mobility matrices.
variables.narr: Relevant variables measure job-to-job transitions (counts and dates), occupational codes before/after change (ISCO, national classifications), status/skill-level change (ISEI, EGP, prestige scores), promotion events, change in earnings, sector/industry change, geographic mobility for employment, employment status transitions (unemployed↔employed), and reasons for mobility. Exclude single-item variables only loosely related to mobility (e.g., current occupation only without prior history) or variables about organizational mobility of firms rather than individual career moves.

instruments_tools.desc: Survey modules, life-history calendars, coding schemes and analytical tools for measuring and analysing occupational mobility (job history questionnaires, occupational coding manuals, mobility matrices and sequence-analysis software).
instruments_tools.narr: Relevant instruments include standardized job-history modules and life-course calendars that capture start/end dates and job characteristics, occupational coding schemes (ISCO, national classifications), indices of status/skill (ISEI, prestige scales), mobility matrices and statistical/sequence-analysis tools (e.g., TraMineR) and questionnaire items eliciting reasons for job change. Exclude instruments that focus solely on employer-level measures, organizational HR systems without individual career detail, or tools unrelated to tracking job transitions.

publication.desc: Publications on occupational/work-related attitudes: work values, job-related beliefs, attitudes toward employment, vocational orientations, work ethic, and employment-related norms and preferences.
publication.narr: Include empirical and theoretical studies addressing attitudes toward work and occupation, such as work values, preference for job security vs. flexibility, attitudes to vocational training, occupational aspirations, job satisfaction as an attitudinal construct, and public attitudes toward occupations. Exclude publications solely about occupational structure, labor-market outcomes without attitudinal measures, or clinical personality literature that does not connect traits to job attitudes.

research_data.desc: Survey and panel data containing measures of occupational attitudes and work-related values, including items on job preferences, work ethic, career aspirations and evaluations of occupational roles.
research_data.narr: Relevant datasets provide attitudinal items (Likert scales or categorical responses) on work values, importance of career success, preference for work–life balance, attitudes toward vocational education, occupational prestige perceptions, and measures of job satisfaction as an attitude. Include longitudinal surveys tracking changes in work attitudes. Exclude datasets with no attitudinal content or those limited to objective employment facts without respondents' opinions or values.

variables.desc: Variables capturing work-related attitudes: work values (e.g., autonomy, security, income importance), job satisfaction scales, occupational aspirations, career intentions, and attitudes toward vocational training and employment policies.
variables.narr: Relevant variables include Likert-scale items or indexes on importance of job attributes (security, income, status), measures of intrinsic/extrinsic work motivation, commitment to a profession, occupational aspirations and expectations, willingness to retrain, and evaluative items on vocational education. Exclude strictly behavioral variables (e.g., hours worked) or socio-demographic variables unless combined with direct attitude items.

instruments_tools.desc: Validated scales and survey items used to measure occupational attitudes and work values, such as work values inventories, job satisfaction questionnaires and modules on occupational preferences and vocational orientations.
instruments_tools.narr: Relevant instruments include standardized work-values inventories, Job Satisfaction scales (single-item or multi-item), measures of intrinsic/extrinsic motivation, career aspiration modules, and questionnaire batteries used in major social surveys to elicit work attitudes. Include translation/adaptations for German contexts. Exclude psychometric instruments unrelated to occupational attitudes (e.g., personality tests without a work-specific component) or instruments that only capture employers' perspectives.

publication.desc: Research on the occupational or professional self: professional identity, vocational self-concept, occupational self-efficacy, career identity and the role of self-perception in occupational choices and career development.
publication.narr: Include studies on how individuals perceive their professional role (professional identity, centrality of work to the self), development of vocational self-concept over the life course, occupational self-efficacy and confidence in job-related competencies, and the link between self-concept and career behavior. Exclude general self-concept literature without occupational focus, clinical self-esteem studies unrelated to work, or papers about organizational identity (firm-level) rather than individual professional identity.

research_data.desc: Datasets measuring professional identity constructs: occupational self-concept, occupational self-efficacy, career identity, role centrality, and related measures collected in surveys, career studies and longitudinal panels.
research_data.narr: Relevant datasets contain validated scales or items assessing occupational self-efficacy, strength/centrality of professional identity, identification with occupational groups, perceived competence, and career self-concept measures, including repeated measures over time. Exclude datasets without individual-level psychological measures of occupational self or those focusing only on employer-side organizational identity.

variables.desc: Variables operationalizing the 'professional self': occupational self-efficacy scores, identity centrality, identification with occupation/profession, perceived competence, vocational self-concept dimensions and stability of career identity.
variables.narr: Include variables that measure confidence in performing occupational tasks, the importance of professional role to self-definition, statements of 'I see myself as a [profession]', measures of role conflict affecting professional identity, and scales for career commitment. Exclude generic self-esteem items unless explicitly framed in the occupational/professional domain.

instruments_tools.desc: Psychometric scales and survey modules for assessing professional identity and occupational self-concept, such as occupational self-efficacy scales, career identity questionnaires, and life-history tools capturing identity development.
instruments_tools.narr: Relevant instruments include validated occupational self-efficacy scales, professional identity scales/adaptations for specific professions, career adaptability and identity questionnaires (e.g., Career Adapt-Abilities items), and interview guides/life-history calendars focusing on identity formation in work. Exclude instruments measuring general personality traits or organizational-level identity measures without an individual occupational-self focus.

publication.desc: Publications addressing public evaluation of social policies: citizen attitudes toward welfare state programs, assessments of effectiveness and fairness of social policy, and scholarly analyses of policy acceptance and legitimacy.
publication.narr: Include empirical and normative studies measuring or theorizing how individuals and groups evaluate social policy instruments (e.g., pensions, unemployment benefits, healthcare, family policies), perceived effectiveness, satisfaction with social policy, and determinants of support or opposition. Include cross-national comparisons, surveys of public opinion, and impact analyses of policy reforms on public evaluations. Exclude technical policy design papers without public-evaluation data, or studies on fiscal sustainability without linking to public perceptions.

research_data.desc: Survey data and opinion polls that record evaluations of social policy measures, citizen satisfaction with welfare services, and support for policy instruments and reforms.
research_data.narr: Relevant datasets feature items on support for welfare spending, satisfaction with specific social programs (pensions, unemployment insurance, health care), perceived effectiveness and fairness of social policy, trust in social institutions, and reactions to policy changes. Include cross-sectional and panel surveys (national and comparative). Exclude datasets that only record policy parameters (benefit levels) without public opinion indicators, or administrative policy implementation data without evaluative measures.

variables.desc: Variables capturing evaluation of social policy: support/opposition to welfare programs, satisfaction ratings, perceived fairness/effectiveness, willingness to pay/higher taxes for social programs, and trust in welfare institutions.
variables.narr: Include Likert-scale or categorical measures of approval for specific social policies, overall satisfaction with the welfare state, perceived adequacy of benefits, perceived beneficiaries, and policy priority rankings. Also include variables on perceived redistribution preferences and willingness to finance policies. Exclude variables describing policy provision (eligibility, benefit amounts) unless paired with attitudinal assessments.

instruments_tools.desc: Survey modules, question batteries and experimental designs used to measure public evaluation of social policy, including vignettes, policy-specific items and comparative opinion modules.
instruments_tools.narr: Relevant instruments include standardized opinion-question batteries on welfare attitudes, modules used in comparative surveys (e.g., items on welfare support), vignette experiments assessing reactions to policy scenarios, and validated scales measuring trust in social institutions and perceived policy effectiveness. Exclude instruments focused only on administrative policy metrics or technical costing tools without measures of public evaluation.
