publication.desc: Research on supervisor–subordinate relationships: leader–member exchange, supervisory support, workplace relations with managers, mentoring and trust between employees and their supervisors.
publication.narr: Include empirical and theoretical studies examining the quality and effects of relationships between employees and their immediate supervisors, including leader–member exchange (LMX), supervisory support, perceived fairness, trust, conflict, mentoring and feedback processes. Include outcomes such as job satisfaction, performance, turnover intentions, and well-being. Exclude studies focused only on broad leadership styles at the organizational level without attention to dyadic relationships, or historical/organizational structure analyses without interpersonal focus.

research_data.desc: Datasets from workplace and organizational surveys that include measures of supervisor–employee relationship quality, supervisory behavior, feedback frequency, mentoring, conflict and trust in direct supervisors.
research_data.narr: Relevant datasets contain items measuring LMX quality, perceived supervisor support, frequency/quality of feedback, conflict with manager, supervisory fairness, and mentoring experiences, ideally linked to employee outcomes. Include multi-level or matched supervisor–employee surveys. Exclude datasets lacking any supervisor-related attitudinal items or those that record only aggregate leadership ratings without dyadic detail.

variables.desc: Variables operationalizing the relationship with a supervisor: LMX scores, perceived supervisory support, trust in supervisor, frequency/quality of feedback, conflict/abuse indicators, and presence/quality of mentoring.
variables.narr: Include validated measures such as LMX-7 items or composite scores, scales of perceived supervisor support, items on feedback frequency and developmental support, ratings of fairness and conflict with supervisor, and indicators of mentoring and sponsorship. Exclude generic management-level variables that do not capture the employee’s perception of their direct relationship with a supervisor.

instruments_tools.desc: Questionnaires, validated scales and measurement modules for assessing supervisor–employee relations, notably Leader–Member Exchange instruments, supervisory support scales and workplace conflict/mentoring measures.
instruments_tools.narr: Relevant instruments include the LMX-7 (or other LMX measures), perceived supervisor support scales, mentoring relationship inventories, instruments measuring supervisory fairness and abusive supervision, and multi-source feedback tools capturing dyadic relations. Exclude leadership instruments that only measure leader traits or organizational-level leadership climate without items on the dyadic supervisor–subordinate relationship.

publication.desc: Publications (articles, books, reports, policy papers) in German or English focused on adult education, continuing education, lifelong learning, and adult learning policies and programs, especially in German-speaking contexts.
publication.narr: Include empirical studies, literature reviews, program evaluations, policy analyses, and theoretical work that address adult education ('Bildung Erwachsen'), continuing vocational training, informal and non-formal learning in adulthood, participation barriers, adult learning outcomes, and policy frameworks in Germany, Austria, Switzerland, or comparative European studies. Prefer sources that explicitly discuss adult learners, adult educational institutions, adult pedagogy, vocational retraining, or lifelong learning strategies. Exclude publications solely about compulsory schooling, higher education for traditional-age students, child or adolescent education, and purely clinical education unrelated to adult learning (unless tied to adult training programs).

research_data.desc: Datasets and study data on adult education participation, lifelong learning activities, vocational training for adults, continuing education programs, and adult learning outcomes (national surveys, cohort studies, administrative data).
research_data.narr: Include national or international surveys and administrative datasets that measure adult education participation and training (e.g., Adult Education Survey (AES), PIAAC, CVTS, national continuing education registries), program evaluation datasets, longitudinal studies tracking adult learners, and time-use or labor market linkage data that capture participation in adult learning. Exclude datasets that only cover compulsory school-age children, university students below typical adult-learner contexts, or purely qualitative single-case narratives without structured data unless part of mixed-methods study with extractable data.

variables.desc: Variables capturing adult learning status and context: participation in courses, type of course, frequency/duration, modes (formal/non-formal/informal), motives, barriers, prior education, employment status, age, outcomes (skills, employment changes), and institutional affiliations.
variables.narr: Include variables indicating adult education participation (binary/counts), course type and subject, hours spent in training, certification obtained, reasons for participation, obstacles to participation (cost, time, childcare), socioeconomic indicators (age, gender, education level, occupation), and measurable outcomes (literacy/numeracy scores, employment transitions, wage changes). Exclude variables strictly about school curricula, childhood learning milestones, or biomedical health measures unrelated to adult learning outcomes.

instruments_tools.desc: Survey modules, questionnaires, standardized assessments and evaluation tools used to measure adult education and lifelong learning (e.g., AES questionnaire modules, PIAAC instruments, program evaluation templates).
instruments_tools.narr: Include validated survey instruments and questionnaire modules that capture participation in adult learning, motivations and barriers, and adult skill assessments (literacy, numeracy) such as AES and PIAAC instruments, course attendance logs, program evaluation protocols, and adult learning scales. Exclude instruments designed for primary/secondary education settings only, or clinical tools not adapted for measuring adult learning engagement.

publication.desc: Publications in German or English on care work ('Care Arbeit'), including paid and unpaid caregiving, eldercare, childcare, domestic care, labor conditions in care sectors, gendered division of care, and care policy.
publication.narr: Include empirical research, policy analyses, labor studies, ethnographies, and comparative reports that focus on care work performed in households, care institutions, and formal care sectors. Relevant topics: care labor market, unpaid family caregiving, migrant care workers, working conditions, wages, care policies, gender inequalities, and care commodification. Prefer studies addressing Germany or other European contexts when tagged 'Care Arbeit'. Exclude publications solely about clinical health outcomes without focus on care labor, veterinary or non-human care contexts, or general labor topics not specifying care tasks.

research_data.desc: Datasets and administrative records on paid and unpaid care work, time-use data, labor statistics for care sectors, caregiver surveys, and program evaluations of care services.
research_data.narr: Include time-use surveys (e.g., national time-use surveys, Eurostat), labor force data for health and social care occupations, caregiver modules in household surveys, longitudinal caregiver panels, datasets on wages/working hours in care professions, and administrative registries for care service provision. Also include datasets capturing informal caregiving prevalence and intensity. Exclude datasets unrelated to caregiving tasks (e.g., general industry data without care-sector detail) or clinical datasets focused only on patient health outcomes without caregiver measures.

variables.desc: Variables describing caregiving activity and context: caregiver status, hours of care provided, type of care tasks, paid/unpaid status, employment conditions, wages, training, relationship to care recipient, and care-recipient needs.
variables.narr: Include variables indicating whether respondent is an informal or formal caregiver, weekly hours spent on caregiving, types of activities (personal care, medical assistance, household tasks), employment status and sector, contract type, wage level, access to training, extent of state support, care recipient characteristics (age, disability level), and measures of caregiver burden and wellbeing. Exclude variables that do not disaggregate care-specific activities or that only measure general household tasks without caregiving intent.

instruments_tools.desc: Survey modules, scales and measurement tools for assessing care work, caregiver burden, time-use instruments, and occupational classification tools relevant to care sectors.
instruments_tools.narr: Include validated instruments such as caregiver burden scales (e.g., Zarit Burden Interview), time-use diary instruments, occupational classification codes for care professions (ISCO/standard national codes), caregiver questionnaires embedded in household surveys, and program evaluation tools for care services. Exclude clinical assessment tools focused only on patient diagnosis without caregiver-oriented items, or generic workplace instruments lacking care-specific items.

publication.desc: Academic and policy publications reporting on attitudes, beliefs, perceptions, and public opinion regarding climate change, including determinants of concern, risk perception, behavioral intentions, and policy support.
publication.narr: Include quantitative and qualitative studies, reviews, and policy briefs that directly investigate public attitudes toward climate change, beliefs about causes and risks, climate change skepticism or denial, willingness to act, and support for mitigation/adaptation policies. Prefer works using survey data or experimental designs measuring attitudinal constructs. Exclude publications about climate science per se without social-attitudinal focus, or technical modeling of climate processes absent public opinion analysis.

research_data.desc: Survey datasets and opinion polls measuring individual and collective attitudes toward climate change, risk perception, policy preferences, behavioral intentions, and segmentation (e.g., 'Six Americas').
research_data.narr: Include large cross-national and national surveys with climate attitude modules (e.g., ESS modules when relevant, Eurobarometer, World Values Survey, Gallup, Pew Research, Yale/George Mason 'Climate Change in the American Mind', national climate opinion polls), panel datasets tracking attitude change, and experimental survey data on messaging effects. Exclude purely physical climate datasets (temperature, emissions) unless paired with social opinion measures; exclude datasets without explicit climate-attitude variables.

variables.desc: Attitudinal variables: belief in anthropogenic climate change, perceived severity and risk, concern level, worry, perceived personal and societal impact, behavioral intentions, policy support, trust in science, and climate-related values and norms.
variables.narr: Include variables measuring belief in climate change existence and causes (human vs natural), degree of concern or worry, perceived risk to self/community/nation, willingness to change behavior (e.g., reduce energy use, accept costs), support for specific policies (carbon tax, renewables, regulation), trust in scientific expertise, political ideology, and self-reported mitigation/adaptation actions. Exclude variables that only measure environmental attitudes in a generic sense without explicit mention of climate change.

instruments_tools.desc: Survey instruments, validated scales and segmentation tools used to measure climate change attitudes, concern, risk perception and behavioral intent (e.g., standardized survey items, 'Six Americas' segmentation, experimental vignette protocols).
instruments_tools.narr: Include commonly used survey question batteries about climate beliefs and concern, validated psychometric scales for environmental concern (when applied to climate), segmentation instruments (e.g., Yale/George Mason 'Six Americas'), and experimental stimuli or messaging protocols used to test attitude change. Exclude instruments focused solely on technical climate literacy tests unrelated to attitudinal measures.

publication.desc: Publications across social science and natural science that address climate change broadly: causes, impacts, mitigation, adaptation, climate policy, societal responses, and interdisciplinary studies linking physical climate data with social/economic outcomes.
publication.narr: Include peer-reviewed articles, technical reports, assessment reports, policy briefs, and interdisciplinary studies that analyze climate change science, impacts (environmental, economic, social), mitigation and adaptation strategies, public policy and governance, and socio-economic consequences. Prioritize works that present empirical evidence, model results, or policy evaluation. Exclude documents unrelated to anthropogenic climate change such as isolated weather reports or non-climate environmental topics unless explicitly tied to climate change.

research_data.desc: Datasets on climate variables (temperature, precipitation, emissions), impact data (sea-level, crop yields), socio-economic datasets linked to climate (vulnerability, emissions inventories), and integrated datasets combining physical and social indicators.
research_data.narr: Include observational climate datasets (HadCRUT, CRU, NOAA, NASA GISS), greenhouse gas emissions inventories, CMIP model outputs, impact datasets (sea-level, extreme events), and socio-economic datasets used in climate impact research (agricultural yields, health outcomes, migration linked to climate), as well as integrated assessment model outputs. Exclude datasets that are purely administrative and unrelated to climate or datasets lacking metadata to establish relevance to climate change research.

variables.desc: Physical and social variables relevant to climate research: atmospheric temperature, precipitation, greenhouse gas concentrations, emissions by sector, sea-level, extreme event counts, vulnerability indices, adaptation measures, mitigation policy indicators, and socio-economic covariates.
variables.narr: Include variables capturing climate system metrics (mean/seasonal temperatures, anomalies, precipitation), emissions metrics (CO2, CH4 by source/sector), frequency/magnitude of extreme events, exposure and vulnerability measures (population at risk, infrastructure), policy variables (carbon pricing, renewable share), and socio-economic controls (GDP, demographics, land use). Exclude variables unrelated to climate processes or impacts (e.g., unrelated economic microdata without linkage to climate exposure).

instruments_tools.desc: Models, measurement instruments, survey modules, remote sensing products, and tools used in climate research and policy analysis (climate models, downscaling tools, emission accounting methods, remote sensing datasets, public opinion survey modules).
instruments_tools.narr: Include climate model ensembles (CMIP), downscaling tools, remote sensing products (MODIS, GRACE), greenhouse gas accounting methodologies, climate impact assessment frameworks, vulnerability and risk assessment tools, and social-science instruments measuring climate perceptions and policy preferences. Exclude tools that do not pertain to climate-related measurement, modeling, or assessment.

publication.desc: Scholarly and policy publications analyzing conceptions, definitions, and lay/theoretical understandings of democracy, democratic values, legitimacy, democratic quality, and citizen perceptions of democratic principles.
publication.narr: Include theoretical work, comparative studies, empirical analyses, and survey-based research that explicitly examine how democracy is conceptualized (procedural vs substantive, liberal vs participatory), public conceptions of democracy, normative debates on democratic legitimacy, and links between conceptions and political behavior. Prioritize publications that operationalize or measure conceptions of democracy. Exclude works that discuss democratic institutions only in technical legal terms without engagement with conceptions or public understandings.

research_data.desc: Datasets capturing public attitudes toward democracy, definitions of democracy, evaluations of democratic performance, civic engagement measures, and experimental data on conceptions of democracy (e.g., WVS, ESS, LAPOP).
research_data.narr: Include cross-national and national surveys with items on support for democracy, definitions (e.g., agreement with democratic statements), preferences for democratic principles (freedom, equality, rule of law), evaluations of democratic performance, and datasets that explore correlates of democratic conceptions (education, political ideology). Also include panel or experimental datasets that probe causal factors shaping conceptions. Exclude datasets that only measure institutional indicators (e.g., V-Dem) without citizen-level conception items, unless combined with public-opinion modules.

variables.desc: Variables reflecting conceptions and evaluations of democracy: support for democracy, preferred democratic attributes (participation, competition, rights), satisfaction with democracy, tolerance of non-democratic alternatives, perceived legitimacy, and related political attitudes.
variables.narr: Include variables that ask respondents to define or choose what democracy means, rate importance of democratic elements (free elections, civil liberties, social justice), measure satisfaction with democratic performance, tolerance for authoritarian alternatives, trust in democratic institutions, and behavioral indicators like voting or protest participation tied to democratic beliefs. Exclude variables unrelated to conceptions (e.g., electoral results) unless used as contextual covariates.

instruments_tools.desc: Survey question batteries, vignettes, scales and experimental instruments designed to measure public conceptions of democracy, democratic values, legitimacy, and related constructs.
instruments_tools.narr: Include validated survey modules from major studies (e.g., World Values Survey democracy items, European Social Survey modules on political values), vignette-based instruments probing trade-offs among democratic principles, and experimental protocols testing messaging on democracy. Also include coding schemes for classifying conceptions in qualitative data. Exclude instruments that measure only institutional indicators without capturing citizen-level conceptions or normative understandings.

publication.desc: Publications examining individual or household decision-making, attitudes, and behaviors related to consumption and purchasing across channels and contexts.
publication.narr: Include empirical and theoretical studies on consumer decision processes, buying behavior, brand loyalty, advertising effects, online shopping, impulse purchases, consumer satisfaction, and cross-cultural comparisons of consumption. Include marketing, psychology, and behavioral economics perspectives that directly address how consumers choose, evaluate, and use products or services. Exclude publications focused solely on firm-level financial performance, supply-chain logistics, macroeconomic demand forecasting without individual/household behavior, or purely producer/firm strategies that do not measure consumer responses.

research_data.desc: Datasets capturing consumer choices, intentions and behaviors from surveys, experiments, transaction logs, and observational studies.
research_data.narr: Include consumer panel and scanner data, household expenditure surveys, online transaction logs, stated-preference and choice-experiment datasets, experimental data on buying decisions, eye-tracking and neurophysiological datasets tied to marketing stimuli, and longitudinal consumer panels. Exclude aggregated national consumption aggregates, firm accounting data without consumer-level linkage, and purely supply-side or production datasets.

variables.desc: Variables measuring aspects of purchasing behavior, preferences, attitudes, and demographic correlates relevant to consumption.
variables.narr: Include variables such as purchase frequency, spending/expenditure, product choice, brand awareness, willingness-to-pay, price sensitivity, purchase intention, satisfaction, loyalty, impulse buying, consumption occasions, and socio-demographics (age, income, household composition). Exclude firm financial indicators (profits, revenues) or macroeconomic aggregates that do not represent consumer-level behavior.

instruments_tools.desc: Survey instruments, experimental protocols, tracking tools and coding schemes used to measure consumer behavior.
instruments_tools.narr: Include questionnaires and scales for attitudes and intentions, purchase diaries, point-of-sale scanner protocols, choice experiment designs, conjoint analysis tools, eye-tracking and clickstream measurement protocols, field/online experimental scripts, and coding manuals for observational shopper studies. Exclude instruments devoted exclusively to firm accounting, manufacturing processes, or non-consumer economic metrics.

publication.desc: Publications related to COVID-19 (SARS-CoV-2) including epidemiology, public health, social and economic impacts, and policy responses to the pandemic.
publication.narr: Include research on COVID-19 transmission, case studies, clinical outcomes, vaccination and vaccine hesitancy, public-health interventions (NPIs), health-system impacts, mental health consequences, economic and social effects of the pandemic, and evaluations of pandemic policy measures. Include multidisciplinary work (medical, epidemiological, social sciences) if explicitly about COVID-19. Exclude publications not about SARS-CoV-2 or the 2019–present pandemic (e.g., unrelated coronaviruses) unless they directly inform COVID-19 understanding.

research_data.desc: Datasets that record COVID-19 cases, testing, clinical outcomes, behaviors, mobility, and survey responses during the pandemic.
research_data.narr: Include case counts, hospitalization and mortality records, seroprevalence studies, testing and vaccination registries, contact-tracing datasets, mobility and social-distancing mobility data, clinical trials on COVID-19 treatments/vaccines, and population surveys about behavior and attitudes toward COVID-19 measures. Exclude datasets unrelated to COVID-19 timing or population (e.g., pre-2019 respiratory virus datasets) unless explicitly connected to COVID-19 analyses.

variables.desc: Variables that capture infection status, clinical outcomes, preventive behaviors, and pandemic-relevant attitudes and exposures.
variables.narr: Include variables such as SARS-CoV-2 test result, PCR/antigen status, symptom onset and severity, hospitalization, ICU admission, vaccination status and dose dates, compliance with NPIs (mask use, distancing), mobility indices, exposure history, serology results, and pandemic-related mental-health indicators. Exclude generic health variables that are not linked to COVID-19 without clear relevance.

instruments_tools.desc: Diagnostic protocols, survey instruments, epidemiological models and measurement tools used in COVID-19 research.
instruments_tools.narr: Include PCR and antigen testing protocols, serological assay descriptions, standardized COVID-19 symptom checklists, validated survey modules on pandemic behavior and attitudes, contact-tracing system descriptions, mobility-tracking methodologies, statistical and epidemiological modeling tools (SEIR models, R estimation), and clinical-trial protocols for COVID-19 interventions. Exclude laboratory methods unrelated to SARS-CoV-2 and tools intended for non-pandemic infectious disease contexts unless adapted for COVID-19.

publication.desc: Publications on democracy (demokratie) including democratic institutions, participation, democratization, and threats to democratic governance.
publication.narr: Include comparative and national studies on democratic institutions, electoral systems, party competition, citizen participation, trust in democracy, civil liberties, democratic backsliding, democratization processes, and normative theory of democracy. Include works in German and other languages if they address democracy-related topics. Exclude studies that use the term 'democracy' metaphorically in unrelated contexts (e.g., 'market democracy' without political-institutional analysis).

research_data.desc: Datasets on political regimes, elections, public opinion, and institutional measures relevant to democracy studies.
research_data.narr: Include election results, voter turnout data, public-opinion surveys on democratic attitudes (e.g., ESS, WVS), panel studies on political behavior, cross-national indices of democracy and rights (V-Dem, Polity, Freedom House), and expert-coded datasets on institutional features. Exclude datasets that are purely administrative or non-political without connection to democratic processes.

variables.desc: Variables capturing regime type, political participation, civil liberties, institutional arrangements, and democratic attitudes.
variables.narr: Include variables such as regime classification (democracy/autocracy), electoral competitiveness, turnout, protest participation, trust in institutions, satisfaction with democracy, freedom of press indices, judicial independence, civil liberties scores, and party-system fragmentation. Exclude economic or social variables unless used to analyze their relationship with democratic outcomes and explicitly labeled as part of democracy research.

instruments_tools.desc: Survey questions, coding manuals, and indices used to measure democratic practices, institutions, and attitudes.
instruments_tools.narr: Include validated questionnaire modules on political participation and democratic satisfaction, coding schemes and manuals for regime classification (Polity, V-Dem codebooks), electoral data collection protocols, and interview guides for qualitative studies of democratic institutions. Exclude tools developed only for non-political administrative measurement or tools that measure broad governance without reference to democratic criteria.

publication.desc: Publications on depressive disorders and depressive symptoms, covering epidemiology, diagnosis, etiology, treatment, and outcomes.
publication.narr: Include clinical and population-based studies of major depression, dysthymia, depressive symptomatology, risk and protective factors, psychotherapy and pharmacotherapy trials, longitudinal course of depression, comorbidity with other mental or physical disorders, and public-health impacts. Exclude papers that mention 'depression' only as a transient mood in non-clinical contexts without measurement or analysis of depressive symptoms/disorders.

research_data.desc: Datasets from clinical trials, cohort studies, epidemiological surveys, and registries that measure depression or depressive symptoms.
research_data.narr: Include datasets containing diagnostic assessments (DSM/ICD), symptom scales (PHQ-9, BDI, CES-D), treatment outcomes, health-care utilization for depression, longitudinal cohort data on mental health, and administrative psychiatric registries. Exclude datasets lacking measures of depressive symptoms or diagnosis, or those focused solely on unrelated psychiatric conditions without depression measures.

variables.desc: Variables that quantify depressive severity, diagnosis, symptom profiles, treatment, and correlates.
variables.narr: Include variables such as depression diagnosis (DSM/ICD), symptom scores (PHQ-9, BDI, CES-D scores), onset age, episode duration, remission status, suicide ideation/attempts, treatment type and adherence, comorbid anxiety, psychosocial stressors, and functional impairment. Exclude generic mood descriptors without validated measurement or clinical relevance.

instruments_tools.desc: Validated screening tools, diagnostic interviews, treatment protocols, and assessment batteries for depression research.
instruments_tools.narr: Include instruments such as the PHQ-9, Beck Depression Inventory (BDI), CES-D, Hamilton Depression Rating Scale (HDRS), SCID diagnostic interview, Mini International Neuropsychiatric Interview (MINI), psychotherapy manuals, clinical-trial protocols, and standardized rating procedures. Exclude unvalidated mood checklists or single-item measures that do not reliably assess depressive symptoms or diagnoses.

publication.desc: Publications on digitalization and digital technologies, including digital economy, digital skills, e-government, digital education, and the social effects of digital transformation.
publication.narr: Include empirical and theoretical work on adoption and impacts of digital technologies (internet, mobile, platforms, AI), digital policy, digital divides and inequality, digital labor, e-governance, online behaviors, and digital transformation in organizations and education. Exclude uses of 'digital' as a generic file format reference or unrelated technical mentions without social, economic, or institutional context.

research_data.desc: Datasets measuring internet and technology use, digital skills, platform activity, and indicators of digital infrastructure and adoption.
research_data.narr: Include surveys on internet use and digital skills (e.g., Eurostat ICT surveys), platform and social-media usage logs, broadband/infrastructure coverage data, administrative data on e-government uptake, digital economy indicators, and user-behavior analytics. Exclude purely technical system-logs with no human behavior component or datasets only about non-digital (analog) processes.

variables.desc: Variables describing access to, use of, skills with, and impacts of digital technologies.
variables.narr: Include variables like internet access (broadband, mobile), frequency and type of online activities, digital literacy/digital skills scores, device ownership, platform engagement metrics, e-government service usage, teleworking frequency, and measures of digital inequality. Exclude variables that are unrelated to digital technology usage or that refer only to offline phenomena without a digital link.

instruments_tools.desc: Assessment tools, surveys, analytics methods and protocols used to measure and study digital technology use and its effects.
instruments_tools.narr: Include digital-literacy assessment instruments, standardized ICT-use questionnaires, web and app analytics tools and protocols, platform API datasets and scraping methodologies, user-experience testing protocols, and measures for digital inclusion/exclusion. Exclude tools solely for hardware benchmarking or non-human machine performance metrics that do not inform social science questions about digitalization.

publication.desc: Publications that address digital competence/digital skills: definitions, frameworks, assessments, education and workplace implications.
publication.narr: Include scholarly articles, books, reports and conference papers that define or operationalize 'digital competence' (e.g. DigComp and related frameworks), describe assessment instruments, present empirical measurements (student, teacher, worker populations), discuss training/interventions to improve digital skills, or evaluate outcomes of digital competence on learning and labor-market results. Include theoretical and review articles that synthesize constructs and measurement approaches. Include pieces in German and English and policy documents from education and labor agencies. Exclude publications that only discuss technical IT infrastructure, software development techniques or network engineering without addressing human skills, or that use the phrase solely in marketing contexts without conceptual or empirical content.

research_data.desc: Datasets and data collections measuring digital competence or related digital skill indicators.
research_data.narr: Include survey datasets, assessment results, standardized test data, longitudinal studies and cohort data that contain direct measures of digital skills (objective test scores or validated self-assessments), digital literacy modules within broader surveys, log data tied to skill assessment tasks, and metadata/codebooks. Include national or international assessments (or subcomponents) measuring digital competence and datasets from intervention studies evaluating training programs. Exclude raw technical network logs, purely system-level performance metrics, or usage-only telemetry that cannot be linked to measures of competence or documented assessment tasks.

variables.desc: Variables capturing digital competence constructs and closely related indicators.
variables.narr: Include variables that measure or proxy digital competence: objective test items/scores for digital tasks, composite competency indices, validated scale items (self-efficacy in digital tasks, digital problem solving), frequency of technology use for work/study, participation in digital training, familiarity with software/tools, and domain-specific digital skills (e.g. information evaluation, coding). Include sociodemographic variables and educational attainment as control variables when reported alongside competence measures. Exclude variables that only record device or network characteristics without behavioral or skill interpretation.

instruments_tools.desc: Assessment instruments, competency frameworks and measurement tools for digital competence.
instruments_tools.narr: Include validated questionnaires, standardized test batteries, competency frameworks (e.g. DigComp, ISTE standards), rubrics for digital task performance, observational protocols, item banks for assessing digital literacy, and manuals documenting administration and scoring. Also include digital learning/training curricula and validated pre/post questionnaires used in interventions. Exclude proprietary instruments with no documentation, technical software tools unrelated to assessment (e.g. server monitoring), or general ICT infrastructure checklists that do not assess human competence.

publication.desc: Publications on digitization and its effects on work: labor markets, job tasks, skills, organization and employment relations.
publication.narr: Include empirical, theoretical and policy publications examining how digitalization (automation, AI, ICT adoption, platform work) changes job content, task composition, required skills, employment levels, job quality, working conditions, and organizational practices. Include sectoral studies, comparative labor-market analyses, impact assessments, case studies of workplace digital transformation, and reviews. Include publications on regulation, social dialogue and policy responses. Exclude pieces that treat digitization only as background technological change without linking to work, or purely technical ICT research not addressing labor or organizational outcomes.

research_data.desc: Datasets addressing relationships between digitalization and work: job tasks, employment outcomes, firm ICT use and platform work.
research_data.narr: Include surveys of firms and workers with measures of ICT adoption, task composition and automation exposure, administrative labor-market data linked to technology indicators, employer-level datasets on digital investments and HR outcomes, job vacancy and skills demand data, longitudinal panels tracking workers through technological change, and platform work datasets (gig economy). Include metadata and codebooks. Exclude datasets that measure only technical network metrics or consumer digital behavior without workplace or labor-market linkages.

variables.desc: Variables measuring digitalization at work, job tasks, automation risk and labor outcomes.
variables.narr: Include variables capturing firm-level ICT adoption, presence of automation/AI, use of specific digital tools, frequency and intensity of digital task performance, job task descriptors, occupational task scores (e.g. routine vs non-routine), training in digital skills, telework incidence, contract type, wages, hours, employment status, job stability, productivity measures and health/wellbeing indicators related to digitalization. Also include industry, occupation codes, and demographic controls. Exclude variables only about consumer online behavior not tied to employment.

instruments_tools.desc: Measurement instruments and tools for researching digitalization and work.
instruments_tools.narr: Include surveys and questionnaires for firms and employees on ICT use and digital task content, task-based job analysis instruments, occupational classification crosswalks (to map tasks to automation risk), skill demand taxonomies, employer survey modules, audit tools for workplace digital maturity, and software to analyze job postings or platform work data. Include validated measurement guides and coding manuals. Exclude technical IT deployment manuals and proprietary HR systems without methodological documentation.

publication.desc: Publications specifically focused on digitalization at the workplace: implementation, effects on tasks, workers and management.
publication.narr: Include case studies, empirical research and reviews examining workplace-level digital transformation: adoption of digital tools, changes in workflows and task design, effects on employee skills, productivity, job satisfaction and health, managerial practices, and training. Include interventions to support digital transitions, change management studies, and sector-specific workplace analyses. Exclude general theoretical discussions of digitization without workplace focus or studies limited to consumer digital adoption.

research_data.desc: Workplace-level datasets capturing digital technologies, task changes and worker outcomes.
research_data.narr: Include firm or establishment surveys with modules on workplace digitization, employee surveys tied to specific workplaces, observational data on task workflows pre/post digital introduction, administrative HR records matched to technology deployment, and longitudinal employer-employee linked data capturing digital transitions. Include metadata and instruments used to collect data. Exclude datasets that record only high-level national ICT indicators without workplace disaggregation.

variables.desc: Variables measuring digitalization processes and consequences at the workplace level.
variables.narr: Include variables recording presence and type of workplace digital technologies (software, automation, collaboration tools), measures of task redesign, digital skill requirements, training provided, changes in work organization (remote work, flexible scheduling), productivity/performance metrics, absenteeism, occupational health outcomes, and employee perceptions of change. Include workplace identifiers, sector, size and management practices. Exclude variables that only indicate consumer device ownership or household internet access without workplace context.

instruments_tools.desc: Tools and instruments for assessing workplace digitalization and its impacts.
instruments_tools.narr: Include workplace assessment checklists, digital maturity models, staff surveys and interview protocols focusing on digital tool adoption and task change, observational protocols for workflow analysis, training evaluation instruments, and guidance documents for implementing digital change. Also include coding schemes for categorizing workplace technologies and task types. Exclude general ICT procurement guides lacking research-oriented measurement detail.

publication.desc: Publications on the relationship between digitization and work broadly, including labor market, occupational and organizational perspectives.
publication.narr: Include research that links digitalization processes to changes in employment, job content, skills demand, workplace organization, occupational health and socio-economic inequalities. Accept cross-disciplinary work from economics, sociology, organizational studies, education and public policy that addresses digitization's consequences for work. Include empirical analyses, theoretical contributions and policy evaluations. Exclude materials that discuss digital technology in non-work contexts without drawing implications for labor or occupations.

research_data.desc: Data collections that enable analysis of digitization effects on employment, occupations and workplaces.
research_data.narr: Include datasets on technology adoption, occupational task measures, job postings scraped for digital skill demand, employer and employee surveys with digitization modules, longitudinal labor market panels, and matched employer-employee data linking technology use to outcomes. Include structured metadata, codebooks and documentation enabling reproducible analysis. Exclude datasets limited to consumer digital engagement or network performance metrics unrelated to work.

variables.desc: Variables reflecting digitalization exposure at job, worker and firm levels, and associated labor outcomes.
variables.narr: Include measures of ICT use intensity, automation indicators, digital task frequency, required digital competencies, teleworking prevalence, platform work indicators, job insecurity, wages, productivity, and employment transitions. Also include occupational codes, industry identifiers and demographic controls. Include variables capturing training, upskilling and management responses. Exclude variables solely describing individual leisure internet use.

instruments_tools.desc: Measurement frameworks and instruments for studying digitization's impact on work and occupations.
instruments_tools.narr: Include validated survey modules for ICT and digital task measurement, job analysis tools that classify task content by digital intensity, instruments to measure skill mismatch, software for text-mining job ads to extract digital skill demand, and guidelines for mapping technologies to occupations. Include coding manuals and replication resources. Exclude developer-oriented tools that measure system performance without linking to human work.

publication.desc: Publications on discrimination in schools: evidence, mechanisms, interventions and policy relevant to students and school staff.
publication.narr: Include empirical studies, theoretical analyses, literature reviews and policy reports examining discrimination in educational settings by race/ethnicity, migration background, gender, disability, socioeconomic status, religion, sexual orientation or other protected characteristics. Include research on discriminatory practices, teacher bias, tracking and streaming, exclusionary discipline, attainment gaps, segregated schooling, microaggressions and anti-discrimination interventions. Include evaluation studies of programs aimed at reducing discrimination and legal/policy analyses. Exclude documents about general bullying unless explicitly linked to discrimination categories, or studies focused on higher education admissions policies only if not connected to school-level discrimination.

research_data.desc: Datasets documenting discriminatory patterns and related variables within school settings.
research_data.narr: Include student-level administrative data on enrollment, tracking, disciplinary actions, assessment results and school placement disaggregated by protected characteristics; school climate surveys with measures of perceived discrimination; teacher referral and evaluation records; longitudinal cohort studies tracking minority student outcomes; and datasets from evaluations of anti-discrimination interventions. Include codebooks and variable documentation. Exclude anonymized datasets lacking any indicators of group membership or any variables enabling analysis of discrimination.

variables.desc: Variables that measure discrimination, inequality and related constructs in school contexts.
variables.narr: Include variables indicating student demographics (ethnicity, migration background, language status, socioeconomic status, disability status, gender, religion), indicators of school processes (tracking/streaming, streaming recommendations, special education placement), disciplinary records (suspensions, expulsions), teacher assessments/grades, test scores, measures of experienced discrimination or perceived bias, inclusion/exclusion indicators, and school-level composition and resources. Include variables capturing anti-discrimination measures or interventions. Exclude variables that cannot be disaggregated by group characteristics and therefore cannot inform discrimination analyses.

instruments_tools.desc: Instruments and tools for measuring discrimination, bias and school climate.
instruments_tools.narr: Include validated survey instruments for perceived discrimination and school climate, observational protocols for classroom interactions, teacher implicit bias tests (e.g. adapted IATs), coding schemes for disciplinary decisions, measurement tools for tracking and streamlining practices, evaluation frameworks for anti-discrimination programs, and interview/qualitative guides for investigating discriminatory experiences. Include manuals and psychometric documentation. Exclude informal checklists without validation or tools unrelated to school-level discrimination measurement.

publication.desc: Publications (articles, books, reports) addressing discrimination: its forms, causes, prevalence, policy responses, and impacts in social, labor, education, housing, health, and institutional contexts.
publication.narr: Relevant publications are empirical studies, reviews, theoretical works, and policy reports that explicitly investigate discrimination (diskriminierung) or related concepts such as exclusion, unequal treatment, bias, prejudice, or institutional discrimination. Included are works on discrimination on grounds of race/ethnicity, gender, age, disability, religion, migration status, sexual orientation, or other protected characteristics; research on measurement and methodology for discrimination; and evaluations of anti-discrimination policies and interventions. Exclude publications that merely mention the term without substantive analysis, works focused solely on general inequality without reference to discriminatory mechanisms, and items about biological/medical processes that do not address social discrimination.

research_data.desc: Datasets and data collections measuring experiences, perceptions, or instances of discrimination, including survey data, audit studies, administrative records, and experimental datasets.
research_data.narr: Include datasets that contain variables or modules on perceived discrimination, experienced discriminatory events, audit study outcomes, employer/staffing discrimination experiments, complaints or case records, and indicators of institutional discrimination across domains (employment, education, housing, health). Also include longitudinal and cross-national surveys with discrimination modules. Exclude datasets that do not contain any discrimination-related measures, purely biomedical datasets unrelated to social discrimination, or data that only use 'discrimination' as an unrelated technical term.

variables.desc: Variable definitions and codebooks capturing measures of discrimination: self-reported experiences, perceived discrimination scales, victimization items, audit outcomes, complaint counts, and proxy indicators.
variables.narr: Relevant variables are those explicitly measuring discrimination (e.g., 'experienced discrimination in last 12 months', 'ever treated unfairly because of ethnicity', perceived workplace discrimination scales), variables capturing discriminatory behaviors in experiments or audits (e.g., callback rates by applicant characteristic), and administrative indicators (complaints filed, decisions overturning discrimination claims). Exclude demographic variables that do not operationalize discriminatory experiences, and variables with ambiguous labels not tied to discrimination concepts.

instruments_tools.desc: Surveys, scales, experimental protocols, audit study designs, coding schemes, and measurement instruments developed to assess discrimination and related constructs.
instruments_tools.narr: Include validated questionnaires and scales measuring perceived or experienced discrimination, standardized modules used in social surveys, protocols for field experiments and correspondence/audit studies, coding manuals for discrimination case records, and psychometric evaluations of discrimination measures. Exclude instruments unrelated to social discrimination (e.g., technical discrimination algorithms in signal processing) and generic survey tools lacking discrimination content.

publication.desc: Scholarly and policy publications on education: systems, attainment, access, inequality, pedagogy, labor market returns, and education policy at all levels (early childhood to adult education).
publication.narr: Relevant publications include empirical studies, theoretical analyses, evaluations, and policy reports focused on education topics such as school access, educational attainment, curriculum and pedagogy, teacher quality, educational inequality, special education, vocational training, higher education, lifelong learning, and education policy reforms. Include comparative and country-specific research, quantitative and qualitative studies, and research linking education to outcomes like earnings and social mobility. Exclude publications that refer to 'education' only metaphorically or peripherally, studies solely about non-educational organizations using 'education' as a label, and highly technical works in unrelated fields that use 'education' in a different sense.

research_data.desc: Datasets on educational processes and outcomes: enrollment, attainment, test scores, longitudinal cohort studies, school census data, administrative records, and program evaluation data.
research_data.narr: Include survey datasets (e.g., PISA, TIMSS, national education surveys), administrative school records, longitudinal cohorts tracking educational trajectories, datasets from randomized or quasi-experimental evaluations of educational interventions, and labor market datasets that include education variables. Exclude datasets lacking education-related variables or those where education appears only as a minor demographic descriptor without substantive educational measures.

variables.desc: Variables relating to education: enrollment status, highest educational qualification, years of schooling, test scores, field of study, school characteristics, teacher-student ratios, and participation in educational programs.
variables.narr: Relevant variables explicitly measuring educational dimensions: school attendance, grade repetition, qualifications attained, standardized test results, literacy/numeracy measures, type of school (public/private/vocational), classroom resources, teacher qualifications, and measures of educational attainment over time. Exclude variables that are tangential demographics with no clear educational meaning or ambiguous labels not tied to schooling or learning.

instruments_tools.desc: Measurement instruments and tools used in education research: standardized tests, assessment batteries, curriculum evaluation tools, survey modules on education, and program evaluation protocols.
instruments_tools.narr: Include validated achievement tests, assessment instruments (e.g., reading/math tests), survey modules and questionnaires about schooling and educational attainment, teacher and school evaluation tools, and protocols for implementing and evaluating educational interventions. Exclude general-purpose survey tools without education modules and instruments from unrelated technical domains.

publication.desc: Publications examining attitudes toward Islam and Muslims: public opinion studies, prejudice research, media discourse analyses, and studies on policy implications and social integration.
publication.narr: Include empirical and theoretical works that explicitly measure or analyze attitudes toward Islam or Muslims ("Einstellung zum Islam"), including public opinion surveys, social-psychological studies on prejudice and Islamophobia, media and political discourse analyses, and research on the effects of attitudes on policy, discrimination, and social cohesion. Studies may focus on country-specific or cross-national comparisons, subgroups, or temporal change. Exclude publications that deal with theological scholarship about Islam without addressing public or social attitudes, and works that use 'Islam' only as a background descriptor without analyzing attitudes.

research_data.desc: Datasets containing measures of attitudes toward Islam or Muslims: survey modules, opinion polls, longitudinal attitude panels, and experimental data on prejudice or intergroup attitudes.
research_data.narr: Relevant datasets include public opinion surveys and modules with questions about feelings toward Islam/Muslims, trust, perceived threat, support for policies affecting Muslims, and measures of Islamophobia; panel datasets tracking attitude change; and experimental datasets testing interventions to change attitudes. Exclude datasets without items on Islam/Muslim attitudes or those that only record respondents' religious affiliation without attitudinal measures.

variables.desc: Variables capturing attitudes toward Islam: feeling thermometers, agree/disagree items on Islam-related statements, perceived threat measures, policy preference items related to Muslim communities, and stereotype scales.
variables.narr: Include variables explicitly assessing respondents' views about Islam or Muslims (e.g., 'warmth toward Muslims', 'Islam is compatible with democracy', 'are Muslims a threat to national culture'), measures of social distance from Muslims, and items on discriminatory preferences or policy support targeting Muslim populations. Exclude generic religiosity variables that do not specify attitudes toward Islam, or variables that only identify respondents' religion.

instruments_tools.desc: Survey questions, scales, experimental vignettes, and coding schemes developed to measure attitudes toward Islam and related constructs (Islamophobia, social distance, threat perceptions).
instruments_tools.narr: Include validated attitude scales and survey modules on Islam/Muslims, feeling thermometer items, social distance scales adapted for Muslim targets, vignettes and experimental protocols assessing bias toward Muslims, and coding manuals for media or discourse analysis about Islam. Exclude measurement tools unrelated to attitudes toward Islam or generic instruments without adaptation to Muslim targets.

publication.desc: Publications on attitudes toward immigration/migrants: public opinion research, determinants of immigration attitudes, political consequences, and policy debates.
publication.narr: Include studies that investigate public attitudes toward immigration ("Einstellung zur Zuwanderung"), including support or opposition to immigration levels, attitudes toward specific immigrant groups, determinants of immigration attitudes (economic, cultural, security), media and political framing effects, and links to voting or policy preferences. Both cross-sectional and longitudinal analyses, comparative studies, and evaluations of messaging interventions are relevant. Exclude works focused solely on migration flows, legal procedures, or migrants' own attitudes unless they pertain to public attitudes about immigration.

research_data.desc: Datasets with measures of attitudes toward immigration: national and international opinion polls, survey modules on immigration policy preferences, and experimental datasets on migration attitudes.
research_data.narr: Relevant are surveys containing items on immigration attitudes (e.g., desired levels of immigration, attitudes toward refugees, economic/cultural threat questions), longitudinal panels tracking attitude shifts, and experimental datasets testing interventions or framing effects. Include data that disaggregate attitudes by target group (e.g., refugees, labor migrants). Exclude datasets lacking immigration-attitude measures or those solely documenting migration statistics without attitudinal content.

variables.desc: Variables measuring attitudes toward immigration: support/opposition to immigration levels, policy preference items, perceived economic/cultural threat, openness to refugees, and social distance toward migrants.
variables.narr: Include explicit attitude variables (e.g., 'allow more/fewer immigrants', 'immigrants are a threat to jobs/culture', 'would you accept immigrants as neighbors'), items on policy positions (border control, asylum), and scales measuring tolerance or prejudice toward migrants. Exclude variables that only identify migrants or immigrants as demographics without measuring respondents' attitudes.

instruments_tools.desc: Survey modules, scales, vignettes, and experimental protocols designed to measure or influence attitudes toward immigration and migrants.
instruments_tools.narr: Include standardized question batteries on immigration attitudes, validated threat and social distance scales adapted for migrants, experimental vignette designs manipulating immigrant characteristics, and coding schemes for media or political discourse about migration. Exclude measurement tools not tailored to migration attitudes or purely administrative tools about migration processes.

publication.desc: Publications analyzing attitudes toward foreigners: public opinion, prejudice toward non-nationals, social integration, and consequences for policy and discrimination.
publication.narr: Relevant publications explicitly study attitudes toward foreigners ("Einstellung zu Ausländern") or non-citizen groups, including social-psychological research on prejudice and xenophobia, surveys of public sentiment toward immigrants and foreign residents, analyses of determinants of xenophobic attitudes, and implications for social cohesion and policy. Include comparative and national studies, trend analyses, and works linking attitudes to discriminatory behaviors. Exclude studies about foreign policy or international relations that use 'foreigner' in a diplomatic or state-centric context without addressing public attitudes toward people.

research_data.desc: Datasets containing measures of attitudes toward foreigners: opinion polls, social surveys, longitudinal panels, and experiments measuring xenophobia or social distance to non-nationals.
research_data.narr: Include datasets with items on feelings toward foreigners, willingness to accept foreigners as neighbors/co-workers, perceived threats from foreigners, and policy preferences affecting foreigners. Experimental and vignette datasets that manipulate foreigner characteristics are relevant. Exclude datasets without questions on foreigners or those that treat 'foreigner' only as a trait of respondents without attitudinal measures.

variables.desc: Variables that capture attitudes toward foreigners: feeling thermometers, social distance items, perceived threat scales, and policy preference questions specific to foreign populations.
variables.narr: Include explicit variables such as 'warmth toward foreigners', 'would you accept foreigners as neighbors', 'foreigners take jobs from locals', support for restrictions on foreigners, and measures of xenophobic sentiments. Exclude general demographic variables indicating foreigner status or nationality that do not measure attitudes.

instruments_tools.desc: Measurement instruments for attitudes toward foreigners: survey questions, xenophobia scales, experimental vignettes, and coding schemes for discourse about foreigners.
instruments_tools.narr: Include validated scales and survey modules assessing xenophobia and attitudes toward foreigners, social distance measures, experimental protocols testing bias against foreigners, and tools for content analysis of media or political rhetoric about foreigners. Exclude instruments unrelated to social attitudes or those focusing on diplomatic/legal definitions rather than public perceptions of people.

publication.desc: Scholarly publications (articles, books, chapters, reports) analyzing attitudes toward 'foreigners', migrants, immigrants, or ethnic outgroups; includes theoretical and empirical studies in sociology, political science, social psychology, and migration studies.
publication.narr: Include works that empirically or theoretically address attitudes, opinions, stereotypes, prejudice, xenophobia, social distance, integration attitudes, or public opinion regarding 'foreigners' (Fremde) or immigrants. Relevant publications cover national or comparative studies, qualitative and quantitative analyses, longitudinal and cross-sectional research, policy reports, and literature reviews on immigrant attitudes. Exclude items that focus exclusively on unrelated meanings of 'Fremde' (e.g., literary uses without social-attitudinal analysis), studies on mobility or tourism that do not address attitudes toward outgroups, and purely biological/medical studies that do not examine social attitudes.

research_data.desc: Survey datasets, panel data, and experimental data that measure attitudes toward foreigners, immigrants, or ethnic outgroups, including national social surveys, migration modules, and cross-national datasets.
research_data.narr: Include datasets containing variables measuring attitudes to foreigners/immigrants (e.g., feeling thermometers, social distance, willingness to accept immigrants, perceived threats), experimental vignette data on outgroup attitudes, and modules from large surveys (e.g., ESS, Eurobarometer, World Values Survey, national social surveys) that explicitly ask about 'Fremde' or immigrants. Exclude datasets without attitudinal items about foreigners, purely administrative population registers, and datasets that only record migration flows without public-opinion measures.

variables.desc: Variable labels and operationalizations that capture attitudes toward foreigners/immigrants: social distance, xenophobia indices, acceptance scales, perceived threat, trust, and contact measures.
variables.narr: Include variables named or operationalized as attitudes toward foreigners/immigrants, social distance (e.g., willingness to live next door/work with/marry a foreigner), xenophobia or prejudice scales, perceived economic/cultural threat, feeling thermometer scores for 'foreigners' or immigrant groups, and intergroup contact frequency/quality. Exclude demographic variables only (age, sex) unless they are combined with attitudinal measures, and variables that measure migration status alone without attitudinal content.

instruments_tools.desc: Questionnaires, survey modules, scales and coding schemes used to measure attitudes to foreigners: social distance scales (e.g., Bogardus items), prejudice/xenophobia indexes, contact measures, and vignette instruments.
instruments_tools.narr: Include validated instruments and bespoke survey modules that measure attitudes toward foreigners or immigrants (e.g., Bogardus Social Distance Scale items adapted for immigrants, threat/perceived competition scales, feeling thermometer items, experimental vignettes manipulating immigrant characteristics). Also include coding manuals and question wordings used in major surveys. Exclude measurement tools unrelated to social attitudes (e.g., clinical scales) and instruments that only measure immigrant demographics without attitudinal items.

publication.desc: Research publications examining attitudes toward gender, gender roles, gender equality, sexism, and related normative beliefs across disciplines such as sociology, gender studies, psychology, and political science.
publication.narr: Include empirical and theoretical publications on gender attitudes (attitudes about gender roles, gender equality in work/family/politics, gender ideology, sexism, and discrimination), comparative and national studies, longitudinal trends, and interventions to change gender attitudes. Exclude publications that use 'gender' solely as a demographic variable without analyzing attitudes, technical gender theory texts with no attitudinal focus, and medical/biological studies that do not engage with social attitudes.

research_data.desc: Datasets containing measures of gender attitudes: survey modules on gender role beliefs, support for gender equality, sexism scales, and related behavioral intention items from national and cross-national surveys.
research_data.narr: Include datasets with items on gender role ideology, support for gender equality policies (e.g., quotas, parental leave), ambivalent sexism measures, and behavioral measures related to gender attitudes. Relevant sources include ESS, ISSP modules on family and gender, World Values Survey items, national gender surveys, and experimental datasets on gender attitudes. Exclude datasets lacking attitudinal measures about gender or those that only record respondents' gender without opinion items.

variables.desc: Variables operationalizing attitudes toward gender: gender role ideology, support for equality, ambivalent sexism subscales, policy support, and stereotypes about male/female traits and capabilities.
variables.narr: Include variables labeled or constructed as traditional/egalitarian gender attitudes, ambivalent sexism (hostile and benevolent sexism), beliefs about women’s employment or leadership, willingness to share domestic labor, and policy support for gender-equality measures. Also include variables measuring gendered stereotypes, perceived gender discrimination, and gender-targeted policy preferences. Exclude purely descriptive demographic variables or occupational classifications unless combined with explicit attitudinal indicators.

instruments_tools.desc: Questionnaires and measurement tools used to assess gender attitudes: standardized scales (e.g., Ambivalent Sexism Inventory), ISSP/EFA gender modules, question batteries on gender roles, and coding schemes for gender-attitude items.
instruments_tools.narr: Include validated instruments and commonly used survey question wordings for measuring gender attitudes (Ambivalent Sexism Inventory, Gender Role Attitudes scales, ISSP Family and Changing Gender Roles module items), guidance on constructing indices, and experimental vignettes manipulating gender cues. Exclude instruments that measure biological sex or gender identity only, or clinical instruments unrelated to social attitudes.

publication.desc: Scholarly publications analyzing attitudes toward Islam and Muslims, Islamophobia, integration debates, and public opinion concerning Islam in societal and political contexts.
publication.narr: Include empirical and theoretical studies on public attitudes toward Islam/Muslims, prejudice and discrimination against Muslims, media representation, political mobilization around Islam, and comparative research on Islam-related attitudes. Also include policy analyses and surveys of public opinion about Islamic practices and Muslim communities. Exclude theological treatises on Islam that do not address public attitudes, purely historical studies without connection to contemporary attitudes, and medical research unrelated to social perceptions.

research_data.desc: Datasets that measure attitudes toward Islam or Muslims: national and cross-national opinion surveys, targeted attitude modules, and experimental data on anti-Muslim attitudes and social distance.
research_data.narr: Include datasets with items on favorability/unfavorability toward Islam or Muslims, perceived threat from Islam (cultural/security), social distance measures vis-à-vis Muslims, support for policies affecting Muslims (e.g., mosque building, headscarf bans), and experimental manipulations about Muslim identity. Relevant sources include ESS, Eurobarometer, World Values Survey, national opinion polls, and specialized Islamophobia studies. Exclude datasets without Islam/Muslim attitudinal measures and administrative datasets with only population counts.

variables.desc: Variables capturing attitudes to Islam/Muslims: favorability ratings, social distance items, perceived threat scales (cultural/security/economic), discrimination experiences, and policy preference variables.
variables.narr: Include variables explicitly measuring views toward Islam or Muslims, such as feeling thermometer scores, willingness to accept Muslim neighbors/colleagues, indexes of Islamophobia, perceived compatibility of Islam with national values, and support/opposition to specific policies affecting Muslims. Also include variables for contact with Muslims and media exposure to Islamic issues. Exclude general religiosity measures that do not specify attitudes toward Islam or Muslims.

instruments_tools.desc: Measurement instruments and survey modules for attitudes toward Islam: Islamophobia scales, social distance questionnaires, question wordings on Muslim-related policies, and vignette experiments concerning Muslim characteristics.
instruments_tools.narr: Include validated scales and commonly used items for measuring anti-Muslim attitudes (e.g., Islamophobia Scale adaptations), Bogardus-style social distance items tailored to Muslims, policy-question batteries (e.g., mosque, dress codes), and experimental vignettes manipulating religious identity. Also include coding guides and translations of question wordings. Exclude theological assessment tools or instruments measuring Muslim religiosity without items on public attitudes toward Islam.

publication.desc: Publications on employment, labor market dynamics, workplace policies, and employment-related outcomes in Poland, including comparative studies of the Polish labor market.
publication.narr: Include empirical studies, policy reports, working papers, and books addressing employment rates, unemployment, labor force participation, job quality, informal employment, migration-for-work, youth employment, gendered employment patterns, and labor market reforms in Poland. Also include comparative European analyses where Poland is a focal case. Exclude publications about employment in other countries that merely mention Poland in passing, and studies unrelated to labor market or employment (e.g., general demographic history without labor analysis).

research_data.desc: Datasets relevant to employment in Poland: national labor force surveys, administrative employment registers, EU microdata (e.g., EU LFS, SILC), and specialized Polish panel studies containing employment variables.
research_data.narr: Include datasets that provide employment status, occupation, industry, working hours, wages, contract type, transitions in employment, and job search variables for Poland. Examples include the Polish Labour Force Survey, EU-LFS extracts for Poland, Generations and Gender Survey Poland if containing employment modules, and administrative social security/employment registers. Exclude datasets without employment-related variables or those not covering Poland specifically.

variables.desc: Variables describing employment outcomes in Poland: employment/unemployment status, sector/industry, occupation codes, contract type, working hours, wages/salary, job tenure, and labor market transitions.
variables.narr: Include variables indicating current employment status (employed, unemployed, inactive), detailed occupation (ISCO), industry (NACE), full-/part-time status, temporary/permanent contract, net/gross wages, hours worked, job search activity, and reason for job exit/hire. Also include variables on informal employment and cross-border commuting when relevant to Poland. Exclude variables unrelated to labor (e.g., clinical health measures) unless linked to employment outcomes.

instruments_tools.desc: Survey instruments and administrative tools used to measure employment in Poland: LFS questionnaires, national employment survey modules, coding manuals (ISCO/NACE), and administrative data linkage protocols.
instruments_tools.narr: Include full question wordings from labor force and employment surveys used in Poland (Polish LFS, EU-LFS modules), standardized occupation and industry coding schemes (ISCO, NACE), wage imputation procedures, and documentation for linking administrative employment records. Also include questionnaires for employment histories and job quality assessments. Exclude instruments unrelated to employment measurement or those applicable only outside the Polish context without adaptation.

publication.desc: Scholarly works on alienation from work (Entfremdung der Arbeit), including theoretical treatments (Marxist and sociological), empirical studies of job alienation, and research on related constructs like meaning at work and disengagement.
publication.narr: Include theoretical analyses of work alienation (classical Marxist theory and modern revisions), empirical studies measuring dimensions of alienation (powerlessness, meaninglessness, isolation, self-estrangement), occupational studies, organizational psychology research on alienation and job satisfaction, and comparative labor studies. Exclude uses of 'alienation' unrelated to work (e.g., cultural alienation in a non-work context) unless explicitly linked to employment or occupational experience.

research_data.desc: Datasets containing measures of work alienation or related constructs (job meaning, engagement, burnout, job satisfaction) from workplace surveys, employee panels, and national surveys with work modules.
research_data.narr: Include datasets with items operationalizing work alienation (e.g., Seeman-based scales), measures of job meaning, autonomy, control, task variety, and social isolation at work. Relevant sources include organizational surveys, European Working Conditions Survey, national workplace panels, and company employee surveys. Exclude datasets that only record occupation or industry without attitudinal/psychological measures concerning work experience.

variables.desc: Variables operationalizing dimensions of work alienation: powerlessness, meaninglessness, normlessness, isolation, self-estrangement, lack of autonomy, and low task significance.
variables.narr: Include variables explicitly labeled as alienation or constructed from items addressing feelings of powerlessness at work, lack of control/autonomy, work being meaningless or monotonous, social isolation from colleagues, inability to realize oneself in work, and related indices combining these facets. Also include related measures such as job satisfaction, organizational commitment, and burnout when used to assess alienation. Exclude purely economic variables (wages/hours) unless combined with subjective alienation measures.

instruments_tools.desc: Measurement instruments for work alienation: validated scales (e.g., Seeman's scales, Blauner’s items), questionnaires for autonomy/control, job meaning scales, and coding manuals for constructing alienation indices.
instruments_tools.narr: Include established instruments and question batteries measuring work alienation and its subdimensions (e.g., Seeman's alienation constructs, Work Alienation Scale adaptations, items on autonomy and meaningfulness), survey modules from EWCS or company HR surveys, and guidance on index construction and validation. Also include qualitative interview guides focusing on alienation experiences at work. Exclude general wellbeing instruments not tied to work context unless they incorporate workplace-specific items.

publication.desc: Publications addressing the natural, built and social environment, including environmental science, environmental policy, pollution, sustainability, environmental health, and environmental education.
publication.narr: Relevant publications report empirical studies, reviews, theory, policy analyses or evaluations focused on environmental topics: ecology, climate change, air/water/soil pollution, environmental policy and governance, sustainability transitions, environmental justice, urban and built environment studies, and environmental attitudes/behaviour. Include cross-disciplinary social science work that treats environmental outcomes or human–environment interactions as a principal focus. Exclude works that use 'environment' only metaphorically or as incidental context (e.g., generic organizational "work environment" references with no environmental or ecological content), unless the organizational environment is analyzed for environmental outcomes or sustainability.

research_data.desc: Datasets that measure environmental conditions, exposures, policies or human attitudes/behaviours toward the environment, including monitoring data, survey modules and geospatial/environmental health data.
research_data.narr: Include datasets containing environmental monitoring (air, water, soil quality), geospatial data on land use/green space, exposure and health linkage data, longitudinal or cross-sectional surveys with environmental modules (attitudes, behaviour, risk perception), and policy or administrative databases on environmental regulation and implementation. Exclude datasets unrelated to environmental phenomena (e.g., purely economic or organizational datasets) unless they contain substantive environmental measures or linkages.

variables.desc: Variables operationalizing environmental conditions, exposures, perceptions, attitudes and behaviours, e.g., pollution indices, green space proximity, ecological indicators, and measures of environmental concern or pro-environmental behaviour.
variables.narr: Relevant variables include objective environmental measures (PM2.5, NOx, water contaminants, biodiversity indices), GIS-derived measures (distance to parks, land-cover percentages), and socio-psychological variables (environmental concern, risk perception, frequency of recycling, energy consumption, willingness-to-pay). Exclude variables that only incidentally mention 'environment' without measuring environmental attributes or attitudes (for example, a variable labeled "environment" that is a general control for context with no environmental meaning).

instruments_tools.desc: Measurement instruments and tools used in environmental research: ecological assessment protocols, environmental attitude scales, sensors and monitoring devices, GIS tools, and survey modules (e.g., ISSP/ESS environment modules).
instruments_tools.narr: Include validated attitude scales (e.g., NEP), standardized monitoring protocols, sensor specifications and calibration procedures, GIS/remote sensing workflows, and survey modules designed to capture environmental attitudes, behaviours and perceptions. Exclude generic measurement tools that are not applied to environmental measurement (e.g., general psychometric scales with no environmental items) unless adapted for environmental research.

publication.desc: Publications studying attitudes toward the environment: measurement, determinants, outcomes, cross-national comparisons, and links between attitudes and behaviour or policy support.
publication.narr: Include empirical and theoretical publications that define, measure, validate or analyse environmental attitudes (e.g., concern for environment, ecological worldview, climate worry), including psychometric studies of scales, determinants (socio-demographic, cultural, political), and consequences for behaviour and policy preferences.
