Exclude texts that mention environmental attitude only peripherally or focus solely on objective environmental indicators without considering attitudes or perceptions.

research_data.desc: Survey and panel datasets that include measures of environmental attitudes and related constructs (e.g., ISSP Environment module, European Social Survey items, national surveys with environmental questions).
research_data.narr: Include cross-sectional and longitudinal survey datasets, modules and harmonized collections containing items on environmental concern, NEP items, willingness-to-pay, perceived risks, and behavioural intentions. Also include experimental datasets testing interventions to change environmental attitudes. Exclude datasets lacking attitudinal items or containing only objective environmental measures with no attitudinal/perceptual variables.

variables.desc: Variables capturing environmental attitudes and related constructs: scale scores (NEP, environmental concern indices), single-item measures (concern about climate change), and related belief/perception indicators.
variables.narr: Relevant variables are composite scores and individual items assessing environmental concern, ecological worldview, perceived seriousness of environmental problems, climate change belief, support for environmental policies, and self-reported pro-environmental behaviours. Include coding information, item wording, response scales and psychometric properties. Exclude variables labeled ambiguously that do not measure attitudes (e.g., purely behavioural or objective environmental metrics) unless paired with attitudinal items.

instruments_tools.desc: Validated instruments and survey modules for measuring environmental attitudes: NEP scale, Environmental Concern scales, ISSP/ESS environment modules, and experimental vignettes for attitude measurement.
instruments_tools.narr: Include multi-item scales (e.g., New Ecological Paradigm), standard survey modules (ISSP Environment, ESS environment-related items), validated short-form scales, question batteries with phrasing and response options, and measurement guides. Also include tools for scale validation (factor analysis scripts, reliability coefficients). Exclude generic attitude instruments that do not include environmental content.

publication.desc: Publications on Erziehung (upbringing, education, socialization): family socialization, parenting, early childhood education, formal education processes, and pedagogical theory, including German-language literature.
publication.narr: Include empirical studies, theoretical works and reviews focusing on upbringing, parenting practices, childrearing, educational methods (Erziehung in German pedagogical sense), socialization processes, and comparative studies of educational systems. Include German-language publications and works that use 'Erziehung' as a primary concept. Exclude uses of 'Erziehung' in highly specialized non-pedagogical senses (e.g., historical usages unrelated to human development) or documents that only mention the term tangentially.

research_data.desc: Datasets relevant to Erziehung: household and family surveys, child development panels, school-based studies, and longitudinal cohorts that record parenting, education, and socialization measures.
research_data.narr: Include datasets with variables on parenting style, parental involvement, child outcomes (cognitive, socioemotional), early childhood programs, educational attainment and pedagogical interventions. Prefer datasets with items or variables labeled in German or from German-speaking contexts, but also include international data relevant to upbringing and education research. Exclude datasets that do not contain measures related to upbringing, parenting or educational processes.

variables.desc: Variables measuring aspects of Erziehung: parental practices, disciplinary strategies, educational activities, home learning environment, teacher attitudes, and child development outcomes.
variables.narr: Include variables capturing parenting styles (authoritative, authoritarian, permissive), frequency of parent–child activities, disciplinary measures, indicators of early learning environment (e.g., HOME inventory items), school pedagogy variables, and child cognitive and socio-emotional outcome measures. Exclude variables unrelated to upbringing or educational socialization (e.g., purely economic indicators) unless directly used to study Erziehung.

instruments_tools.desc: Measurement instruments and pedagogical tools used in research on Erziehung: parenting questionnaires, HOME inventory, standardized child development tests, teacher-report scales, and curriculum/intervention materials.
instruments_tools.narr: Include validated parenting and family functioning questionnaires (e.g., Parenting Styles and Dimensions Questionnaire), observational protocols, early childhood assessment tools, teacher rating instruments, and intervention manuals for parenting or educational programs. Include German-language instruments or translations and documentation of reliability/validity. Exclude tools that are not designed to measure upbringing, parenting or educational processes.

publication.desc: Publications on evaluation in social work (Evaluation Soziale Arbeit): program evaluation, outcome assessment, methods and best practices specific to social work practice and services, including German-language literature.
publication.narr: Include empirical evaluations of social work programs, methodological papers on evaluation design in social work, case studies, systematic reviews and theoretical contributions on measuring social work outcomes. Focus on works that address evaluation frameworks, indicators of client well‑being, fidelity, implementation, and effectiveness within social work contexts. Exclude generic program-evaluation literature with no application to social work or documents that only mention social work tangentially.

research_data.desc: Datasets derived from evaluations of social work programs: administrative case files, outcome measurement datasets, longitudinal follow-ups of clients, and monitoring data collected for program assessment.
research_data.narr: Include datasets from randomized or quasi-experimental evaluations of social work interventions, routine outcome monitoring systems used by social service agencies, administrative records on service delivery and client outcomes, and qualitative evaluation datasets (interviews, focus groups). Prefer datasets containing pre/post measures, comparison groups, or implementation fidelity metrics. Exclude datasets from unrelated social programs unless they are directly relevant to social work services and evaluation.

variables.desc: Variables used in social work evaluation: client outcomes (well-being, employment, recidivism), service usage, fidelity indicators, process measures, and contextual factors affecting program success.
variables.narr: Relevant variables include standardized outcome scales (quality of life, symptom scales), indicators of service access and intensity, recidivism or re-referral rates, client satisfaction, and implementation/process measures (caseworker contacts, adherence to protocol). Include socio-demographic covariates commonly used in evaluation. Exclude variables that do not inform intervention effectiveness or implementation (e.g., unrelated administrative codes) unless necessary for record linkage.

instruments_tools.desc: Evaluation instruments and tools for social work: outcome measurement scales, case management systems, logic models, standardized assessment tools (e.g., HoNOS, CORE-OM where applicable), and guidelines for programme evaluation in social work.
instruments_tools.narr: Include validated outcome scales used in social care, structured assessment tools, protocols for routine outcome monitoring, implementation fidelity checklists, cost-effectiveness templates, and evaluation toolkits tailored to social work practice (including German-language toolkits). Also include qualitative evaluation guides and mixed-methods instruments commonly used in social work evaluations. Exclude general evaluation tools that are not adapted to social work contexts unless documented as applied successfully in social work settings.

publication.desc: Publications examining external political efficacy: conceptualization, measurement, determinants, consequences for political behaviour, and cross-national comparisons.
publication.narr: Include theoretical and empirical studies that define and measure external political efficacy (the belief that political institutions and actors are responsive to citizens), its antecedents (trust, representation, media, socioeconomic status), and outcomes (participation, protest, policy support). Include scale development/validation papers and comparative research using national or cross-national survey data. Exclude works that only discuss internal efficacy or general political efficacy without separate treatment of external efficacy.

research_data.desc: Survey datasets containing measures of external political efficacy: e.g., ANES, ESS, Eurobarometer, ISSP, GSS and national election studies that include efficacy items.
research_data.narr: Include datasets with one- or multi-item measures of external political efficacy (e.g., items about responsiveness of government, influence over decisions), often alongside political trust and participation measures. Preference for datasets enabling comparative analysis or longitudinal study of efficacy. Exclude datasets lacking efficacy or closely related attitudinal items.

variables.desc: Variables operationalizing external political efficacy and closely related constructs: survey items and composite indices measuring perceived responsiveness of government, influence over political decisions, and trust in institutions.
variables.narr: Include individual items (e.g., 'People like me have no say in what the government does'), composite external efficacy scales, and coding information (item wording, response categories, scoring). Also include related variables such as political trust, internal political efficacy, political participation, and socio-demographics used as covariates. Exclude poorly defined variables that do not capture perceptions of institutional responsiveness.

instruments_tools.desc: Measurement instruments and survey modules used to assess external political efficacy: validated scale items, survey batteries from major studies (ANES, ESS, ISSP), and analytic tools for constructing efficacy indices.
instruments_tools.narr: Include standard question wordings and response formats for external efficacy items, validated multi-item scales where available, harmonization guides for cross-national comparison, and codebooks/scripts for scale construction and reliability testing. Exclude measurement tools that only address internal efficacy or general civic attitudes without items on institutional responsiveness.

publication.desc: Studies and reports on family–work interactions, work–family conflict, parental employment, reconciliation policies, and employment patterns among parents.
publication.narr: Include publications (articles, books, reports, policy papers) that examine how family responsibilities and employment interact: parental employment trajectories, part‑time vs full‑time work, maternity/paternity leave, childcare use and access, flexible working arrangements, work–family conflict, employer practices affecting families, and cross‑national comparisons of family‑friendly labour policies. Include empirical studies, longitudinal analyses, and policy evaluations. Exclude works focused solely on unrelated labour market topics (e.g., unemployment without family context), purely clinical family therapy, or biological/fertility studies that do not address employment or reconciliation of work and family.

research_data.desc: Datasets capturing employment and family variables: panel surveys, cross‑sectional household surveys, time‑use studies, administrative employment and benefits records, and matched employer‑employee data.
research_data.narr: Include datasets that enable analysis of parents' labour force participation, working hours, occupation, leave uptake, childcare utilization, household composition, and related outcomes (income, job mobility). Relevant types: longitudinal panels (e.g., household panels, cohort studies), time‑use diaries, register/administrative data linking employment and family status, employer surveys on flexible work, and cross‑national comparative data. Exclude purely clinical or genomic datasets, datasets without family or employment variables, and those lacking documentation for construction of family/employment indicators.

variables.desc: Key variables on family composition and employment: parental employment status, working hours, occupation, job tenure, leave usage, childcare arrangements, number/age of children, marital status, and household income.
variables.narr: Include variables that measure: current employment (employed/unemployed/out of labour force), working hours (hours/week, part‑time/full‑time), occupation/industry, job contract type, career breaks, maternity/paternity/parental leave (duration, uptake), childcare use and costs, number and ages of children, household composition, partner's employment, household income, education, commute time, and job flexibility. Also include subjective measures: perceived work–family conflict, job satisfaction related to family, and employer support. Exclude variables unrelated to family or employment (e.g., detailed clinical biomarkers) or variables without documentation for coding.

instruments_tools.desc: Survey modules, time‑use diaries, life‑history calendars, administrative linkage protocols, employer questionnaires, and standard scales measuring work–family conflict and reconciliation policies.
instruments_tools.narr: Include instruments used to collect or measure work–family data: household roster modules, employment histories, occupational coding schemes (e.g., ISCO), standardized time‑use diaries, validated scales for work–family conflict/work‑life balance (e.g., Netemeyer work–family conflict items), parental leave and childcare modules, life history calendars capturing career and family events, employer survey instruments on flexible work, and protocols for linking administrative employment/benefit records to family registers. Exclude instruments focused only on clinical assessment or unrelated domains.

publication.desc: Research on the interplay between family life and career development: career trajectories of parents, gendered career outcomes, childcare effects on career progression, and organizational career policies.
publication.narr: Include publications that investigate how family formation, parenthood, and caregiving influence career paths, promotion chances, occupational mobility, earnings trajectories, and career interruptions. Also include employer and policy analyses addressing career support (mentoring, flexible schedules, parental leave impact on careers). Prioritize empirical longitudinal research, qualitative career histories, and comparative studies of career outcomes by family status. Exclude literature solely about family therapy, fertility biology, or career studies that do not consider family or caregiving factors.

research_data.desc: Datasets that document career histories alongside family events: panel studies, employer HR data, administrative registers linking employment, earnings and family status, and qualitative career interview data.
research_data.narr: Include data enabling analysis of career outcomes in relation to family life: longitudinal employment histories, wage records, promotions, occupational codes, parental leave records, family formation dates, and childcare usage. Relevant sources: national registers, household panels, employer HR databases, and life history interview datasets. Datasets should permit temporal sequencing of family events and career changes. Exclude datasets lacking career trajectory or family event information.

variables.desc: Variables capturing career and family events: promotion history, earnings, job tenure, job mobility, occupational status, leave spells, number/age of children, and partner employment.
variables.narr: Include variables measuring career outcomes (wages/income, promotions, occupational status/authority level, full/part‑time status, job tenure and contract type, career interruptions, re‑entry timing), and family indicators (date of childbirth, number/age of children, caregiving responsibilities, spousal employment). Also include education, training participation, workplace policies available, and subjective career aspirations. Exclude variables that do not allow linking family events and career timelines.

instruments_tools.desc: Career history modules, employer HR surveys, life‑history calendars, promotion and salary coding schemes, qualitative interview guides on career and family balancing.
instruments_tools.narr: Include instruments for capturing career trajectories and family timing: structured career history questionnaires, administrative payroll and HR data extraction tools, life course calendars mapping births and job changes, occupational coding (ISCO), pay scale coding, standardized measures of career progression and ambition, and semi‑structured interview guides exploring career decisions after family events. Exclude instruments not designed to record temporal links between family and career.

publication.desc: Scholarly works on transformations in gender roles within families: changing division of labour, parental roles, gender role attitudes, and implications for family structure and policy.
publication.narr: Include publications that analyze shifts in gender norms and practices inside households: trends in fathers' involvement in childcare, women's labour market participation, negotiation of household tasks, couple dynamics, intergenerational changes in gender attitudes, and policy effects on gender role change. Include quantitative trend analyses, qualitative ethnographies, cross‑national comparisons, and theoretical work on gender and family change. Exclude studies that treat gender only biologically or that focus exclusively on non‑family institutional gender dynamics without linking to family life.

research_data.desc: Surveys and qualitative datasets that capture gender attitudes, division of household labour, parental involvement, childcare responsibilities, and temporal changes (repeat cross‑sections, panels, time‑use data).
research_data.narr: Include datasets documenting attitudes toward gender roles (e.g., ESS, WVS), time‑use diaries showing allocation of domestic and care tasks, panel or cohort studies measuring change over time within households, and qualitative interview collections on gendered practices. Also include cross‑national comparative datasets that allow study of policy impacts on gender roles. Exclude datasets that lack measures of gender attitudes or intra‑household task allocation.

variables.desc: Measures of gender attitudes, division of household labour, time spent on childcare/domestic tasks, employment by gender, parental leave uptake by gender, and household decision‑making indicators.
variables.narr: Include variables such as: responses to gender attitude statements (e.g., views on working mothers, male breadwinner model), time‑use minutes by activity and by household member, caregiver role indicators (primary carer), distribution of specific chores, parental leave uptake and duration by sex, employment status by gender, negotiation/decision‑making variables, and indicators of childcare arrangements. Also include demographic controls (age, education, cohort). Exclude generic demographic variables without gendered household context.

instruments_tools.desc: Standardized attitude batteries (e.g., ESS gender items), time‑use diary instruments, household task inventories, qualitative interview guides on gender and family, and coding schemes for task allocation.
instruments_tools.narr: Include measurement instruments used to study changing gender roles: survey modules on gender role attitudes (items from ESS, WVS, Eurobarometer), validated scales for egalitarianism, 24‑hour or activity‑based time‑use diaries, household chore checklists, life history interviews capturing shifts in role expectations, observational protocols for family interaction, and methods for coding and quantifying task division. Exclude tools not applicable to measuring gendered behaviour or attitudes in family contexts.

publication.desc: Broad literature on family: family structure, life course transitions, parenting, households, kinship, intergenerational relations, family policy, and demographic trends.
publication.narr: Include publications covering empirical and theoretical research on families and households: marriage/cohabitation, divorce/separation, fertility and childbearing, parenting practices, intergenerational support, household composition, kin networks, demographic change, family policy, and socioeconomic determinants of family outcomes. Include cross‑disciplinary work (sociology, demography, social policy, psychology) and both quantitative and qualitative studies. Exclude works that use 'family' only metaphorically or unrelated technical uses (e.g., mathematical families) and clinical case reports not addressing broader family processes.

research_data.desc: Comprehensive datasets on family and household topics: censuses, household surveys, panel/cohort studies, vital statistics, register data, time‑use studies, and qualitative family interview collections.
research_data.narr: Include data sources that allow analysis of family composition and dynamics: national censuses and vital registration (births, marriages, deaths), household budget and labour force surveys with family modules, longitudinal household panels, cohort studies following family life courses, time‑use surveys for household behaviour, and qualitative datasets on family relationships. Data should contain household/kinship identifiers or modules to construct family units. Exclude datasets unrelated to family or lacking documentation to assemble family measures.

variables.desc: Core family variables: household composition, marital/cohabitation status, number and age of children, parental status, kin availability, household income, fertility histories, residential arrangements, and intergenerational transfers.
variables.narr: Include variables that allow characterization of family structure and dynamics: household roster entries, relationship to head, marital status, partnership dates, childbirth dates, fertility histories, number/age of children, coresidence with parents/children, caregiving receipt/provision, household income and resources, housing arrangements, and measures of family support and conflict. Also include demographic controls (age, sex, education, region). Exclude variables that cannot be linked to family units or lack sufficient metadata.

instruments_tools.desc: Household rosters, family history calendars, vital record linkage protocols, time‑use instruments, parenting questionnaires, kinship matrix coding schemes, and qualitative interview guides on family life.
instruments_tools.narr: Include instruments for collecting family data: standard household roster modules, life‑history and event history calendars capturing marriages and births, protocols for linking administrative vital records to survey data, 24‑hour and episode‑based time‑use diaries, parenting and caregiving scales, intergenerational transfer modules, and semi‑structured interview guides on family relationships. Include classification schemes for household types and kinship coding. Exclude instruments that do not support constructing family or household indicators.

publication.desc: Research at the intersection of family and gender: gendered family roles, parenting practices, division of labour, gender inequalities within households, and gendered effects of family policy.
publication.narr: Include empirical and theoretical publications exploring how gender shapes family life and how family contexts shape gender relations: studies on maternal and paternal roles, gender gaps in earnings and care, negotiation of household tasks, gendered impacts of parenthood, intersectionality (race/class) in family gender dynamics, and evaluations of policies affecting gender equality in families. Prioritize works that explicitly analyze both family and gender dimensions. Exclude research addressing gender in non‑family institutions only, or family studies that ignore gendered processes.

research_data.desc: Datasets linking family composition and behaviour to gendered attitudes and practices: time‑use, attitude surveys, household panels with gender modules, administrative data with parental gender roles, and qualitative gendered family studies.
research_data.narr: Include datasets providing measures of family structure, division of labour, caregiving, parental leave/use by sex, employment by gender, and gender attitude items. Relevant sources: time‑use surveys disaggregated by sex, cross‑national attitude surveys (ESS, WVS), panel datasets capturing changes in family roles by gender, and qualitative interview sets focused on gendered family experiences. Exclude datasets lacking sex‑disaggregated family measures or gender attitude indicators.

variables.desc: Variables linking gender and family: sex/gender of household members, gender attitudes, time spent on domestic and care work by gender, parental leave uptake by sex, employment status by sex, and measures of intra‑household decision making.
variables.narr: Include variables that permit analysis of gendered family dynamics: respondent sex/gender, partner's sex/gender, gender identity if available, allocation of household chores and childcare by gender, paid/unpaid work hours by gender, parental leave and flexible work uptake by sex, attitudes toward gender roles, measures of power/decision making in the household, and indicators of gendered outcomes (income gaps, career interruptions). Also include intersectional markers (education, ethnicity). Exclude variables without gender or family relevance.

instruments_tools.desc: Gender attitude batteries, sex‑disaggregated time‑use diaries, household chore inventories, parental leave registries by sex, interview guides on gendered family roles, and coding schemes for gendered task allocation.
instruments_tools.narr: Include instruments designed to capture gendered dimensions of family life: validated gender‑attitude items (ESS/WVS), 24‑hour and activity‑based time‑use instruments with respondent sex, modules on distribution of household tasks, administrative registries recording parental leave by gender, qualitative interview protocols probing gendered decision making and care practices, and analytical tools for coding and quantifying gendered divisions of labour. Exclude measurement tools that do not distinguish gender or cannot be applied to family contexts.

publication.desc: Scholarly and policy publications that define, measure, compare or evaluate types of employment contracts and work arrangements (e.g., full-time, part-time, temporary/fixed-term, permanent, self-employed, gig work, on-call, zero-hours, agency work, telework). Includes comparative, historical, legal, labor-economics, and social policy studies addressing causes, consequences and measurement issues of different employment forms.
publication.narr: Relevant publications: empirical articles, reviews and reports that explicitly focus on the classification, prevalence, determinants or outcomes of distinct forms of employment; papers that use international or national definitional frameworks (ILO, EU) or propose typologies of employment. Include studies of working hours, contract type, job tenure, precarious work and gig economy that report operational definitions. Exclude works that use 'form' in unrelated senses (e.g., corporate legal form, organizational form unrelated to individual employment contracts), publications solely about macroeconomic indicators without disaggregating employment types, or papers that only nominally mention employment form without measures or definitions.

research_data.desc: Datasets and survey modules that record employment contract and arrangement details: employment status, contract type (permanent/temporary), working hours, self-employment vs. employee, agency/gig work, telework/home-based work, job tenure and multiple job-holding. Typical sources include labor force surveys, panel studies and employer-employee linked data.
research_data.narr: Relevant data: microdata from labor force surveys and panels (e.g., EU-LFS, national LFS/microcensus, household panel surveys such as SOEP/GSOEP, CPS, national longitudinal employer-employee datasets) and targeted surveys of gig/platform workers or temporary agency workers that contain variables describing contract type, working hours, pay basis, and job security. Include administrative or employer establishment data that can be linked to individual contract types. Exclude datasets that only provide aggregate employment counts without contract-level detail, or data that cover organizational/legal forms unrelated to individual worker contracts.

variables.desc: Variables that operationalize the concept of employment form: employment_status, contract_type, job_type, employment_relation, working_hours, hourly_hours_category, part_time_indicator, temporary_contract_indicator, self_employed_flag, tenure_months, multiple_jobs_flag, gig_worker_flag, telework_indicator, agency_worker_flag.
variables.narr: Relevant variables: fields explicitly capturing type of employment contract/arrangement (permanent vs. temporary; full- vs. part-time; self-employed vs. employee), working hours and schedule, source of contract (agency/platform), number of jobs, and measures of contract precarity (duration, notice period). Prefer variables with standardized coding (ILO/EU definitions) or clear codebooks. Exclude variables that only indicate employer legal form or occupational classification without any contract/arrangement information.

instruments_tools.desc: Questionnaire modules, coding manuals and classification schemes used to collect and code employment form data: employment status modules, contract-type questions, working hours modules, ILO and EU-LFS question sets, labor market coding manuals and job exposure matrices for precariousness.
instruments_tools.narr: Relevant instruments: standard labor force survey question batteries (ILO/EU-LFS style), national microcensus employment modules, panel survey employment modules (SOEP/GSOEP employment history), employer-employee survey modules on contract characteristics, and coding schemes for temporary vs. permanent contracts. Include documentation on harmonization protocols and translation notes. Exclude instruments that only measure firm-level characteristics unrelated to individual contract or that lack items on contract/arrangement type.

publication.desc: German-language and bilingual publications on the relationship between leadership (Führung) and trust (Vertrauen) in organizations and groups: theoretical work and empirical studies examining trust in leaders, leader behaviors that foster trust, leader–member exchange, and organizational trust dynamics.
publication.narr: Relevant publications: empirical articles, German-language dissertations, book chapters and reports that explicitly study how leadership affects trust (trust in managers, trust in leadership), or how trust shapes leadership effectiveness; includes studies using German samples or German-language measures. Include cross-cultural comparisons where leadership and trust constructs are central. Exclude works where 'Führung' refers to guided tours, instructions, or generic steering unrelated to leadership in social/organizational contexts, or publications that mention trust only tangentially.

research_data.desc: Datasets and study materials measuring leadership constructs and trust outcomes in workplaces, teams or organizations, preferably containing scales for trust in supervisor/management and leadership style/behavior variables.
research_data.narr: Relevant data: employee surveys, establishment surveys and linked employer–employee datasets with modules on perceived leadership behaviors, leader–member exchange (LMX), and trust in supervisors/management; experimental or longitudinal datasets examining trust-building interventions or changes in leadership. Include German-language datasets or datasets with validated German translations of trust and leadership scales. Exclude datasets that only measure generalized social trust without workplace/leader referent or those that use 'Führung' only in non-leadership contexts.

variables.desc: Variables that capture leader-related trust and related constructs: trust_in_leader, trust_in_management, perceived_leader_integrity, perceived_leader_competence, leader_member_exchange_score (LMX), organizational_trust, interpersonal_trust_at_work.
variables.narr: Relevant variables: items or composite scores that explicitly reference trust toward supervisors/management or measure dimensions of trust (affective vs. cognitive), perceived leader fairness/honesty/competence, LMX indices, and measures of team-level trust. Prefer variables with validated German translations. Exclude generic societal trust variables that lack explicit workplace or leader referents unless used as contextual comparison.

instruments_tools.desc: Validated scales and survey modules in German or with German translations used to measure leadership and trust: Mayer and Davis trust scales, McAllister affective/cognitive trust scale, LMX-7, scales for trust in management and leader integrity, and leadership questionnaires (e.g., MLQ) that include trust-related subscales.
instruments_tools.narr: Relevant instruments: instruments that explicitly assess trust in leaders or trust-relevant leader behaviors (Mayer and Davis, McAllister, LMX measures), German-language adaptations and manuals, leadership questionnaires (MLQ, authentic leadership scales) when linked to trust outcomes, and coding documentation for aggregated trust measures. Exclude instruments that measure only general social trust without leader referent or tools that assess unrelated concepts (e.g., tourist guiding surveys).

publication.desc: Publications on leadership (Führung) in organizations, teams and political or social movements: theories of leadership, leadership styles (transformational, transactional, servant, authoritarian), leadership effectiveness, leadership development, and cross-cultural leadership studies. Includes German-language and international literature.
publication.narr: Relevant publications: empirical studies, theoretical papers, reviews and practitioner reports that focus on leadership concepts, measurement, antecedents and outcomes at individual, team and organizational levels. Include work on leader traits, behaviors, situational leadership, leadership development programs and leadership assessment. Exclude uses of 'Führung' that refer to tours/guided visits, simple instructions, or non-social leadership contexts (e.g., device controls) that are unrelated to social influence or managerial roles.

research_data.desc: Datasets containing measures of leadership behavior, style, effectiveness, leader-member relations, and leadership development interventions: surveys, 360-degree feedback datasets, organizational case studies and experimental datasets.
research_data.narr: Relevant data: employee surveys with leadership modules, 360-degree assessment datasets, leadership training evaluation data, longitudinal organizational studies that track leadership and outcomes, and cross-national datasets with leadership items. Include datasets with German-language instruments. Exclude datasets that use 'Führung' in non-leadership senses (e.g., product manuals) or datasets lacking explicit leadership measures.

variables.desc: Variables operationalizing leadership: leadership_style, transformational_leadership_score, transactional_leadership_score, authoritarian_leadership_flag, leader_effectiveness_rating, leadership_self_efficacy, LMX_score, leadership_experience_years.
variables.narr: Relevant variables: measures that capture leaders' behaviors, styles and effectiveness (self, subordinate or peer ratings), leader characteristics (tenure, role), and follower outcomes attributed to leadership. Prefer validated composite scores (e.g., MLQ subscales, LMX). Exclude variables that vaguely reference managerial position without any measure of leadership behavior or influence.

instruments_tools.desc: Measurement instruments and assessment tools for leadership: Multifactor Leadership Questionnaire (MLQ), Leader–Member Exchange (LMX) scales, Leadership Practices Inventory (LPI), 360-degree feedback instruments, situational judgment tests and leadership competency frameworks, including German translations/adaptations.
instruments_tools.narr: Relevant instruments: validated leadership questionnaires (MLQ, LPI, LMX-7), 360-degree feedback protocols, leadership development program evaluation tools, coding manuals and translation/adaptation documentation. Include psychometric properties and administration guidelines. Exclude instruments that do not measure leadership constructs or that are intended for unrelated tasks (e.g., tourist guide evaluations).

publication.desc: Publications about gender roles and gender-role attitudes: theoretical and empirical studies on beliefs about appropriate behaviors, responsibilities and identities for genders; research on role socialization, division of labor, family roles, occupational gender norms and changes over time.
publication.narr: Relevant publications: papers, books and reports that measure, analyze or theorize gender role attitudes/identities (e.g., traditional vs. egalitarian role beliefs), their determinants and consequences. Include cross-national comparisons, longitudinal trend analyses and research using attitude scales. Exclude studies solely about biological sex differences without reference to socially prescribed roles, or uses of 'role' in contexts unrelated to gender norms.

research_data.desc: Datasets that include measures of gender-role attitudes or behaviors: national social surveys and modules (e.g., ISSP Family and Changing Gender Roles, European Social Survey, World Values Survey), household surveys with division-of-labor items, and panel studies tracking role attitudes over time.
research_data.narr: Relevant data: survey modules with items on beliefs about gendered responsibilities (work vs. family), attitudes toward women working, childcare and housework allocation, and measures of gender-role identity (BSRI, role salience). Include datasets that allow analysis by cohort, education and employment. Exclude datasets that only record biological sex without measures of role attitudes or behavior.

variables.desc: Variables representing gender-role attitudes and role behavior: gender_role_attitudes, traditional_gender_role_index, egalitarianism_score, attitudes_toward_women_working, childcare_responsibility_belief, division_of_household_labor, bem_sex_role_inventory_scores.
variables.narr: Relevant variables: items or scale scores that explicitly measure normative beliefs about gendered responsibilities (housework, childcare, breadwinner role), self-reported role behaviors, and identity-based role measures. Prefer validated scales (AWS, BSRI) and harmonized items across waves. Exclude variables that only indicate respondent sex/gender with no attitudinal or behavioral content.

instruments_tools.desc: Validated questionnaires and modules for measuring gender roles and attitudes: Attitudes Toward Women Scale (AWS), Bem Sex Role Inventory (BSRI), Gender Role Ideology scales, ISSP/ESS/WVS gender-role modules and coding guides.
instruments_tools.narr: Relevant instruments: survey modules and psychometric scales that assess gender-role beliefs and identities, their German-language adaptations, and codebooks with item wording and coding schemes. Include documentation on scoring, reliability and translations. Exclude instruments unrelated to gender norms (e.g., generic role-identity tools without gender focus).

publication.desc: Publications addressing gender as a social and identity category: studies of gender identity, gender expression, gendered inequalities (labor market, health, politics), gender theory, and intersectional analyses of gender with class, race, sexuality and age.
publication.narr: Relevant publications: empirical and theoretical works that explicitly engage with 'gender' as distinct from biological sex, including research on gender identity, norms, discrimination, policy impacts, and measurement issues. Include studies using gender-disaggregated data or gender-focused qualitative research. Exclude papers that use 'gender' interchangeably with 'sex' without conceptual clarity, or works that do not treat gender as an analytical focus.

research_data.desc: Datasets containing gender-related variables: surveys with sex and gender identity items, administrative records with gender markers, studies on gender-based outcomes (employment, health, violence), and datasets incorporating non-binary and transgender measures.
research_data.narr: Relevant data: microdata that record gender identity/expression (including two-step measures: sex at birth and current gender), datasets on gender-based violence, labor-market datasets with gender-disaggregated indicators, and qualitative datasets on gender experience. Include data with non-binary categories or explicit gender modules. Exclude datasets that only capture sex at birth without any conceptualization of gender when the research question concerns gender as identity or social role.

variables.desc: Variables capturing gender constructs: gender_identity, sex_at_birth, current_gender, gender_expression, gender_nonconformity_flag, gender_role_attitudes, reported_discrimination_due_to_gender, gender_binary_flag.
variables.narr: Relevant variables: explicit measures of gender identity (including non-binary/transgender options), variables distinguishing sex and gender, measures of gender norms and experiences (discrimination, roles), and harmonized codes for analysis. Prefer clearly documented coding and, for identity measures, inclusion of open/other categories. Exclude variables that only indicate biological sex when the intended concept is social gender identity or norms.

instruments_tools.desc: Survey modules, questionnaires and coding guides for measuring gender and related constructs: two-step gender identity items, Gender Identity/Gender Minority measures, gender norms modules (ESS, ISSP items), and documentation for coding sex/gender in administrative data.
instruments_tools.narr: Relevant instruments: validated items and best-practice question wording (two-step method: sex assigned at birth + current gender), scales measuring gender norms and expression, and coding manuals addressing non-binary and transgender categories. Include guidelines on ethical collection of gender data and translation notes for different languages. Exclude instruments that conflate sex and gender without clear items or lack documentation on response options and coding.

publication.desc: Scholarly publications addressing the study of gender as a social, cultural, political and historical category, including feminist theory, masculinity studies, queer studies and intersectional analyses.
publication.narr: Include: peer‑reviewed articles, books, book chapters, review articles and conference papers that explicitly focus on gender (social constructions of sex, gender identities, gender inequality, gender policy, intersectionality). Relevant geographic or historical case studies are in scope. Exclude: purely biomedical or genetic studies of biological sex differences that do not treat gender as a social construct; popular media pieces, opinion blogs, and non‑scholarly content unless published in an academic venue.

research_data.desc: Datasets and study collections that contain measures related to gender attitudes, gender identity, gendered behaviours, gender inequality indicators, or qualitative interview/ethnographic data about gender.
research_data.narr: Include: survey microdata, panel data, census variables with gender breakdowns, datasets of interviews, focus groups or ethnographies on gender, data on gender‑based violence, gender pay gap microdata, and indicator datasets (e.g., gender equality indices). Exclude: datasets that only record biological measures (e.g., hormone levels) without social/gender variables; administrative data with only binary sex codes and no contextual gender variables unless reinterpreted by authors as gendered outcomes.

variables.desc: Variables capturing gender identity, gender roles and norms, attitudes toward gender equality, gendered behaviours, and intersectional attributes linked to gender.
variables.narr: Include: variables named gender, sex assigned at birth, gender identity, gender expression, masculinity/femininity scores, gender role attitudes, division of household labour, childcare responsibility, experiences of discrimination by gender, intersectional identifiers (race, class, sexuality) that interact with gender. Exclude: physiological or clinical biomarkers used solely for biological sex classification where no social/gender interpretation is provided.

instruments_tools.desc: Validated scales, survey modules, interview guides and coding schemes used to measure gender attitudes, roles, identities and related constructs.
instruments_tools.narr: Include: instruments such as Bem Sex Role Inventory, Gender Role Attitudes scales, gender ideology items, interview/observation guides for gender studies, coding schemes for qualitative gender analysis, and standardized modules (e.g., ISSP/ESS gender modules). Exclude: clinical diagnostic tools unrelated to social gender (e.g., endocrine assays), or tools focused solely on biological sex measurement without social/gender components.

publication.desc: Academic literature on the concept of general self‑efficacy: theoretical foundations, psychometric evaluations, applications and correlational/causal studies across populations.
publication.narr: Include: empirical studies, theoretical articles, literature reviews and meta‑analyses that explicitly discuss general self‑efficacy as a construct (e.g., Schwarzer and Jerusalem), its measurement, validity, cross‑cultural adaptations and links to outcomes (health, education, work). Exclude: studies that only address domain‑specific self‑efficacy (e.g., academic, sporting) unless they also include or compare a general self‑efficacy measure.

research_data.desc: Datasets that contain measures of general self‑efficacy (total scores or item‑level data), including longitudinal and cross‑sectional studies where general self‑efficacy is a variable.
research_data.narr: Include: survey datasets, cohort studies and experiments that include the General Self‑Efficacy Scale (GSE) or equivalent general self‑efficacy measures, with documentation of items and scoring. Exclude: datasets containing only domain‑specific self‑efficacy measures without a general/self‑efficacy instrument.

variables.desc: Variables representing general self‑efficacy, usually operationalized as scale total scores or subscale scores from validated instruments.
variables.narr: Include: variables labeled general self‑efficacy, GSE_total, self‑efficacy_score, aggregated Likert scale scores from general self‑efficacy instruments, and item‑level variables for psychometric analysis. Exclude: variables that measure only situational or task‑specific self‑efficacy unless accompanied by a general self‑efficacy measure.

instruments_tools.desc: Measurement instruments and manuals for assessing general self‑efficacy, their translations, scoring rules and validation studies.
instruments_tools.narr: Include: General Self‑Efficacy Scale (Schwarzer and Jerusalem) and its validated language versions, psychometric papers, item lists, scoring instructions, administration guidelines, and short/long form variants. Exclude: instruments that measure only domain‑specific self‑efficacy (e.g., Academic Self‑Efficacy Scale) unless they include a general self‑efficacy component.

publication.desc: Research publications about Generation Y (Millennials): demographic, social, occupational, cultural and attitudinal studies that identify or analyze this birth cohort.
publication.narr: Include: empirical and theoretical works that explicitly focus on or identify Generation Y / Millennials (commonly born roughly 1980s–mid/late 1990s), covering topics such as labour market behavior, political attitudes, family formation, consumption, technology use and cohort comparisons. Exclude: generic youth studies without cohort specification and studies using different cohort labels unless they clearly overlap and map to Generation Y by birth years.

research_data.desc: Datasets that allow analysis of Generation Y, either by explicit cohort identifiers or by birth year ranges enabling cohort selection.
research_data.narr: Include: survey and panel data with respondent birth year or age so Generation Y can be selected, longitudinal cohorts covering Millennials, and administrative datasets where cohort membership can be inferred. Exclude: datasets lacking age or birth year information or those where cohort analysis is impossible.

variables.desc: Variables enabling identification or characterization of Generation Y and their characteristics: birth year, age, cohort indicators and common outcomes studied for this group.
variables.narr: Include: birth_year, age_at_survey, generation_label (e.g., 'Millennial', 'Generation Y'), employment status, educational attainment, family formation markers, technology usage, political attitudes and other variables frequently analyzed by cohort. Exclude: variables that cannot be linked to respondent age or birth cohort.

instruments_tools.desc: Survey modules, questionnaires and analytic tools designed or commonly used to study generational cohorts, and methods for cohort assignment and age‑period‑cohort analysis.
instruments_tools.narr: Include: questionnaires with items on values, technology use, work preferences tailored to Millennials, codebooks that flag generational cohorts, and statistical tools/methods for cohort comparison (APC models). Exclude: tools unrelated to cohort identification or analyses that do not support cohort stratification.

publication.desc: German and international publications on general self‑efficacy (generelle Selbstwirksamkeit), covering theory, measurement, validation and applied research.
publication.narr: Include: German‑language and translated studies that explicitly treat 'generelle Selbstwirksamkeit' or the General Self‑Efficacy construct (e.g., Schwarzer and Jerusalem German version), psychometric evaluations, and applied research linking it to outcomes. Exclude: publications dealing only with context‑specific Selbstwirksamkeit (e.g., schulische Selbstwirksamkeit) unless they also address the general construct.

research_data.desc: Datasets containing measures labeled generelle Selbstwirksamkeit or the German version of the General Self‑Efficacy Scale, including item‑level data and scale scores.
research_data.narr: Include: German surveys, cohort studies, or international datasets with German subsamples that include the Allgemeine Selbstwirksamkeit/GSE items; documentation of translations and reliability statistics. Exclude: datasets with only domain‑specific self‑efficacy items and no general self‑efficacy measure.

variables.desc: Variables measuring general self‑efficacy in German datasets: scale totals, item responses, and variable labels such as 'generelle_Selbstwirksamkeit' or 'SWE'.
variables.narr: Include: variables for Gesamtscore der Allgemeinen Selbstwirksamkeit, individual item variables (Likert responses), and related constructs (self‑confidence, coping expectations) when linked to the general self‑efficacy concept. Exclude: variables referring solely to situational Selbstwirksamkeit without a general measure.

instruments_tools.desc: German instruments and translations for measuring general self‑efficacy, manuals, item lists and validation studies (e.g., Suche for 'Allgemeine Selbstwirksamkeitserwartung').
instruments_tools.narr: Include: German version of the General Self‑Efficacy Scale (Schwarzer and Jerusalem), translation/adaptation documentation, scoring instructions, normative data for German populations, and psychometric studies. Exclude: instruments that only measure domain‑specific Selbstwirksamkeit and lack a general component.

publication.desc: Scholarly works on sex/gender and gender roles (geschlecht und Geschlechterrollen), including studies of role expectations, socialization, division of labour and normative gender behaviour.
publication.narr: Include: empirical and theoretical literature on gender roles, role socialization, attitudes toward gendered divisions of work, masculinity/femininity constructs, and policy studies addressing role norms. Both German and international publications are relevant where they explicitly address gender roles. Exclude: studies focused solely on biological sex without addressing roles or norms.

research_data.desc: Datasets containing measures of gender role attitudes, household division of labour, occupational segregation, socialization practices and related qualitative data on gender roles.
research_data.narr: Include: survey modules (e.g., ISSP family/gender modules, ESS items) with gender role attitude items, time‑use data showing division of labour, interview/ethnographic datasets on role socialization, and administrative data on occupational gender segregation. Exclude: datasets that only record respondent sex without any measures of roles, attitudes or behaviour.

variables.desc: Variables that operationalize gender roles and related attitudes/behaviours: role attitude scales, time use in domestic tasks, occupational sector by gender, and masculinity/femininity measures.
variables.narr: Include: variables such as gender_role_attitude, household_task_hours, childcare_responsibility, Bem masculinity/femininity scores, attitudes toward women's employment, and indicators of occupational gender composition. Exclude: simple sex or gender identifiers without accompanying role or attitude measures.

instruments_tools.desc: Validated scales, survey questions, interview guides and coding manuals used to measure gender roles, role attitudes and gendered behaviour.
instruments_tools.narr: Include: instruments like the Bem Sex Role Inventory, Attitudes Toward Women Scale, Gender Role Attitudes items found in ISSP/ESS, time‑use survey instruments, qualitative interview guides on gender socialization, and coding schemes for role content analysis. Exclude: biological measurement tools and instruments not addressing social role constructs.

publication.desc: Publications that address gender roles and the social expectations, behaviors and responsibilities associated with gender. Includes empirical articles, theoretical papers, books and reports on gender role attitudes, socialization, division of labor, family roles, workplace roles and intersections with health, education, and policy.
publication.narr: Include publications in German or other languages that explicitly study 'gender role' (singular) as a social construct: empirical studies measuring role endorsement, theoretical treatments of role concepts, historical or comparative analyses of gender role formation, and applied research linking gender role expectations to outcomes (health, employment, family life, identity). Include qualitative and quantitative work as well as policy reports. Exclude works that use the word 'role' in non-gender contexts (e.g. job role descriptions without reference to gender), purely biological sex-differences research that does not address social roles, and materials where 'role' appears only tangentially.

research_data.desc: Datasets that capture gender role attitudes, behaviors, and role-related practices. Examples: social surveys, time-use studies, cohort studies with role-related modules, cross-national modules on family and gender attitudes.
research_data.narr: Include datasets containing measures of gender role attitudes or behaviors (e.g. survey items on who should do childcare/housework, occupational role expectations, caregiving roles), time-use data showing division of labor, cohort studies with socialization or role items, and cross-national modules (e.g. ISSP, ESS modules) that permit analysis of gender-role constructs. Exclude datasets that only record biological sex without any measures of roles, datasets about organizational job roles unrelated to gender, or animal/biological datasets.

variables.desc: Variables that operationalize gender role concepts: attitudinal items, behavioral indicators, role allocations, and demographic covariates.
variables.narr: Include variables measuring gender role attitudes (agreement with statements about expected male/female behaviors), self-reported division of household labor and care, occupational role and employment status by gender, role conflict/role strain scales, measures of gender identity related to roles, and relevant demographics (sex, age, education, marital status). Exclude variables that only record sex/gender without any role-related content, and variables unrelated to social roles (e.g. purely biological measures).

instruments_tools.desc: Validated scales and survey modules used to assess gender roles, plus coding schemes and questionnaires relevant to role attitudes and behaviors.
instruments_tools.narr: Include instruments such as the Bem Sex Role Inventory (BSRI), Attitudes Toward Women Scale, Gender Role Attitudes items in ISSP/ESS, role conflict/strain scales, time-use instruments that allow computing division of labor, and translations/adaptations of these tools in German. Also include coding guides and questionnaire modules used in large surveys to capture gender-role data. Exclude clinical instruments unrelated to social role measurement and generic organizational job-role tools that do not address gender.

publication.desc: Publications on gender roles (plural), including research on stereotypes, normative expectations, role changes over time, cross-cultural comparisons, and the effects of gender roles on social outcomes.
publication.narr: Include empirical studies, reviews, comparative and historical analyses, policy papers and qualitative research that explicitly investigate 'gender roles' as social norms, stereotypes, or patterns of behavior across contexts (family, work, education). Include cross-national comparisons and trend analyses of changing gender roles. Exclude publications that use the term in passing without substantive analysis, studies focused solely on biological sex differences without social role discussion, and irrelevant disciplinary uses of 'roles' (e.g. system roles in IT).

research_data.desc: Datasets enabling analysis of gender-role norms and their distribution: repeated surveys, cross-national modules, longitudinal cohorts, and qualitative collections about role expectations.
research_data.narr: Include datasets with items on gender-role stereotypes, who-does-what behavioral measures, attitudes toward traditional vs. egalitarian roles, and longitudinal data tracking role change. Relevant sources include ISSP modules on family/gender, ESS items, national attitude surveys, time-use surveys, and qualitative interview corpora on gender norms. Exclude datasets that lack role-related content or only record biological sex.

variables.desc: Variables reflecting collective and individual-level gender role norms: stereotype endorsement, expectations for men/women, distribution of household tasks, occupational segregation indicators.
variables.narr: Include variables such as agreement with stereotypical statements, reported primary caregiver/household responsibilities, indicators of occupational concentration by gender, measures of normative pressure, and community- or country-level aggregates of role attitudes. Exclude isolated biological health markers or administrative codes that do not inform about roles or norms.

instruments_tools.desc: Survey modules, scales and qualitative protocols used to measure gender-role attitudes and stereotypes, and comparative coding schemes for cross-cultural research.
instruments_tools.narr: Include instruments like ISSP and ESS gender/family modules, Bem Sex Role Inventory and its adaptations, Attitudes Toward Women Scale, stereotype endorsement items, standardized time-use diaries, and interview guides for qualitative studies of gender norms. Exclude instruments that do not pertain to gender norms or role expectations.

publication.desc: Publications covering health in broad sense: public health, epidemiology, health services, clinical studies, health policy, health behavior, and population health analyses.
publication.narr: Include empirical studies, reviews, clinical reports, health policy analyses and books that focus on physical or population health, disease burden, prevention, health promotion, health care delivery and determinants of health. Include studies at individual and population levels, in German and other languages. Exclude non-health uses of 'gesundheit' (colloquial exclamation) and publications in unrelated domains (e.g. veterinary health unless explicitly about human health when relevant).

research_data.desc: Health-related datasets such as health surveys, administrative health records, registries, clinical trial data, population health surveillance and biomarker datasets.
research_data.narr: Include national health surveys (e.g. GEDA, DEGS, SOEP health modules), disease registries, hospital discharge data, mortality records, cohort studies with health measures, and clinical trial datasets. Data should permit analysis of morbidity, mortality, health behaviors, service use, and biomarkers. Exclude datasets that do not contain health-related variables or that pertain only to non-human subjects unless explicitly relevant.

variables.desc: Variables commonly used in health research: morbidity, mortality, diagnoses, self-rated health, health behaviors, biomarkers, utilization and socioeconomic determinants.
variables.narr: Include variables such as ICD/diagnosis codes, self-rated health, chronic condition indicators, prevalence/incidence measures, BMI, blood pressure, smoking/alcohol use, physical activity, health service use (visits, hospitalizations), and socioeconomic covariates. Exclude variables unrelated to health outcomes or determinants.

instruments_tools.desc: Validated health measurement instruments and tools: health surveys, clinical assessment instruments, questionnaires, and coding systems used in health research.
instruments_tools.narr: Include instruments such as SF-36/SF-12, EQ-5D, WHO health surveys, GHQ, standardized clinical assessment protocols, laboratory assay methods, and coding systems like ICD and ATC. Also include population health surveillance tools and measurement guides. Exclude instruments unrelated to health measurement (e.g. purely administrative business tools).

publication.desc: Publications on mental health and psychological wellbeing, including epidemiology of mental disorders, clinical psychiatry, psychotherapy research, public mental health, and studies of stress, wellbeing and mental health services.
publication.narr: Include empirical and review articles, clinical reports, policy analyses and books that address mental health outcomes (depression, anxiety, stress, well-being), mental health services, determinants and interventions, and population-level mental health trends. Include both clinical and community-focused research. Exclude publications that deal solely with neurological disorders without psychiatric/psychological relevance or that mention 'psychisch' only peripherally.

research_data.desc: Datasets focused on mental health: psychiatric registries, population mental health surveys, clinical trial data for mental health treatments, and cohort studies with mental health measures.
research_data.narr: Include datasets containing validated measures of mental disorders or symptoms (diagnoses, symptom scales), service use for mental health, suicide and self-harm registries, and longitudinal cohorts tracking mental health. Examples: national mental health surveys, DRKS/clinical trial datasets for psychiatric interventions, and epidemiological studies with GHQ/PHQ/BDI. Exclude datasets lacking mental health variables or focusing purely on neurological physiology absent psychological measures.

variables.desc: Variables measuring psychiatric diagnoses, symptom severity, psychological well-being, suicidality, treatment and service use, and mental-health-relevant covariates.
variables.narr: Include variables such as ICD/DSM diagnoses, scores on PHQ-9, GAD-7, GHQ-12, BDI, WHO-5, psychiatric hospitalization, medication use for mental disorders, measures of stress and resilience, and functional impairment. Exclude variables that do not concern mental health (e.g. general biomarkers without linkage to mental health).

instruments_tools.desc: Psychometric instruments and clinical tools for assessing mental health: screening questionnaires, diagnostic interviews, standardized clinical scales and service-use measurement instruments.
instruments_tools.narr: Include commonly used validated instruments such as PHQ-9, GAD-7, GHQ-12, BDI, HADS, WHO-5, MINI, SCID, and service-use questionnaires and PROMs for mental health. Also include coding schemes for psychiatric diagnoses (ICD-10/DSM) and assessment protocols used in clinical and epidemiological studies. Exclude tools not validated for mental health assessment or instruments intended solely for neurological testing without psychiatric relevance.

publication.desc: Publications focusing on patient health, patient populations, patient experiences, clinical outcomes, patient safety, and health care delivery for patients.
publication.narr: Include empirical studies, clinical reports, qualitative research and reviews that explicitly study patients: disease-specific patient cohorts, patient-reported outcomes, studies of patient pathways, care quality, satisfaction, adherence, and health outcomes in clinical populations. Exclude publications about general population health without a focus on patients or those that use 'patient' metaphorically.

research_data.desc: Datasets concerning patients: clinical registries, hospital administrative data, electronic health records, patient surveys, and trial participant data.
research_data.narr: Include datasets with patient-level clinical data (diagnoses, treatments, outcomes), registries for specific diseases, hospital discharge datasets, electronic health record extracts, patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs) and satisfaction surveys, and randomized controlled trial data with patient participants. Exclude population surveys that do not identify patient status, and datasets that only cover healthy volunteers without patient groups.

variables.desc: Variables pertaining to patient status, clinical diagnoses, treatment modalities, outcomes, service use, and patient-reported measures.
variables.narr: Include variables like diagnosis codes, treatment type, medication, length of stay, readmission, mortality, clinical outcome measures, PROMs, patient satisfaction, adherence, comorbidities, and socio-demographics of patient groups. Exclude variables unrelated to patient care or outcomes (e.g. organizational finances) and variables from non-patient samples.

instruments_tools.desc: Instruments and tools for assessing patient health and experience: clinical outcome measures, PROMs, satisfaction surveys, clinical assessment protocols and registries.
instruments_tools.narr: Include tools such as PROMIS, EQ-5D, SF-36, disease-specific outcome scales, patient satisfaction instruments (e.g. HCAHPS where applicable), clinical case report forms, standardized follow-up protocols, and registries used to monitor patient outcomes. Exclude instruments not intended for patient assessment or administrative tools unrelated to patient health.

publication.desc: Publications on workplace-based health, occupational health management, and company-level health promotion and prevention measures.
publication.narr: Relevant publications address health promotion, occupational safety and health (OSH) programs, workplace health policies, company-level interventions, organizational determinants of employee health, return-to-work programs, occupational health services, and evaluations of health promotion at the enterprise level. Include empirical studies, reviews, program descriptions, policy analyses, and economic evaluations focused on businesses, firms, factories, schools or other workplaces. Exclude publications limited to individual clinical care outside the workplace, general population health without connection to workplaces, purely clinical disease biology unrelated to occupational context, or publications solely about health care institutions unless framed as workplace health for staff.

research_data.desc: Datasets and research data on company- or workplace-level health indicators, intervention trials in enterprises, and organizational surveys of health management.
research_data.narr: Include datasets from workplace health promotion trials, company-level surveys of health policies and OSH practices, administrative records on workplace sickness absence, worksite exposure assessments, aggregated firm-level health outcome data, and longitudinal employer cohorts. Data must be linked to workplace context (e.g., firm, department, occupational group) or evaluate interventions implemented at the company level. Exclude population-level health surveys without workplace identifiers, clinical patient registries not capturing workplace variables, or datasets only about health care utilization outside employment context.

variables.desc: Variables measuring workplace health management, organizational exposures, and aggregated employee health outcomes.
variables.narr: Relevant variables include company-level indicators (presence of health promotion programs, occupational safety policies, number of occupational health staff), aggregated sickness absence rates, work-related injury rates, workplace exposure metrics (noise, chemicals, ergonomics), measures of psychosocial work environment at organizational level (e.g., job demands, control, support), and indicators of program implementation and reach. Exclude variables that measure only individual clinical biomarkers unrelated to work context or demographic-only variables without workplace linkage.

instruments_tools.desc: Instruments and tools used for assessing and implementing workplace health programs, organizational risk assessments, and OSH management systems.
instruments_tools.narr: Include validated questionnaires and checklists for workplace health promotion and occupational safety (e.g., workplace health climate scales, organizational-level psychosocial risk assessment tools), implementation toolkits for enterprises, intervention manuals, company-level audit instruments, and employer survey instruments. Exclude clinical diagnostic instruments used only in medical settings, instruments solely measuring general population health unrelated to workplace, or tools designed exclusively for patient care.

publication.desc: Literature on health within the workplace: employee health status, working conditions, and in-company health interventions.
publication.narr: Include research on how work environment, organizational practices, and occupational exposures affect health of employees; studies evaluating workplace interventions (ergonomics, mental health programs, workplace wellness); surveillance reports of work-related illnesses and injuries; and qualitative work on employee perceptions of health at work. Exclude literature that discusses health in non-workplace contexts only, primary clinical research without workplace linkage, or studies of health systems not addressing workplace staff or conditions.

research_data.desc: Research datasets documenting health outcomes and exposures measured within workplaces or among employed persons.
research_data.narr: Relevant data include occupational cohort studies, company-level health surveillance data, surveys of working conditions and self-reported health, exposure measurement data gathered on-site, records of work-related incidents, and evaluation datasets of workplace interventions. Datasets should explicitly link health measures to workplace setting or employment status. Exclude datasets limited to non-working populations, general health surveys lacking work-related variables, or clinical trials unrelated to workplace implementation.

variables.desc: Variables capturing individual and contextual measures of health and working conditions within the workplace.
variables.narr: Include individual health outcomes among employees (self-rated health, musculoskeletal complaints, mental health symptoms, sickness absence), workplace exposure variables (physical, chemical, ergonomic, psychosocial), job characteristics (occupation, shift work, working hours), and organizational factors (management practices, safety climate). Exclude variables that do not connect health measures to employment or workplace context.

instruments_tools.desc: Assessment instruments and implementation tools for measuring and improving health in workplace settings.
instruments_tools.narr: Include validated employee health questionnaires (e.g., job-content questionnaires, effort–reward imbalance scales, workplace stress inventories), ergonomic assessment tools, workplace risk assessment protocols, intervention toolkits used in companies, and monitoring instruments for occupational exposures. Exclude instruments intended only for clinical diagnosis outside occupational assessment or tools not applicable to workplace settings.

publication.desc: Studies and reports on the health of employees and other employed persons across occupations and sectors.
publication.narr: Include empirical research, reviews, surveillance reports, and policy analyses that focus on the physical, mental, and social health of workers. Topics include prevalence and determinants of work-related diseases, mental health among employees, absenteeism and presenteeism, occupational morbidity and mortality, and subgroup analyses by occupation, industry, gender, age. Exclude research on non-employed populations, clinical studies not addressing employment-related factors, or studies about employers' finances without health focus.

research_data.desc: Individual-level datasets on the health status, health behaviors, and work-related exposures of employed persons.
research_data.narr: Include worker cohorts, cross-sectional and longitudinal surveys of employed populations, administrative employment-health linkage data, sick-leave registries, occupational disease registries, and biomonitoring data for employed groups. Data should permit analysis of health outcomes among workers. Exclude datasets that do not distinguish employed from non-employed participants or that lack employment-related variables.

variables.desc: Individual health indicators and employment-related variables relevant to the health of workers.
variables.narr: Relevant variables encompass self-rated health, diagnosed conditions, mental health scales (depression, anxiety), musculoskeletal complaints, frequency and duration of sickness absence, presenteeism measures, workplace exposures, job characteristics, occupational class, and health behaviors among employees. Exclude variables that solely measure organizational attributes without linking to employee health outcomes.

instruments_tools.desc: Survey instruments, clinical measures, and occupational assessment tools used to measure employee health and work-related exposures.
instruments_tools.narr: Include validated health questionnaires for working populations (e.g., GHQ, SF-12/36, WHO-5), scales for work stress and psychosocial risks, instruments for measuring absenteeism/presenteeism, occupational exposure measurement tools, and protocols for workplace health examinations. Exclude instruments intended for general population screening when not validated for employed subgroups, or tools unrelated to occupational health assessment.

publication.desc: Publications on health complaints and symptom reports, including somatic and psychosomatic symptoms in working populations.
publication.narr: Include studies documenting prevalence, determinants, and consequences of self-reported health complaints (e.g., pain, fatigue, headaches, gastrointestinal symptoms, sleep problems), work-related symptom clusters, and clinical or survey-based assessments of symptom burden. Include research on reporting patterns, occupational antecedents of complaints, and intervention studies reducing symptom prevalence. Exclude purely diagnostic clinical case reports without relevance to population-level complaints, studies of laboratory biomarkers without symptom correlation, or publications focused only on major disease diagnoses unless symptoms are central.

research_data.desc: Datasets containing symptom and complaint measures, health complaint inventories, and survey data on symptom prevalence.
research_data.narr: Include cross-sectional and longitudinal survey data with symptom checklists, occupational health records recording complaints, symptom diary datasets, psychosomatic symptom inventories, and datasets linking complaints to exposures or outcomes (e.g., absence). Data should allow analysis of prevalence, severity, and correlates of health complaints. Exclude datasets lacking direct symptom measures or those limited to clinical diagnostic tests without symptom information.

variables.desc: Variables that capture self-reported symptoms, somatic complaints, and psychosomatic indicators.
variables.narr: Include variables for frequency, severity, and duration of specific complaints (musculoskeletal pain, headaches, fatigue, sleep disturbances, gastrointestinal complaints), composite symptom scores, psychosomatic symptom scales, and health-related quality-of-life items tied to complaints. Include variables that record timing and work-related attribution of complaints. Exclude laboratory-only biomarkers that do not reflect patient-reported symptoms.

instruments_tools.desc: Questionnaires and measurement tools for assessing health complaints and symptom burden.
instruments_tools.narr: Include validated symptom checklists and inventories (e.g., SCL-90 somatisation items, somatic symptom scales, standardized pain questionnaires), daily symptom diaries, sleep disturbance instruments, and occupational symptom assessment tools. Also include protocols for clinical evaluation of symptom complaints in occupational health. Exclude purely laboratory instruments that do not measure subjective complaints.

publication.desc: Publications on violence in its various forms: interpersonal, domestic, workplace, sexual, political, and community violence.
publication.narr: Include empirical studies, reviews, policy analyses, and program evaluations addressing causes, prevalence, risk factors, consequences, prevention, and intervention related to physical, sexual, psychological, and structural violence.
