Cover settings such as homes, schools, workplaces, public spaces, conflict zones, and institutions. Include studies on self-reported victimization, perpetration, bystander behavior, and service responses. Exclude literature solely on criminal procedure without health/social outcomes, animal violence not framed in human social research, or purely theoretical treatments with no empirical or applied focus unless they inform measurement or intervention.

research_data.desc: Datasets on experiences and perpetration of violence, crime statistics, victimization surveys, and program evaluation data.
research_data.narr: Include national and local victimization surveys, longitudinal cohorts with violence exposure data, administrative records (police, social services, healthcare) related to violent incidents, conflict and war-related datasets, and evaluation datasets of violence prevention programs. Data should measure types of violence, timing, perpetrators, settings, and outcomes. Exclude datasets without explicit measures of violence, or those limited to animal or purely economic crime measures without human violence context.

variables.desc: Variables measuring types, frequency, severity, timing, context, and consequences of violent acts and exposures.
variables.narr: Relevant variables include indicators of physical assault, sexual violence, intimate partner violence, child abuse, workplace violence, bullying, hate-motivated incidents, exposure to political/collective violence, PTSD and other health sequelae, injuries resulting from violence, perpetrator relationship, and reporting and service utilization. Include variables on protective factors and prevention exposure. Exclude variables unrelated to violent behavior or exposure.

instruments_tools.desc: Measurement instruments and tools for assessing violence exposure, perpetration, and response, and for implementing prevention/intervention programs.
instruments_tools.narr: Include validated survey instruments and screening tools (e.g., Conflict Tactics Scale, WHO Violence Against Women instrument, juvenile delinquency/violence scales), incident reporting protocols, risk assessment tools, observational coding schemes for violent events, and program manuals for prevention/intervention (e.g., bystander training, domestic violence interventions). Exclude forensic lab methods unrelated to social measurement, instruments only for animal behavior, or tools that do not capture human-directed violence.

publication.desc: Publications addressing violence involving children and adolescents (victimization, perpetration, exposure) across contexts such as family, school, peers, community, and online.
publication.narr: Include empirical articles, reviews, policy reports and book chapters that focus on physical, sexual, psychological, or relational violence where at least one party is a child or adolescent (typically ages ~0–19). Relevant topics: youth perpetration, youth victimization, exposure to domestic or community violence, bullying/cyberbullying, dating violence among adolescents, and prevention/intervention programs targeted at young people. Include studies from criminology, psychology, public health, education and social work. Exclude works that primarily address adult-only samples, large-scale armed conflict or terrorism when youth are not the primary focus, non-violent delinquency without a violence component, and purely theoretical pieces with no empirical or applied focus on youth.

research_data.desc: Datasets and surveys that measure violence affecting children and adolescents, including victimization surveys, school-based studies, child protection records, and cohort studies with violence-related variables.
research_data.narr: Include cross-sectional and longitudinal datasets capturing child/adolescent experiences of physical, sexual, emotional abuse, neglect, bullying, dating violence, exposure to domestic or community violence, or perpetration. Relevant sources: school surveys, child protection and CPS administrative data, cohort studies that include violence modules, and criminological victimization surveys disaggregated by age. Data should allow identification of age groups and contexts of violence. Exclude datasets that only cover adult violence without age breakdown, animal violence datasets, or datasets focused solely on macro-level conflict metrics unless they include youth-specific measures.

variables.desc: Variables that measure youth-directed or youth-perpetrated violence and related outcomes (victimization, perpetration, frequency, severity, context, and correlates).
variables.narr: Include variables such as self-reported victimization (physical, sexual, emotional), bullying victim/perpetrator indicators, dating violence measures, exposure to domestic violence, number of incidents, severity indicators, location/context of incidents (school, home, online), perpetrator relationship, help-seeking, reporting to authorities, protective factors (e.g., parent supervision), and mental/behavioral health outcomes linked to violence. Exclude variables that are generic criminal counts without age attribution or that measure only non-violent behaviors (unless explicitly linked to violent acts).

instruments_tools.desc: Validated instruments and screening tools used to assess violence involving youth, prevention program measures, and standardized questionnaires for child/adolescent violence.
instruments_tools.narr: Include instruments such as the Juvenile Victimization Questionnaire (JVQ), Conflict Tactics Scales (CTS) adapted for adolescents, Olweus Bullying Questionnaire, Cyberbullying scales, Childhood Trauma Questionnaire (CTQ) for retrospective adolescent reports, school-based victimization modules, and standardized screening tools used by child protection services. Also include evaluation tools for youth violence prevention programs. Exclude adult-only violence instruments without youth validation and generic crime-record extraction protocols that lack measures specific to children or adolescents.

publication.desc: Publications examining cross-national or global measures and comparisons of life satisfaction and subjective well‑being across populations and countries.
publication.narr: Include empirical studies, comparative analyses, methodological papers, and reports that use or critique global measures of life satisfaction (e.g., Cantril ladder, single-item life satisfaction questions, SWLS) to compare countries, regions or population subgroups. Relevant topics: trends over time, determinants of national life satisfaction, happiness economics, cross-cultural measurement invariance, and policy implications. Exclude studies only focused on narrow clinical populations without broader subjective well‑being context, or purely theoretical discussions that do not engage with cross-national measurement or data.

research_data.desc: Cross-national datasets and surveys containing life satisfaction measures suitable for global comparisons (e.g., World Values Survey, Gallup World Poll, European Social Survey).
research_data.narr: Include large-scale international surveys and datasets that include standardized life satisfaction or subjective well‑being items and allow country-level comparisons or global estimates. Relevant sources: World Values Survey, European Social Survey, Gallup World Poll, OECD Better Life Index data on life satisfaction, ISSP, and Harmonized datasets pooling multiple national surveys. Exclude single-country datasets without cross-national linkage, datasets lacking direct life satisfaction or comparable subjective well‑being items, and opinion polls with poor methodological documentation.

variables.desc: Variables that operationalize life satisfaction and global subjective well‑being, including single-item and multi-item scales and country-level aggregates.
variables.narr: Include variables for global life satisfaction such as Cantril Self-Anchoring Scale (ladder), single-question life satisfaction items (e.g., 'All things considered, how satisfied are you with your life?'), Satisfaction With Life Scale (SWLS) scores, country-level average life satisfaction indicators, and demographic moderators (age, gender, income, education). Also include variables capturing domain satisfactions contributing to life satisfaction (health, income, social support). Exclude variables that measure only momentary affect without evaluative life satisfaction or purely domain-specific outcomes unlinked to overall life evaluation.

instruments_tools.desc: Standard instruments and survey items used to assess life satisfaction and facilitate cross-national comparability.
instruments_tools.narr: Include validated instruments such as the Cantril ladder, the Satisfaction With Life Scale (SWLS), OECD's single life satisfaction item, and standardized questionnaire modules from World Values Survey, ESS, Gallup, and ISSP used for global comparability. Also include translation and harmonization protocols, anchoring vignettes and methods/tools for testing measurement invariance across cultures. Exclude ad hoc or unvalidated single items without comparability information and instruments intended only for clinical diagnostic use unrelated to life evaluation.

publication.desc: Publications on health from a social-science and public-health perspective, including physical and mental health, health behaviors, healthcare access, and health determinants and outcomes.
publication.narr: Include empirical studies, reviews, policy analyses, and public health reports addressing population health, disease burden, health inequalities, health behaviors (smoking, diet, exercise), mental health, healthcare utilization and access, health policy, and social determinants of health. Studies may be cross-sectional, longitudinal or intervention evaluations. Exclude purely molecular, cellular or bench-lab biomedical research that does not engage with population- or social-level health questions, veterinary health, or highly specialized clinical case reports lacking broader public-health relevance.

research_data.desc: Datasets covering health status, health behaviors, healthcare utilization, clinical outcomes, and social determinants collected in surveys, cohorts, administrative registers or health surveillance systems.
research_data.narr: Include national and international health surveys (e.g., health interview surveys, NHIS, DHS, Eurostat health data), longitudinal cohort studies with health measures, hospital/claims administrative datasets, disease registries, and public health surveillance data. Relevant variables include morbidity, mortality, self-rated health, biomarkers, mental health scales, and healthcare access/utilization. Exclude purely genetic sequence repositories without phenotypic health data and datasets solely focused on non-human health.

variables.desc: Health-related variables capturing status, behaviors, outcomes, determinants, and service use (e.g., self-rated health, chronic conditions, BMI, mental health scores, healthcare utilization).
variables.narr: Include self-rated health measures, diagnosed chronic condition indicators, morbidity and mortality measures, biomarkers (e.g., blood pressure, cholesterol) when linked to population data, mental health screening scores (PHQ-9, GHQ), health behaviors (smoking, alcohol, physical activity), BMI, functional limitations, health insurance status, healthcare utilization metrics, and socioeconomic determinants of health. Exclude purely administrative coding subsets without health-relevant fields or variables only about laboratory assays without linkage to population health outcomes.

instruments_tools.desc: Validated instruments and measurement tools commonly used in population health research and public health surveillance.
instruments_tools.narr: Include instruments such as SF-36/SF-12 (health-related quality of life), EQ-5D, PHQ-9, GAD-7, GHQ-12, AUDIT, standardized physical activity and dietary questionnaires, clinical measurement protocols for blood pressure/BMI, and survey modules from WHO STEPS, DHS, and national health interview surveys. Also include coding schemes for ICD diagnoses in administrative data and tools for health inequality measurement. Exclude highly specialized laboratory assay kits or clinical devices not used in population-level measurement.

publication.desc: Publications on working from home / telework / remote work, focusing on effects for employees, organizations, work–life balance, productivity, ergonomics, and policy.
publication.narr: Include empirical studies, literature reviews, case studies and policy analyses that examine home-based work arrangements (telework, remote work, work-from-home), their prevalence, determinants, effects on job performance, well-being, work–family conflict, organizational practices, digitalization, and occupational health/ergonomics. Include research on telework during COVID-19 and comparative analyses across sectors. Exclude publications solely about setting up home office furniture sales/retail, purely technical IT infrastructure guides without social or organizational analysis, or non-work-related home-office aesthetics.

research_data.desc: Datasets and surveys measuring telework prevalence, patterns of working from home, associated outcomes (productivity, well‑being), and employer practices.
research_data.narr: Include labor force and employer surveys with telework modules, time-use surveys that identify home-based work, longitudinal panels tracking shifts to home office (e.g., COVID-era modules), organizational datasets on remote work policies, and ergonomics/occupational health study data for home workers. Relevant variables include telework frequency, hours worked at home, employer support, equipment provided, productivity/self-reported performance, and home working conditions. Exclude datasets about home ownership or household consumption that do not capture work activities, and retail sales datasets for furniture or office equipment unless linked to remote work research.

variables.desc: Variables capturing remote work arrangements and outcomes: telework frequency/intensity, work hours/location, job satisfaction, productivity, work–family conflict, and home workspace characteristics.
variables.narr: Include variables indicating whether respondents work from home, number of days/hours worked at home, employer telework policy, availability of equipment, self-reported productivity, job satisfaction, stress and mental health measures linked to remote work, commuting time saved, work–life balance measures, ergonomic conditions of home workspace, and household composition while teleworking. Exclude variables that only indicate general internet use without relation to work or those that track purely leisure activities at home.

instruments_tools.desc: Survey modules, scales and measurement tools used to assess telework practices, remote work outcomes, and home-office ergonomics.
instruments_tools.narr: Include validated survey items and modules for measuring telework frequency and intensity, remote-work environment checklists, work–family conflict scales (e.g., Carlson et al. work–family conflict scale), remote-work productivity/self-efficacy measures, time-use diary instruments capturing work location, and ergonomic self-assessment checklists for home offices. Also include employer policy templates and evaluation tools for remote work programs. Exclude generic IT configuration guides or product-specific setup manuals unrelated to research measurement.

publication.desc: Publications on immigration and migrants, covering migration flows, integration, policy, socioeconomic outcomes, health, and legal status.
publication.narr: Include empirical studies, reviews, policy analyses and theoretical works that address international migration, immigrant integration and assimilation, labor market outcomes of immigrants, refugee/asylum issues, migration policy and laws, remittances, transnationalism, and migrant health and education. Relevant disciplines: sociology, demography, economics, political science, public health and law. Exclude studies exclusively about internal migration (unless relevant), tourism travel statistics not related to migration, and purely historical migration narratives with no contemporary analytical relevance unless explicitly comparative.

research_data.desc: Datasets and administrative sources capturing migration status, flows, immigrant characteristics, integration indicators, and asylum/refugee records.
research_data.narr: Include population registers, immigration and naturalization administrative data, household and labor force surveys with migrant identifiers (country of birth, citizenship, year of arrival), refugee and asylum seeker databases, longitudinal migrant cohort studies, and datasets on remittances and migrant networks. Data should allow analysis of migration status, origin/destination, length of stay and integration outcomes. Exclude datasets that only report tourist or short-term travel without migration intent, and non-human migration data.

variables.desc: Variables that identify and characterize migrants and migration processes: country of birth, citizenship, migration reason/status, length of residence, legal status, language proficiency, and integration outcomes.
variables.narr: Include variables such as migrant status (immigrant, emigrant, refugee, asylum-seeker), country of birth, citizenship, parental country of birth, year of arrival, length of stay, legal residency status, reason for migration, language skills, education credentials, employment and income, housing, naturalization, social integration indicators, and access to services. Also include remittance behavior and transnational ties when linked to migration. Exclude variables that do not permit identification of migration-related attributes or that only measure temporary travel for tourism.

instruments_tools.desc: Standard instruments, questionnaires and coding schemes used in migration research, and tools for measuring integration and legal status.
instruments_tools.narr: Include survey modules and question batteries for migration (e.g., migrant background question sets used in EU surveys), language proficiency assessments, integration scales (social, economic, civic integration indices), legal-status coding schemes, and tools for harmonizing migration variables across datasets (e.g., harmonization guides for country of birth, citizenship, and year of arrival). Also include translations/translation protocols for migrant surveys and instruments for measuring xenophobia or attitudes toward immigrants. Exclude administrative IT systems unrelated to research use and instruments designed solely for immigration officers' operational use without research documentation.

publication.desc: Publications addressing social, economic, health, educational, gender, racial, and spatial inequalities, including theoretical analyses, empirical studies, reviews, and policy discussions.
publication.narr: Relevant publications examine inequality as a primary topic or present substantial empirical or theoretical treatment of disparities (income, wealth, poverty, labor market, health, education, gender, race/ethnicity, regional/urban-rural). Include comparative, cross-national, longitudinal, and case studies, and works that discuss causes, consequences, measurement, and policy responses. Exclude works where 'inequality' is only mentioned tangentially or used metaphorically without substantive analysis (e.g., brief mentions in unrelated topics), and exclude purely methodological papers with no application to social/economic disparities unless they introduce widely used measures of inequality (e.g., Gini) and discuss interpretation.

research_data.desc: Datasets and data collections containing variables suitable for measuring inequality (income, wealth, consumption, health outcomes, educational attainment, employment), including cross-sectional, panel, survey, administrative, and geo-referenced data.
research_data.narr: Include datasets that enable calculation or analysis of inequality (microdata on earnings, household surveys, labor force surveys, social statistics, health surveys, census microdata, tax records, longitudinal panels). Also include harmonized cross-national datasets and data on distributional outcomes by social group or geography. Exclude datasets unrelated to distributional analysis (e.g., purely biological or lab experimental data with no social disparity measures), and exclude metadata-only records without accessible data or documentation that allows inequality analysis.

variables.desc: Variables that measure or are commonly used to analyze inequality: income, wages, wealth, consumption/expenditure, occupational status, education level, health indicators, household composition, region, race/ethnicity, gender, and derived inequality indices (Gini, Theil).
variables.narr: Include variables capturing individual or household economic resources, demographic attributes, labor market outcomes, educational attainment, health measures, and geographic identifiers that allow subgroup comparisons and inequality decomposition. Also include derived variables and indices explicitly labeled as inequality measures. Exclude variables that do not permit assessment of disparities (single-case identifiers without demographic/contextual attributes) or highly aggregated indicators that prevent subgroup or distributional analysis.

instruments_tools.desc: Questionnaires, survey modules, scales, measurement protocols, and software/tools used to collect or analyze inequality-related data and to compute distributional statistics and decomposition methods.
instruments_tools.narr: Include survey instruments that capture income, consumption, employment, education, health, and household characteristics; coding manuals; tools for measuring inequality (Gini calculators, decomposition routines, microsimulation models); and software packages and reproducible code for inequality analysis. Exclude instruments unrelated to distributional measurement (e.g., clinical instruments without socioeconomic variables) and tools that only visualize non-distributional data.

publication.desc: Scholarly works on trust in information, credibility of sources, information-seeking behavior, misinformation and disinformation, and the role of institutions and media in shaping public trust.
publication.narr: Include publications that investigate trust in information sources (news media, social media, governmental communications, experts), factors influencing perceived credibility, trust dynamics in digital environments, effects of misinformation, and interventions to build or measure trust in information. Empirical, theoretical, and review articles are relevant. Exclude papers where 'trust' refers to interpersonal trust unrelated to information exchange, or where information trust is only a passing phrase without substantive engagement.

research_data.desc: Datasets capturing perceptions of information credibility, media trust scales, experiments on trust in information, social media content annotated for trustworthiness, and observational data about information consumption and trust outcomes.
research_data.narr: Include survey data measuring trust in news, institutions, experts, or specific information items; experimental datasets testing interventions on perceived credibility; annotated corpora identifying trustworthy/untrustworthy content; and behavioral traces linking information exposure to trust indicators. Exclude datasets lacking measures related to information credibility or trust, and purely technical logs without contextual trust measures.

variables.desc: Variables assessing trust in information and sources: trust scales for media/institutions/experts, perceived credibility ratings, source trustworthiness, exposure to misinformation, fact-checking behavior, and confidence in knowledge.
variables.narr: Include validated items and indices measuring trust in specific information sources (e.g., television news, online news, social media), general media trust, perceived accuracy/credibility of messages, willingness to share, and behavioral proxies (clicks, shares tied to trust judgments). Exclude variables that measure unrelated forms of trust (e.g., generalized social trust) unless they are explicitly linked to information contexts.

instruments_tools.desc: Survey instruments, experimental protocols, coding schemes, annotation guidelines, and software/tools for measuring and analyzing trust in information and credibility assessments.
instruments_tools.narr: Include questionnaires and validated scales for media or source trust, experimental designs for credibility interventions, coding manuals for annotating trustworthiness of content, fact-checking frameworks, and analytical tools for sentiment/credibility detection. Exclude technical tools that only perform linguistic processing without relevance to trust measurement, unless paired with trust annotation protocols.

publication.desc: Publications on information policy and information politics: regulation, governance, political use of information, transparency, information control, and the political implications of information flows and technologies.
publication.narr: Include works that address policies governing information (data protection, freedom of information, media regulation), the political uses of information and communication (propaganda, public diplomacy, surveillance, open government), and scholarly analyses of how information shapes political processes. Include normative, empirical, and legal studies focused on the politics of information. Exclude publications that only mention 'information' in technical contexts without linking to policy or political effects.

research_data.desc: Datasets related to information policy and politics: legislative texts, policy databases, records of information access requests, datasets on government transparency, censorship events, and datasets tracking political information campaigns.
research_data.narr: Include collections of laws and regulations on data/information, datasets documenting FOI requests/responses, indices of press freedom/censorship, corpora of political communication campaigns, and cross-national policy indicators on information governance. Exclude technical datasets on information systems without political or policy metadata and datasets unrelated to governance or political uses of information.

variables.desc: Variables capturing aspects of information policy and politics: legal/regulatory indicators, transparency scores, censorship flags, frequency of information control events, access-to-information metrics, and measures of government communication practices.
variables.narr: Include variables that operationalize policy environments (presence/strength of data protection laws, FOI provisions), measures of censorship or content takedowns, indices of media freedom, counts of state information campaigns, and measures of public access to government information. Exclude purely technical variables describing system performance (latency, throughput) unless linked to political/policy outcomes (e.g., digital infrastructure affecting access to information).

instruments_tools.desc: Instruments and tools for studying information policy and politics: policy coding schemes, legal databases, FOI request templates, content censorship monitors, and analytical tools for mapping political information flows.
instruments_tools.narr: Include coding manuals and typologies for classifying information policies, structured templates for collecting FOI data, tools for monitoring and geolocating censorship or takedown events, and software for network analysis of political information dissemination. Exclude purely engineering tools for information systems administration that do not support political/policy research.

publication.desc: Publications on information and communication technologies (ICT): adoption, diffusion, digital skills, digital divide, ICT impacts on society, employment, education, and public services.
publication.narr: Include empirical and theoretical studies of ICT use, access, outcomes of digital technologies (internet, mobile, broadband, e‑government, ICT in education/workplaces), digital inequalities, policy evaluations of ICT programs, and societal implications of ICT proliferation. Exclude highly technical engineering papers focused on hardware design or low-level protocols when they lack social-science relevance to use, access, or impact.

research_data.desc: Datasets on ICT access and use: household ICT surveys, internet usage logs, broadband coverage maps, digital skills assessments, e‑government service usage, and workplace ICT adoption surveys.
research_data.narr: Include microdata capturing device ownership, internet connectivity, frequency and purpose of ICT use, digital literacy test scores, administrative records of e-service uptake, and geospatial data on network infrastructure. Exclude raw network traffic captures or engineering telemetry lacking demographic/contextual information needed for social analysis of ICT impacts.

variables.desc: Variables measuring ICT-related phenomena: internet access, device ownership, connection type and speed, frequency and purposes of use, digital skills, online activities (social media, e-commerce, e-government), and barriers to access.
variables.narr: Include variables that record household/individual-level ICT access (broadband, mobile), skills assessments, online engagement measures, location-based infrastructure indicators, and socioeconomic covariates enabling analysis of the digital divide. Exclude technical-only metrics (packet loss, port numbers) that do not inform social research on ICT adoption or effects.

instruments_tools.desc: Survey instruments, measurement protocols, digital skills tests, usage diaries, and tools for measuring ICT infrastructure and digital engagement.
instruments_tools.narr: Include standardized questionnaires for ICT access and use (e.g., household ICT modules), validated digital literacy assessments, log collection protocols, website/app analytics frameworks for research, and geospatial tools for mapping connectivity. Exclude developer tools and software components intended solely for building ICT systems without measurement or research application.

publication.desc: Publications on political interest (interest in politics): its measurement, determinants, consequences for participation, civic engagement, political knowledge, and attitudes.
publication.narr: Include studies that focus on individual-level political interest or political attentiveness, its relationship with voting and other forms of participation, media consumption patterns, socialization, demographic correlates, and cross-national comparisons. Also include methodological work on measuring political interest. Exclude works where 'interest' refers to policy interest groups or institutional interests rather than individual political interest.

research_data.desc: Datasets containing measures of interest in politics: public opinion surveys, election studies, panel datasets with political attitudinal modules, and time-series surveys tracking political interest over time.
research_data.narr: Include surveys and panels that include items on interest in politics, frequency of following political news, attention to public affairs, and associated behaviors (voting, protest, civic activities). Relevant sources include national election studies and cross-national surveys (e.g., ESS, Eurobarometer). Exclude datasets that do not include explicit measures of interest in politics or that measure organizational 'interest' rather than individual attitudinal interest.

variables.desc: Variables measuring political interest and attentiveness: self-reported interest in politics, frequency of following news/politics, attention to public affairs, political discussion frequency, and indices of political engagement.
variables.narr: Include single-item and multi-item measures where respondents report their level of interest in politics, how often they follow political news, and related behaviors (discussing politics, civic participation). Also include derived scales combining related items. Exclude variables that only measure political knowledge tests without attitudinal indicators unless paired with explicit interest measures.

instruments_tools.desc: Survey questions, modules, validated scales, and experimental protocols used to measure political interest and related constructs (attention, civic engagement).
instruments_tools.narr: Include standard questionnaire items and modules from election studies and international surveys that capture political interest, interview protocols, diary instruments for media attention, and experimental designs testing causal effects on interest. Exclude administrative tools or institutional records that do not directly measure individual political interest.

publication.desc: Publications that study individuals' interest or aspiration to assume leadership or supervisory roles. Includes empirical articles, reviews, theoretical papers and reports on leadership interest, leadership aspiration, desire for promotion, or intent to lead in organizational, educational or political settings.
publication.narr: Relevant publications explicitly address personal interest in leadership (e.g., leadership aspiration, willingness to lead, desire for managerial positions). Include cross-sectional and longitudinal empirical studies, theoretical treatments, and applied reports in German or English. Exclude works that only discuss leadership styles, team leadership effectiveness, organizational leadership structure, or leader traits without linking them to individuals' interest/aspiration to occupy leadership roles. Exclude studies focused solely on leadership training outcomes unless they measure pre-existing or changed interest in leadership.

research_data.desc: Datasets and study collections that contain measures of individuals' interest in leadership or aspiration for supervisory roles. Includes employee surveys, longitudinal career panels, student career intention surveys, and experimental datasets with variables on leadership intent.
research_data.narr: Include datasets with explicit variables measuring leadership interest, leadership career intentions, desire for promotion, or willingness to take supervisory tasks. Accept national or organizational employee surveys, student/graduate follow-ups, and experimental data where leadership choice is an outcome. Exclude datasets that only measure organizational leadership outcomes (performance, style) without a variable capturing personal interest or aspiration to lead.

variables.desc: Variables that operationalize interest in leadership: leadership aspiration, desire to be a manager, willingness to lead, promotion intent, leadership career intentions, and related constructs (leadership motivation).
variables.narr: Include single-item and multi-item scales that explicitly ask about wanting to lead, seeking managerial positions, or choosing leadership responsibilities. Include demographic moderators (age, gender, tenure) when paired with leadership interest variables. Exclude variables that only measure leadership behaviors, efficacy, or style without assessing interest/aspiration.

instruments_tools.desc: Questionnaires, scales and measurement tools that assess interest in leadership or aspiration to lead (e.g., leadership aspiration items, leadership motivation scales), as well as structured interview protocols and vignette measures that elicit willingness to assume leadership.
instruments_tools.narr: Include validated instruments or bespoke survey items that directly measure interest in leadership, promotion intent, or leadership career goals. Include experimental choice tasks and vignettes designed to elicit leadership preference. Exclude tools that measure general leadership ability, leader behavior, or organizational leadership climate when they do not measure individual interest or aspiration to lead.

publication.desc: Publications on work motivation: research about intrinsic and extrinsic motivation at work, employee engagement, motivational antecedents and outcomes, job design effects on motivation, and interventions to enhance workplace motivation.
publication.narr: Relevant publications explicitly address motivation in occupational contexts (paid work, volunteer work, internships). Include empirical studies, meta-analyses, theoretical frameworks (self-determination theory, expectancy theory), and applied evaluations of motivational interventions. Exclude studies of academic or school motivation unless directly tied to work contexts (e.g., vocational training). Exclude literature solely on job satisfaction unless motivation is a primary focus.

research_data.desc: Datasets containing measures of employee motivation, work engagement, intrinsic/extrinsic motivation scales, or related constructs in workplace surveys and organizational studies.
research_data.narr: Include employer or nationally representative surveys and longitudinal panels with variables on work motivation, engagement (e.g., UWES), or motivation-related antecedents/outcomes (performance, turnover). Include experimental and intervention datasets from organizational contexts. Exclude datasets focused on non-work settings (schools, leisure) or those lacking explicit motivation measures.

variables.desc: Variables measuring work motivation and related constructs: intrinsic motivation, extrinsic motivation, work engagement, motivation regulation, goals at work, task significance, autonomy, and motivational outcomes (effort, persistence, turnover intention).
variables.narr: Include validated scales (e.g., UWES, Work Extrinsic and Intrinsic Motivation Scale) and survey items that explicitly assess motivational orientation or intensity at work. Include job characteristics known to affect motivation (autonomy, task variety) when linked to motivation measures. Exclude variables that only capture general attitudes toward work without assessing motivational constructs.

instruments_tools.desc: Measurement instruments and tools used to assess work motivation: standardized questionnaires (e.g., WEIMS, UWES), situational judgment tests, diaries measuring daily motivation, intervention toolkits, and observational coding schemes for motivational behavior at work.
instruments_tools.narr: Include validated questionnaires and measurement protocols that target motivational constructs in occupational settings, daily experience-sampling tools for motivation at work, and experimental paradigms designed to manipulate or assess motivation. Exclude instruments developed for school or clinical contexts unless explicitly adapted and validated for workplace use.

publication.desc: Publications investigating job satisfaction: conceptualizations, determinants (job characteristics, leadership, pay), consequences (performance, turnover, health), measurement issues, cross-cultural comparisons, and interventions to improve satisfaction.
publication.narr: Include empirical studies, reviews and theoretical works where job satisfaction is a primary variable or outcome. Accept workplace-focused research across sectors and populations (employees, volunteers). Include studies on overall and facet-specific job satisfaction. Exclude articles that mention satisfaction only peripherally or focus solely on unrelated outcomes without assessing job satisfaction.

research_data.desc: Datasets and surveys containing job satisfaction measures such as overall satisfaction and facet-specific items from employee surveys, national labor studies, and longitudinal panels.
research_data.narr: Include employer surveys, national labor force panels, organizational climate studies and longitudinal data with validated job satisfaction items (e.g., single-item overall satisfaction, MSQ, JDI). Exclude datasets without job satisfaction measures or those limited to non-work contexts.

variables.desc: Variables that quantify job satisfaction: overall job satisfaction scores, facet scales (pay, supervision, coworkers, work itself), single-item satisfaction indicators, and related wellbeing measures tied to job satisfaction.
variables.narr: Include both global and domain-specific job satisfaction variables and their subscales. Include demographic and occupational covariates when analyzed in relation to job satisfaction. Exclude variables that only measure job performance or engagement if job satisfaction is not included.

instruments_tools.desc: Measurement instruments for job satisfaction such as the Minnesota Satisfaction Questionnaire (MSQ), Job Descriptive Index (JDI), single-item global satisfaction measures, and survey modules used in employee studies.
instruments_tools.narr: Include validated scales and commonly used survey items that measure overall and facet job satisfaction, along with administration guidelines and scoring procedures. Exclude instruments unrelated to job satisfaction (e.g., general life satisfaction scales) unless tied explicitly to the job domain.

publication.desc: Publications about adolescents (youth roughly aged 10–19): health, education, mental health, social behavior, risk behavior, development, and transition to adulthood. Includes empirical studies, reviews and policy reports focused on adolescent populations.
publication.narr: Relevant work centers on persons in adolescence (approximately ages 10–19, flexible to include lower/upper bounds in studies). Include research on physical and mental health, schooling, labor market entry, identity, family and peer influences, and youth policy. Exclude studies focusing solely on children under 10 or adults beyond adolescence unless data are disaggregated for adolescent subsamples.

research_data.desc: Datasets and survey collections focused on adolescents: school-based surveys, youth cohorts, health surveillance (e.g., HBSC, national youth health studies), and longitudinal panels tracking adolescent development.
research_data.narr: Include datasets with adolescent samples or age-disaggregated data covering behaviors, health, education, and social variables. Accept cross-sectional and longitudinal studies, school surveys, and administrative data on youth. Exclude datasets without adolescent-specific data or that aggregate adolescents into broader age ranges without separate indicators.

variables.desc: Variables relevant to adolescents: age-specific indicators (grade, pubertal stage), education status, mental health measures (depression, anxiety), risk behaviors (substance use, delinquency), family background, peer relations, and transition markers (vocational training, school-to-work).
variables.narr: Include variables that directly measure adolescent experiences, developmental status, health and behavior. Include validated measures used with youth (e.g., SDQ). Exclude adult-only measures or variables not applicable to adolescent contexts (e.g., retirement status).

instruments_tools.desc: Instruments and tools for researching adolescents: youth questionnaires, standardized screening instruments (SDQ, CES-DC), school survey instruments, developmental assessment tools, and protocols for interviewing minors (parental consent procedures).
instruments_tools.narr: Include age-appropriate validated instruments and survey modules tailored to adolescents, tools for assessing mental and physical health, and instruments for educational and social behavior research. Exclude adult-focused instruments unless validated for adolescent populations.

publication.desc: Publications concerning children and adolescents (birth through late adolescence): research on development, health, education, family, mental health, socialization, and policy issues affecting minors.
publication.narr: Relevant publications explicitly target children (infancy, childhood) and/or adolescents (up to ~18–19 years). Include empirical studies, longitudinal cohorts, reviews, clinical and educational research, and policy analyses addressing developmental, health, psychosocial, and educational outcomes. Exclude studies exclusively on adult populations or animal studies. Where age ranges are broad, include only if results for children/young people are separately reported.

research_data.desc: Datasets and studies that collect data on children and/or adolescents: birth cohorts, child health surveys, school-based datasets, family panels, and longitudinal studies that follow minors over time.
research_data.narr: Include datasets with samples of children and/or adolescents, covering health, development, education and family contexts (e.g., national child health surveys, birth cohort studies). Prefer data with age-specific measures and longitudinal follow-up. Exclude datasets that do not include minors or that only provide adult retrospective reports without direct child/adolescent measures.

variables.desc: Variables pertinent to children and adolescents: developmental milestones, cognitive and socio-emotional measures, physical health indicators, vaccination and growth data, schooling and attainment, child welfare indicators, and family socioeconomic variables.
variables.narr: Include variables valid for child and adolescent assessment (e.g., CBCL, developmental screening scores, school performance, family structure). Include age-appropriate health and behavior measures. Exclude adult-only indicators (employment status for older adults, retirement) and measures not applicable to minors.

instruments_tools.desc: Measurement tools used with children and adolescents: Child Behavior Checklist (CBCL), Strengths and Difficulties Questionnaire (SDQ), pediatric quality-of-life scales, developmental assessment batteries, school achievement tests, and consent/assent protocols.
instruments_tools.narr: Include validated, age-appropriate instruments and assessment protocols for children and adolescents, as well as survey modules designed for caregivers or schools. Exclude instruments validated only for adults or those unsuitable for minors without documented adaptation and validation.

publication.desc: Publications addressing 'klima' (climate) in broad senses: atmospheric/climatic systems, climate change impacts, climate policy, climate science, climate perception and discourse. Includes empirical studies, reviews, theoretical work, and policy analyses in social and natural sciences.
publication.narr: Relevant publications are those whose primary topic is climate or climatic phenomena (e.g., temperature trends, precipitation patterns, climate modelling, climate policy, public perceptions of climate). Include interdisciplinary works linking climate to health, economics, agriculture, urban planning, and social responses. Exclude items where 'klima' appears only metaphorically or as a minor mention (e.g., office climate used solely as workplace atmosphere) unless the work explicitly treats atmospheric or socio-environmental climate. Include publications in German or English and both empirical and conceptual studies.

research_data.desc: Datasets and data collections about climate: instrumental temperature and precipitation records, remote sensing/climate model outputs, greenhouse gas inventories, climate indices, observational networks, socio-environmental datasets on climate impacts and perceptions.
research_data.narr: Relevant data are time series of meteorological variables, gridded climate model outputs (CMIP etc.), satellite-derived climate products, national emissions inventories, and survey datasets on public attitudes toward climate. Include processed and raw data used to analyze climate patterns, impacts or policy outcomes. Exclude datasets unrelated to atmospheric or socio-environmental climate (e.g., 'organizational climate' survey data) unless clearly tied to environmental/climatic topics.

variables.desc: Variables that measure climatic conditions, drivers, impacts, and public responses: temperature, precipitation, humidity, CO2/CH4 concentrations, sea level, extreme event indices, vulnerability indicators, adaptation measures, climate risk perceptions.
variables.narr: Relevant variables include quantitative meteorological measures (daily/monthly/annual temperature, precipitation, drought indices), greenhouse gas concentrations, derived indices (heatwaves, cold spells, extreme precipitation), and socio-economic variables tied to climate impacts (crop yield losses, health outcomes). Also include attitudinal variables about climate concern and policy support. Exclude variables that use 'climate' only as a metaphor (e.g., corporate climate) unless clearly environmental.

instruments_tools.desc: Measurement and analytic instruments for climate science and social research on climate: meteorological sensors, remote sensing platforms, climate models, climate indices, survey instruments for climate attitudes, vulnerability/adaptation assessment tools.
instruments_tools.narr: Relevant instruments include weather stations, satellite sensors, ocean buoys, global/regional climate models (GCMs/RCMs), reanalysis products, standard climate indices (e.g., SPI, SPEI, Köppen classification), and validated survey questionnaires on climate attitudes and risk perception. Exclude general-purpose measurement tools with no explicit application to climate topics.

publication.desc: Publications specifically on 'klimawandel' (climate change): causes (anthropogenic and natural), impacts, mitigation, adaptation, vulnerability, policy responses, public perceptions, and communication of climate change.
publication.narr: Relevant works explicitly address climate change dynamics, evidence of warming, attribution studies, mitigation strategies (emission reduction, renewable energy), adaptation planning, socio-economic impacts, and public attitudes to climate change. Include empirical studies, case studies, reviews, policy evaluations, and IPCC-related analyses. Exclude publications that mention 'climate change' only peripherally or use the term metaphorically.

research_data.desc: Datasets on climate change: observed warming datasets, long-term temperature records, greenhouse gas inventories, emission scenario data, climate model simulations (projections), impact datasets, and survey data on climate change beliefs and behaviors.
research_data.narr: Include datasets used to quantify historical climate change, future scenario projections (RCP/SSP outputs), national/subnational emission inventories, impact assessments (e.g., crop yields under warming scenarios), and social survey datasets measuring awareness, beliefs, and mitigation/adaptation behaviors. Exclude datasets not directly addressing climate change processes or responses.

variables.desc: Variables that capture change and responses: trends in temperature and extreme events, emission rates, radiative forcing, vulnerability/adaptation indicators, mitigation behaviors, belief in anthropogenic climate change, policy support measures.
variables.narr: Relevant variables measure temporal changes (e.g., decadal temperature trend), frequency/intensity of extremes, CO2 emissions per capita, indicators of adaptive capacity, and attitudinal measures about climate change causes and policy preferences. Exclude static environmental descriptors that do not relate to change unless used to assess change or vulnerability.

instruments_tools.desc: Tools for studying climate change: attribution methods, earth system and integrated assessment models, emission calculators, vulnerability/resilience assessment frameworks, survey instruments measuring climate change perceptions and behavior, and decision-support tools for mitigation/adaptation.
instruments_tools.narr: Include climate models (GCMs/ESMs), statistical attribution techniques, IAMs, carbon footprint calculators, adaptation planning tools (e.g., climate risk assessments), and validated questionnaires on climate change beliefs and actions. Exclude tools with no explicit application to climate change research.

publication.desc: Publications on 'kultur' (culture): cultural practices, arts, heritage, cultural policy, cultural sociology/anthropology, cross-cultural studies, cultural values and identity, and cultural change.
publication.narr: Relevant publications focus on aspects of culture—traditions, norms, rituals, arts and cultural industries, heritage management, cultural policy, cultural identity and practices, and comparative cultural studies. Include theoretical, ethnographic, historical, policy-oriented, and quantitative works. Exclude works where 'culture' is used only in a narrow biological/medical sense (e.g., cell culture) unless paired with socio-cultural content.

research_data.desc: Datasets about cultural phenomena: cultural participation surveys, heritage inventories, arts statistics, ethnographic corpora, cultural consumption and production datasets, and cross-national value surveys related to culture.
research_data.narr: Include survey data on cultural participation, attendance, values and identities (e.g., Eurobarometer cultural modules, ESS cultural items), cultural economics data (ticket sales, funding), museum and heritage registries, and coded qualitative corpora on cultural practices. Exclude biomedical culture data (laboratory cell cultures) and datasets that only mention 'culture' metaphorically (organizational climate) without cultural content.

variables.desc: Variables capturing cultural aspects: participation frequencies, cultural capital indicators, language use, ethnic and cultural identity, values and norms measures, attendance at cultural events, funding/support levels for arts and heritage.
variables.narr: Relevant variables include measures of cultural participation (visits per year), self-reported cultural identity, proficiency/use of languages, indicators of cultural capital (education, tastes), attitudes toward cultural diversity, and institutional measures (number of cultural organizations, funding amounts). Exclude laboratory culture measures and variables unrelated to social/cultural phenomena.

instruments_tools.desc: Tools and instruments for cultural research: standardized survey modules on culture and identity, cultural participation questionnaires, ethnographic interview guides, coding schemes for qualitative cultural data, cultural policy evaluation frameworks, and cultural heritage inventories.
instruments_tools.narr: Include validated survey instruments measuring cultural engagement and values, structured interview guides for ethnography, content analysis coding schemes for cultural texts, and methodological toolkits for evaluating cultural policy and heritage. Exclude biomedical laboratory tools or instruments unrelated to humanities/social scientific study of culture.

publication.desc: Publications on workplace learning ('lernen am Arbeit'): on-the-job learning, informal and formal workplace training, continuing vocational education, learning organisations, apprenticeships, and adult learning in employment contexts.
publication.narr: Relevant publications investigate how learning occurs at work (formal training, mentoring, peer learning, workplace practices), effectiveness of training programs, impacts on skills and career development, organizational learning, and policy on lifelong learning. Include case studies, evaluations, longitudinal studies, and theoretical work. Exclude general education literature not linked to work contexts or uses of 'learning' that are purely technological (machine learning) unless tied to human workplace learning.

research_data.desc: Datasets on workplace learning and training: employer-provided training surveys, continuing vocational education statistics, longitudinal employer-employee matched data, apprenticeship records, and surveys on informal learning at work.
research_data.narr: Include representative surveys of training participation (e.g., CVTS), employer training modules, administrative apprenticeship data, panel data linking training to outcomes (wages, mobility), and qualitative datasets documenting workplace learning practices. Exclude datasets focused on school-based learning without workplace component or datasets about machine learning systems.

variables.desc: Variables measuring workplace learning: participation in training (type, duration), informal learning activities, mentoring received, skill acquisition measures, training costs, employer support, learning outcomes (skill tests, wages, promotion), and workplace learning culture indicators.
variables.narr: Relevant variables capture occurrence and intensity of on-the-job training, certification achieved, frequency of informal learning, employer-provided training hours, individual learning strategies, and outcomes such as productivity or career progression. Exclude variables that measure non-learning aspects of work unless used to analyze learning processes (e.g., job tenure only used to study learning opportunities).

instruments_tools.desc: Instruments for researching workplace learning: training evaluation tools, workplace learning questionnaires, competency assessments, observational protocols for workplace learning, employer survey modules, and tools for measuring informal learning and knowledge transfer.
instruments_tools.narr: Include standardized instruments for assessing training participation and outcomes, validated competency tests, interview guides and observation checklists for workplace learning episodes, and employer questionnaires on training provision. Exclude instruments designed solely for classroom education or for automated/machine learning evaluation.

publication.desc: Publications on left-right orientation ('links-rechts Orientierung'): political ideology, ideological self-placement, left-right constructs, partisan placement, ideology measurement, and the role of left-right orientation in voting and attitudes.
publication.narr: Relevant works explicitly study left-right political orientation, including conceptual debates about the left-right dimension, empirical analyses of self-placement scales, its relationship with policy attitudes and party choice, and cross-national comparisons. Include methodological papers on measuring ideological placement. Exclude non-political uses of left/right (spatial orientation, handedness) unless clearly about political orientation.

research_data.desc: Datasets containing measures of left-right orientation: national and cross-national survey data with ideological self-placement items (e.g., ESS, ISSP, Eurobarometer), panel studies tracking ideological change, and datasets with party position mappings on left-right scales.
research_data.narr: Include survey datasets with explicit left-right self-placement or derived ideological scales, manifesto/party placement datasets (e.g., MARPOR), and longitudinal data capturing shifts in ideological identification. Exclude datasets that record only spatial or physical left/right measures or those lacking political ideological indicators.

variables.desc: Variables that operationalize left-right orientation: self-placement on left-right scales, composite ideological scores (economic/social dimensions), party identification mapped to left-right, issue-based scales aggregated into left-right orientation, and extremes/moderation indicators.
variables.narr: Relevant variables include 0–10 or 1–7 left-right self-placement items, factor scores from issue items representing left-right dimension, categorical left/center/right labels, and consistency measures between self-placement and policy attitudes. Exclude variables measuring non-ideological left/right concepts (body orientation, handedness).

instruments_tools.desc: Instruments for measuring left-right orientation: survey questions for ideological self-placement, battery of policy attitude items for scale construction, psychometric tools for dimensionality analysis, party position coding schemes, and Q-methodology protocols for ideological mapping.
instruments_tools.narr: Include standard left-right self-placement items, validated issue batteries to derive ideological scales, coding manuals for placing parties/manifestos on left-right spectra, and statistical tools (factor analysis, IRT) used to validate left-right measures. Exclude instruments not related to political ideology measurement.

publication.desc: Publications addressing media as channels of communication and information (e.g., mass media, social media, digital platforms), their production, content, audiences, effects, regulation, and representation.
publication.narr: Relevant publications are empirical studies, reviews, theoretical papers, reports, and books that focus on media communication, media use, media effects, media policy, journalism, digital platforms, social media, advertising, media literacy, media representations, and related sociological or political implications. Include publications that examine specific media formats (television, radio, newspapers, online news, blogs, social networking sites), media consumption patterns, media content analysis, audience studies, algorithmic bias in platforms, and media influence on attitudes and behavior. Exclude works where 'media' refers to biological or laboratory media, physical manufacturing media, or unrelated metaphorical uses (unless the communication/media meaning is central). Also exclude purely technical engineering studies of hardware components that do not treat media as channels of communication or social phenomena.

research_data.desc: Datasets and data collections containing media content, media usage metrics, social media corpora, audience surveys, content analysis datasets, and platform analytics relevant to media research.
research_data.narr: Include datasets that record media consumption (time use or audience ratings), survey data on media habits and attitudes, corpora of news articles or social media posts (tweets, Facebook posts, forum threads), annotated content analysis datasets, logs from media platforms, network data about information diffusion, and experimental datasets measuring media effects. Data may be cross-sectional, longitudinal, or event-based and should directly measure media phenomena. Exclude datasets unrelated to communication (e.g., biological media), datasets that only incidentally mention media without measures of media content or use, and raw hardware-level telemetry unrelated to content or audience behavior.

variables.desc: Variables that measure media exposure, consumption, content, engagement, trust, source credibility, platform use, frequency, duration, and media effects (attitudes, knowledge, behavior).
variables.narr: Include variable names and descriptions that capture types of media used (TV, radio, print, online, social media platforms), frequency and duration of media use, intensity of engagement (likes, shares, comments), content categories (news, entertainment, political content), trust in media, perceived bias, source credibility, exposure to specific messages or campaigns, and measures of media effects (knowledge change, attitude change, behavioral intentions). Exclude variables that use the word 'media' in non-communication senses (e.g., culture media in labs) or variables that are too generic without a clear relation to media use or content (e.g., a variable named 'channel' without context).

instruments_tools.desc: Measurement instruments and tools for media research: survey questionnaires, coding schemes for content analysis, media diaries, web-scraping and social media collection tools, platform APIs, and validated scales measuring media-related constructs.
instruments_tools.narr: Relevant instruments include validated survey items and scales for media exposure and media literacy, content analysis codebooks and intercoder reliability protocols, media diaries and experience sampling instruments, tools and scripts for collecting social media data (APIs, crawlers), sentiment and topic analysis pipelines, and methodological protocols for experimental media research. Include documentation, manuals, and codebooks that enable replication. Exclude instruments solely for biological media cultivation, manufacturing quality control, or hardware diagnostics unrelated to communication research.

publication.desc: Publications on characteristics of work (job attributes), work conditions, job quality, job design, employment features, task composition, and occupational characteristics.
publication.narr: Relevant publications include empirical studies, theoretical articles, policy reports, and books that investigate job characteristics such as autonomy, task variety, skill requirements, workload, supervisory relations, work stressors, physical conditions, flexibility, contractual arrangements (temporary vs permanent), job demands–resources, job quality indicators, and occupational qualification profiles. Include research on measurement and conceptualization of work characteristics, sectoral differences, and implications for health, well‑being, productivity, and inequality. Exclude publications that are not about job/work characteristics (e.g., general labor market trends without link to job features), or those using the phrase in unrelated contexts (e.g., product characteristics rather than job attributes).

research_data.desc: Datasets measuring job and work characteristics: surveys, employer records, time-use data, job-exposure matrices, and occupation-level descriptors capturing working conditions and job attributes.
research_data.narr: Include datasets that contain variables on job content (tasks, complexity), working hours, contract type, autonomy and control, mental/physical demands, ergonomic and safety conditions, pay and benefits, training opportunities, and occupational classifications (ISCO, O*NET type descriptors). Also include longitudinal employer-employee matched data and workplace assessments. Exclude datasets that mention 'work' only as employment status without characteristics, or data solely about company-level outcomes without information on job-level features.

variables.desc: Variables describing job characteristics such as autonomy, task complexity, workload, hours, contract type, physical demands, psychosocial risks, role clarity, and training requirements.
variables.narr: Relevant variables explicitly measure attributes of work: job autonomy/control, decision latitude, task variety, repetitiveness, physical workload, exposure to hazards, psychosocial stressors (job demands, social support), working time arrangements (shift work, part-time), contract permanence, overemployment/underemployment, training/skill requirements, and indices of job quality. Include variables coded at worker or job level. Exclude variables that only indicate employment/unemployment status without detailing work characteristics.

instruments_tools.desc: Instruments and tools to assess characteristics of work: job-content questionnaires, psychosocial risk scales, ergonomics checklists, workplace observation protocols, and occupational classification tools.
instruments_tools.narr: Include validated instruments such as the Job Content Questionnaire (JCQ), Effort-Reward Imbalance (ERI) scales, Copenhagen Psychosocial Questionnaire (COPSOQ), O*NET or ISCO-based task inventories, workplace hazard assessment checklists, time-use diaries, and structured job-analysis protocols. Also include measurement manuals, codebooks, and interviewer guides for assessing job attributes. Exclude tools unrelated to measuring job characteristics (e.g., general HR software without assessment modules) or instruments focused only on organizational performance without job-level measurement.

publication.desc: Publications on migration, including international and internal migration flows, causes and consequences, migrant integration, policies, remittances, refugees and asylum, and migration governance.
publication.narr: Relevant publications are empirical, theoretical, or policy-oriented works that analyze migration processes (immigration, emigration, internal migration), determinants (economic, political, environmental), migrant integration and acculturation, labor migration, refugee and asylum studies, return migration, transnationalism, diasporas, remittances, and migration policy and law. Include demographic, sociological, economic, and public-health perspectives. Exclude works that use the term 'migration' in unrelated scientific contexts (e.g., cell migration in biology) unless the human migration meaning is central.

research_data.desc: Datasets on migration: population registers, survey data on migrants, border statistics, asylum and refugee records, remittance datasets, and mobility histories relevant to migration research.
research_data.narr: Include data documenting migration flows (origin-destination matrices), migrant stocks, individual-level surveys with migration histories, administrative records on permits and asylum cases, labor migration statistics, longitudinal studies of migrants, remittance transactions, and geocoded mobility data. Datasets should enable analysis of causes, experiences, integration outcomes, or policy impacts of migration. Exclude biological or ecological datasets referring to organismal migration, and datasets that only tangentially mention migration without usable migration measures.

variables.desc: Variables capturing migration status and characteristics: country/region of birth and residence, migration history, legal status, reason for migration, duration, language proficiency, integration indicators, remittances, and mobility patterns.
variables.narr: Relevant variables include migrant origin and destination, date/year of migration, duration of stay, citizenship and legal/permit status, refugee/asylum status, reason for migration (economic, family, conflict), return intentions, language skills, employment status and occupational mobility, social integration measures, remittance sending/receiving, and household composition changes because of migration. Exclude variables named 'migration' that refer to cell or animal movement in biological studies.

instruments_tools.desc: Instruments and tools for migration research: survey modules and questionnaires capturing migration histories, migration registers, tracking protocols, qualitative interview guides, and coding schemes for legal statuses and reasons for migration.
instruments_tools.narr: Include standardized survey modules (e.g., migration history modules), census questions templates on place of birth and previous residence, administrative register schemas, interview guides for migrant experiences, protocols for longitudinal tracking and sampling of mobile populations, and classification tools for legal statuses and migrant typologies. Also include GIS and mobility-tracking tools used in migration studies. Exclude laboratory tools for biological migration or instruments not designed to measure human mobility and migration processes.

publication.desc: Publications concerning employees/staff (mitarbeiter): employment relations, staff management, workplace behavior, employee well‑being, organizational studies, and HR practices.
publication.narr: Relevant publications include empirical studies, theoretical papers, case studies, and reports about employees, including topics such as job satisfaction, motivation, performance, absenteeism, turnover, employee engagement, workplace relations, HR policies, leadership effects on staff, training and development, and staff demographics. Include works that focus on staff in various sectors and occupational groups. Exclude publications where 'Mitarbeiter' is used in non-employee contexts (e.g., co-author lists) or documents primarily about employers, customers, or markets without focus on employees.

research_data.desc: Datasets on employees: employer-employee linked datasets, staff surveys, payroll/HR administrative records, occupational panels, and personnel files useful for analyzing employee outcomes and workplace processes.
research_data.narr: Include datasets that provide individual-level and job-level information on employees such as demographic characteristics, employment contract, tenure, wages, working hours, performance evaluations, training records, absenteeism, and survey measures of well-being and engagement. Also include matched employer-employee datasets and workplace-level contextual variables. Exclude datasets that only cover employers or organizational finances without staff-level information, or lists of collaborators not indicating employment relationships.

variables.desc: Variables describing employees: demographic and employment attributes, job tenure, contract type, wages, performance measures, satisfaction, absenteeism, turnover intentions, training participation, and workplace relations.
variables.narr: Relevant variables explicitly measure characteristics of employees: employee ID, age, gender, education, occupation, tenure, contract type (permanent/temporary), salary/wage, working hours, job grade, promotion history, performance ratings, job satisfaction, organizational commitment, intention to leave, absenteeism, participation in training, and supervisory relationships. Exclude variables where 'mitarbeiter' appears as an author or contributor label but not as an employee characteristic.

instruments_tools.desc: Instruments and tools for employee research: staff survey questionnaires, HR information systems, performance appraisal instruments, employee engagement scales, exit interview protocols, and staff audit tools.
instruments_tools.narr: Include validated employee-focused instruments such as job satisfaction scales, engagement and commitment questionnaires, 360-degree feedback tools, performance appraisal forms, HR administrative data schemas, staff climate and culture surveys, and interview guides used in employee studies. Also include codebooks and manuals for employee datasets. Exclude general business software unrelated to measuring or researching employees and tools intended only for volunteer or collaborator tracking not tied to employment.

publication.desc: Publications on mobility (mobilität), including transport and commuting, spatial mobility, social mobility, accessibility, migration-related mobility, and mobility behavior and policy.
publication.narr: Relevant publications are studies, reviews, and reports that investigate human mobility behaviors and systems: transportation modes and choices, commuting patterns, travel behavior, urban mobility, accessibility and spatial planning, mobility inequality, social mobility and career mobility, mobility transitions, and mobility-related policy and infrastructure. Include empirical analyses, modeling studies, and qualitative research on barriers and enablers of mobility. Exclude studies that use 'mobilität' solely in metaphorical or unrelated technical contexts (e.g., molecular mobility in physics or chemistry) unless human or social mobility is central.

research_data.desc: Datasets on mobility: travel surveys, GPS and smartphone mobility traces, public transport usage, commuting statistics, origin-destination matrices, and longitudinal data on social mobility.
research_data.narr: Include datasets capturing individual or aggregate movement (travel diaries, sensor/GPS logs, mobile network data, smartcard transit records), commuting flows, modal shares, accessibility measures, transport network attributes, and data on social mobility (intergenerational income/occupation mobility). Also include datasets suited for modeling mobility patterns and evaluating mobility policies. Exclude sensor datasets measuring non-human particle mobility or datasets that do not contain movement or mobility-relevant variables.

variables.desc: Variables measuring mobility: travel frequency, trip distance and duration, mode of transport, commuting time, origin and destination, mobility constraints, accessibility indices, and indicators of social/mobile career mobility.
variables.narr: Relevant variables include number of trips, trip purpose, mode choice (car, bike, public transport, walking), travel time and distance, frequency of travel, commuting patterns, car ownership, access to transport, mobility limitations, accessibility scores, intergenerational occupation/income mobility measures, and modal shift indicators. Exclude variables that use 'mobility' in purely biological or physical senses unrelated to human movement or social mobility unless clearly contextualized.

instruments_tools.desc: Instruments and tools for measuring mobility: travel survey questionnaires, GPS/smartphone logging apps, travel diary protocols, transport modeling software, accessibility calculators, and indicators for social mobility analysis.
instruments_tools.narr: Include standardized travel diary instruments, GPS and smartphone data collection tools, public transport smartcard data processing tools, origin-destination matrix construction protocols, transport demand and traffic simulation models, GIS tools for accessibility analysis, and survey modules for social mobility (e.g., parental occupation/education modules). Also include manuals, coding schemes, and data processing scripts specific to mobility research. Exclude laboratory instruments measuring molecular mobility or tools unrelated to human or social mobility measurement.

publication.desc: Publications on employee motivation and workplace-related motivational processes, including empirical studies, reviews, and theoretical work in organizational/industrial psychology and human resources.
publication.narr: Include studies that investigate motivation among employees, work engagement, job satisfaction, organizational commitment, incentive systems, leadership effects on motivation, motivation interventions in workplace settings, and cross-cultural comparisons of employee motivation. Include both quantitative and qualitative empirical work and meta-analyses. Exclude publications that focus on non-employee populations (e.g., students, athletes) unless the study explicitly concerns workplace or occupational contexts; exclude purely technical HR system descriptions without motivational focus.

research_data.desc: Datasets collected from employees or workplaces measuring motivational constructs, engagement, job attitudes, or intervention outcomes.
research_data.narr: Include survey datasets, longitudinal HR panels, intervention trial data, employee engagement indexes, organizational climate surveys and anonymized administrative HR data that contain measures of motivation, job satisfaction, turnover intention, rewards, or performance linked to motivational variables. Include metadata specifying sample, measurement instruments, and scales. Exclude datasets from non-work contexts, small lab samples of non-employee participants, or datasets lacking any measure of motivation or workplace-related outcomes.

variables.desc: Variables capturing employee motivation and related workplace constructs (intrinsic/extrinsic motivation, engagement, satisfaction, commitment, turnover intention).
variables.narr: Include variables representing validated motivational constructs (e.g., intrinsic/extrinsic motivation scores, work engagement subscales, job satisfaction indices, organizational commitment, motivation-related predictors like leadership style, rewards, autonomy) and key covariates (role, tenure, occupation, industry). Exclude variables unrelated to workplace motivation (e.g., general cognitive tests) unless explicitly analyzed as predictors of employee motivation.
