instruments_tools.desc: Measurement instruments and protocols for assessing employee motivation and workplace engagement (questionnaires, interview guides, observational checklists).
instruments_tools.narr: Include validated instruments and tools used in organizational contexts such as the Utrecht Work Engagement Scale (UWES), Job Diagnostic Survey (JDS), Minnesota Satisfaction Questionnaire (MSQ), Work Extrinsic and Intrinsic Motivation Scale (WEIMS), organizational climate instruments, structured interview protocols for motivation, and workplace observation schemes. Include descriptions of administration, translation/validation for German contexts, and scoring. Exclude ad-hoc or single-item measures without validation unless clearly described as exploratory tools.

publication.desc: Publications addressing the role of motivation in learning processes across educational levels and learning settings, including theoretical frameworks and empirical studies.
publication.narr: Include research on how motivation affects learning outcomes, instructional design targeting motivation, self-regulated learning, achievement motivation, intrinsic/extrinsic motivation in classroom and online learning, motivation interventions, and theoretical accounts (e.g., self-determination theory, expectancy-value). Include experimental, longitudinal, and classroom-based studies as well as reviews. Exclude works solely about motivation in non-learning contexts (e.g., workplace motivation) unless tied to learning/training.

research_data.desc: Datasets that link motivational measures with learning outcomes, instructional variables, or longitudinal learning trajectories.
research_data.narr: Include datasets from schools, universities, MOOCs, training programs, or experimental studies that contain measures of motivation (e.g., intrinsic/extrinsic scales, goal orientation), study strategies, and objective or self-reported learning outcomes (grades, test scores, skill acquisition). Include learning analytics logs that capture engagement correlated with motivational indicators. Exclude datasets without any motivation-related measures or those purely about cognitive ability without learning motivation content.

variables.desc: Variables representing motivation in learning contexts: intrinsic/extrinsic motivation, goal orientation, task value, self-regulation, and learning outcomes.
variables.narr: Include variables such as intrinsic/extrinsic motivation scores, achievement goals, task value, self-efficacy for learning, study strategies, persistence, time on task, course completion, and assessment scores. Include demographic and contextual covariates (age, educational level, instructional format). Exclude variables unrelated to learning motivation (e.g., general workplace engagement) unless linked to training/learning outcomes.

instruments_tools.desc: Instruments and tools for measuring motivation in learning: questionnaires, observational protocols, learning analytics methods, and intervention materials.
instruments_tools.narr: Include validated scales such as the Academic Motivation Scale (AMS), Motivated Strategies for Learning Questionnaire (MSLQ), Goal Orientation Scales, self-regulated learning instruments, situational interest measures, and coding schemes for classroom motivation. Also include tools for measuring online engagement (clickstream, LMS logs), and instructional materials used in motivation interventions. Exclude instruments that do not measure motivational constructs or that are exclusively for non-learning applications.

publication.desc: Publications exploring the relationship between motivation and interest (personal and situational) across educational, psychological, and applied contexts.
publication.narr: Include empirical and theoretical work on how interest and motivation interact (e.g., development of interest, situational vs. individual interest, interest as antecedent/consequence of motivation), measures and interventions to foster interest, and studies linking interest to engagement and learning or behavior. Include cross-disciplinary work (education, psychology). Exclude studies that use 'interest' in a non-psychological sense (e.g., financial or consumer interest) unless psychological interest constructs are central.

research_data.desc: Datasets measuring both interest and motivational constructs, including their development over time or in response to interventions.
research_data.narr: Include surveys, longitudinal panels, experimental datasets, and classroom or domain-specific studies that contain measures of situational and personal interest alongside motivation measures and related outcomes (engagement, persistence). Include metadata describing scales and timing. Exclude datasets that measure only one of the constructs (interest or motivation) without linking them, or that treat interest only as demographic/consumption data.

variables.desc: Variables capturing personal and situational interest and related motivational constructs (engagement, persistence, value, curiosity).
variables.narr: Include variables for personal interest, situational interest, curiosity, task value, intrinsic/extrinsic motivation, engagement, time on task, and persistence. Include contextual moderators (topic domain, learning environment). Exclude unrelated variables (e.g., financial interest metrics) unless clearly operationalized as psychological interest.

instruments_tools.desc: Measurement instruments and protocols for assessing interest and motivation: interest inventories, situational interest scales, curiosity measures, and complementary observational/analytics tools.
instruments_tools.narr: Include validated instruments such as the Situational Interest Scale, Personal Interest Questionnaires, Domain-specific interest inventories, Curiosity scales, and instruments that jointly measure motivation and interest (components of AMS, MSLQ subscales). Also include observational coding schemes and digital measures (e.g., attention/engagement trackers) used to operationalize interest. Exclude tools that measure only consumer preferences or market interest without psychological constructs.

publication.desc: Publications on media use and media consumption patterns, including studies of digital, social, traditional, and multi-platform media usage and effects.
publication.narr: Include empirical studies, surveys, time-use research, and reviews that examine frequency, duration, platforms, purposes (news, entertainment, socializing), media multitasking, demographic differences, and effects of media use. Include cross-national comparisons and studies on media literacy and digital media behaviors. Exclude purely technical telecommunications literature (network infrastructure) unless it directly addresses user media consumption behavior.

research_data.desc: Datasets documenting media usage: surveys, time-use diaries, digital trace data, platform analytics, and content consumption logs.
research_data.narr: Include representative surveys of media habits, longitudinal time-use studies, smartphone/app usage logs, social media activity datasets, web browsing histories (anonymized), and combined self-report and objective measurement datasets that capture platform, frequency, duration, device, and purpose. Include metadata on sampling and measurement methods. Exclude datasets that do not contain media use variables or that only document technical network metrics without user behavior data.

variables.desc: Variables describing media use behavior: frequency, duration, platform type, device, purpose, multitasking, and media content categories.
variables.narr: Include variables such as daily/weekly hours spent on specific media, number of sessions, platform identifiers (TV, radio, social media, streaming services), device used, purposes (news, social contact, entertainment), measures of multitasking, and related demographic covariates. Exclude variables that refer only to technical content delivery parameters (bandwidth, packet loss) unless tied to user consumption patterns.

instruments_tools.desc: Measurement instruments and tools for assessing media use: questionnaires, time-use diaries, passive digital tracking tools, and coding schemes for content and engagement.
instruments_tools.narr: Include validated media use questionnaires, standardized time-use diaries, app and browser logging tools, APIs and analytics methods for social media/platform data collection, and coding manuals for content classification and engagement metrics. Include protocols for ethical data collection and anonymization. Exclude purely network-management tools or content-production software that do not measure user consumption.

publication.desc: Publications on online sport activities, including online fitness services, virtual training, e-sports, digital sport participation, and studies of online sport communities and platforms.
publication.narr: Include empirical and theoretical work on online fitness platforms, live/recorded exercise classes, tele-coaching, virtual competitions, e-sports as sport, participant motivation and adherence to online sport programs, health and performance outcomes, and platform design for sport. Include comparative studies between online and offline sport. Exclude publications only about traditional offline sport unless they compare or integrate online components.

research_data.desc: Datasets related to online sport and fitness: user logs from fitness apps/platforms, e-sports performance data, intervention trials of online exercise programs, and participation metrics.
research_data.narr: Include datasets containing platform usage logs (session frequency, duration, class attendance), wearable-derived activity data linked to online programs, e-sports match and performance statistics, self-report adherence and outcome measures from online interventions, and community engagement metrics. Ensure datasets include variables describing online modality. Exclude datasets solely about offline sporting events without online interaction or that lack measures specific to online delivery.

variables.desc: Variables capturing online sport participation and outcomes: usage frequency, session duration, physical activity metrics, performance stats, adherence, and engagement indicators.
variables.narr: Include variables such as number of online workouts, minutes of activity per session, step counts/heart rate from wearables during online sessions, e-sports performance indicators (scores, rankings), attendance of live classes, user engagement measures (comments, likes), and self-reported fitness outcomes. Include demographics and device/platform identifiers. Exclude variables that do not differentiate online from offline sport activity.

instruments_tools.desc: Instruments and tools for studying online sport: fitness tracking devices, app/platform analytics, e-sports stat trackers, questionnaires on online exercise behavior, and intervention materials for virtual training.
instruments_tools.narr: Include wearable sensors and their data processing protocols, app analytics dashboards, APIs for platform data extraction, validated questionnaires on digital exercise behavior and adherence, performance tracking tools used in e-sports, and manuals for online coaching interventions. Also include methods for measuring user engagement in livestreams. Exclude measurement tools designed solely for in-person sport that have no online adaptation or data export capability.

publication.desc: Publications on vocational/career orientation, career choice, guidance and transitions between education and work.
publication.narr: Relevant publications report empirical studies, reviews, theoretical frameworks or policy analyses about occupational orientation, vocational guidance, career decision-making, transition from school to work, apprenticeships and career counseling. Include works in German or English addressing students, jobseekers, trainees or employees and those comparing guidance systems. Exclude publications focused on non-career meanings of 'orientation' (e.g., spatial orientation), purely macro-level labor market statistics without individual-level orientation or decision-making content, and unrelated domains such as political orientation.

research_data.desc: Datasets measuring career intentions, vocational aspirations, guidance programs and transitions from education to employment.
research_data.narr: Relevant datasets contain individual-level measures of occupational preferences, career intentions, vocational interests, career decision self-efficacy, records of counseling interventions, apprenticeship participation, and longitudinal follow-up of school-to-work transitions. Include national or regional school and youth surveys, cohort studies of students/trainees, program evaluation data for guidance interventions and datasets documenting labor-market entry. Exclude datasets that only provide aggregate employment statistics, datasets about unrelated 'orientation' constructs (e.g., spatial), or purely employer-side HR data without information on individual career orientation.

variables.desc: Variables capturing vocational interests, occupational intentions, career decision-making, guidance received and transition outcomes.
variables.narr: Relevant variables measure career aspiration, preferred occupation, RIASEC codes or interest inventories, vocational guidance attendance, counseling outcomes, career decision self-efficacy, perceived fit, reasons for occupational choice, apprenticeship enrollment, time to employment after education. Include variables coded for analysis (scales, indices, categorical occupational choices). Exclude generic employment variables with no information on orientation or preferences, and variables referring to other kinds of 'orientation' (e.g., geographic orientation).

instruments_tools.desc: Questionnaires, standardized tests and program manuals used to assess vocational interests, career decision-making, and guidance interventions.
instruments_tools.narr: Include validated instruments and tools such as Self-Directed Search, Holland (RIASEC) inventories, Career Adapt-Abilities Scale, Career Decision-Making Self-Efficacy scales, vocational interest inventories, school/counseling program manuals, assessment batteries used in career guidance, and measurement protocols for tracking transitions. Include translation/adaptation documentation and scoring guides. Exclude instruments focused on unrelated constructs (spatial orientation or political orientation) and employer-only HR tools that do not assess individual vocational orientation.

publication.desc: Publications on personality psychology, trait models, assessment, development and applications.
publication.narr: Relevant publications present empirical research, theory, reviews or methodological work on personality structure (e.g., Big Five), trait measurement, personality development across the lifespan, personality and behavior relationships, clinical and differential aspects, cross-cultural comparisons, and applied uses (work, health). Include German and English works that explicitly treat 'Persönlichkeit' as personality/traits. Exclude uses of 'personality' in metaphorical/non-psychological senses (e.g., 'a city's personality'), organizational brand 'personality' absent individual trait measurement, or unrelated constructs like political personality unless tied to personality measures.

research_data.desc: Datasets containing individual-level personality measures, trait inventories, longitudinal personality studies and cross-cultural personality surveys.
research_data.narr: Relevant datasets include measures from instruments such as NEO-PI-R, BFI, TIPI, IPIP scales, temperament inventories, longitudinal panels tracking personality change, twin studies, and datasets linking personality to health, labor market or educational outcomes. Include metadata describing administration, scoring, and sample characteristics. Exclude datasets without personality-related variables, or those where 'personality' is only a peripheral label without standardized measurement.

variables.desc: Variables operationalizing personality traits, facets, temperament, and related scales or indices.
variables.narr: Include variables representing Big Five domains and facets, personality disorder scales where applicable, temperament dimensions, composite personality indices, item-level responses for personality questionnaires, and reliability/scale information. Include coding for reverse-scored items and normative tables if available. Exclude variables that do not measure personality (e.g., single impressions or interviewer assessments that are not validated personality measures) or broad demographic descriptors mislabeled as 'personality.'

instruments_tools.desc: Standardized personality questionnaires, short-form scales, manuals, scoring keys and validation studies.
instruments_tools.narr: Include validated instruments such as NEO-PI-R/3, BFI/10/44, TIPI, IPIP scales, Eysenck inventories, personality disorder instruments, instrument manuals, translation/adaptation documentation, scoring algorithms and psychometric validation reports. Also include computerized assessment tools and coding schemes for personality data. Exclude ad hoc or single-item measures without validation and instruments solely measuring unrelated constructs (e.g., charisma as marketing term).

publication.desc: Publications investigating forms, determinants and consequences of political participation and civic engagement.
publication.narr: Relevant publications examine voting, protest, petitioning, contacting officials, civic volunteering, membership in political organizations, digital political activity, mobilization, inequalities in participation, and theoretical or empirical analyses of determinants and effects. Include cross-national, national and local studies, methodological papers on measuring participation, and reviews. Exclude studies of non-political participation (e.g., purely recreational group participation) unless explicitly linked to civic or political engagement.

research_data.desc: Datasets measuring citizens' political and civic activities, turnout, protest behavior and engagement across contexts.
research_data.narr: Include survey datasets (e.g., ESS, CSES, national election studies), panel studies tracking participation over time, protest event datasets with individual respondent modules, youth participation surveys, and program evaluation data on mobilization interventions. Relevant data contain variables on turnout, contacting, protesting, signing petitions, volunteering for political causes, campaign involvement and online political activity. Exclude datasets lacking political activity measures or containing only organizational membership unrelated to politics.

variables.desc: Variables capturing types and frequencies of political participation, intensity, and forms of civic engagement.
variables.narr: Relevant variables include voter turnout, intention to vote, protest attendance, petition signing, contacting public officials, party/campaign volunteering, political donations, membership in political organizations, frequency of civic actions, and composite participation indices. Include variables that distinguish conventional vs. unconventional and offline vs. online participation. Exclude generic social participation variables without a political dimension (e.g., sports club membership) unless explicitly coded as political/civic.

instruments_tools.desc: Survey modules, validated scales and measurement tools used to assess political participation and civic engagement.
instruments_tools.narr: Include standardized questionnaire modules from major surveys (ESS, CSES, ANES, ISSP) measuring participation, indexes and scoring rules, experimental mobilization protocols, coding schemes for protest/event participation, and measurement guides for online political behavior. Include translation notes and administration protocols. Exclude tools that do not measure political activity or that are purely administrative (e.g., voter registration lists) without individual-level participation measures.

publication.desc: Publications on political efficacy, including internal and external efficacy, measurement and effects on political behavior.
publication.narr: Relevant publications present empirical, theoretical or methodological work on citizens' beliefs about their political influence (internal efficacy) and the responsiveness of institutions/authorities (external efficacy), including effects on turnout, participation and trust. Include cross-national comparisons, scale development, and studies linking efficacy to socio-demographic factors. Exclude works that use 'efficacy' in non-political contexts (e.g., medical treatment efficacy) or general self-efficacy unless explicitly connected to political contexts.

research_data.desc: Datasets that include measures of internal and/or external political efficacy or related perceptions of influence and responsiveness.
research_data.narr: Include survey data (e.g., ESS, ANES, CSES) containing standard political efficacy items, panel datasets tracking efficacy over time, and experimental data manipulating perceived efficacy. Relevant datasets provide item-level responses, scale scores and metadata on question wording and translation. Exclude datasets lacking political-efficacy items or containing only generic self-efficacy not tied to political influence.

variables.desc: Variables measuring internal/external political efficacy, perceptions of political influence and institutional responsiveness.
variables.narr: Include variables for internal efficacy (e.g., 'I consider myself well-qualified to participate in politics'), external efficacy (e.g., 'People like me have no say in what the government does'), composite efficacy indices, item-level responses, and coding for directionality and scale. Include information on reverse-coded items and reliability. Exclude variables measuring general self-efficacy, efficacy in non-political domains, or attitudinal items not interpretable as efficacy.

instruments_tools.desc: Question items, scales and measurement protocols for assessing political efficacy and related constructs.
instruments_tools.narr: Include validated efficacy items and scales used in ESS, ANES, CSES and other surveys, scale construction guides, psychometric validation studies, question-wording variants and translation notes, and experimental instruments manipulating perceived efficacy. Exclude instruments measuring non-political efficacy (e.g., health self-efficacy) unless adapted and validated for political contexts.

publication.desc: Publications on political survey research, methodology, results from political opinion surveys and election studies.
publication.narr: Relevant publications include methodological papers on survey design for political research, reports of national and cross-national political surveys, analyses of survey findings on political attitudes, voting behavior and public opinion, and critiques of measurement. Include documentation of major survey projects and peer-reviewed studies using political survey data. Exclude surveys on non-political topics without political modules and opinion pieces lacking empirical survey evidence.

research_data.desc: Political survey datasets such as election studies, public opinion polls and cross-national modules used for political analysis.
research_data.narr: Include datasets from ANES, ESS, CSES, Eurobarometer, ISSP political modules, national election studies, rolling cross-section surveys, and panel surveys with political modules. Relevant data provide questionnaire, codebook, sampling frame, weighting information and response data for political attitudes, voting and behavior. Exclude non-political survey datasets without political content or administrative records without survey methodology.

variables.desc: Variables commonly collected in political surveys: party identification, ideology, voting behavior, policy attitudes and demographic controls.
variables.narr: Include variables for vote choice, past turnout, voting intention, party identification, left-right self-placement, policy preferences, trust in institutions, political interest, media exposure, and standard demographics used in political analysis. Include question wording variants, coding schemes and weights. Exclude variables unrelated to political analysis (e.g., purely behavioral consumer preferences) unless included as covariates in political studies.

instruments_tools.desc: Survey instruments, questionnaires, coding manuals and methodological toolkits for conducting political surveys.
instruments_tools.narr: Include full questionnaires and modules used in major political surveys (ESS, ANES, CSES, Eurobarometer), interviewer instructions, translation/adaptation files, sampling designs, weighting guides, question batteries for measuring ideology, turnout and party ID, and tools for questionnaire programming and fieldwork. Exclude non-survey tools (e.g., purely administrative election returns) and instruments not applicable to political survey research.

publication.desc: Scholarly and popular publications addressing politics in general: comparative and national studies of political systems, government, public policy, political parties, political institutions, public opinion, political theory, political communication and political history. Includes books, journal articles, reports and edited volumes where politics is the main subject.
publication.narr: Relevant items are publications whose primary focus is political phenomena, such as studies of institutions (parliaments, parties), policy analyses, public opinion research, political theory, and political communication. Include works in German or other languages that analyze politics at national, regional or comparative levels. Exclude publications where the term 'politics' appears only metaphorically, marginally, or as a minor subsection of an unrelated topic (e.g., purely administrative reports, corporate governance documents not addressing public politics). Exclude clinical, biological or technical uses of the word that are unrelated to political science.

research_data.desc: Datasets and data collections that document political phenomena: election returns, party manifestos and coding files, public opinion surveys, political elites datasets, legislative roll-call and handbooks, media content datasets and longitudinal studies of politics.
research_data.narr: Include datasets that directly measure political outcomes or inputs (election data, survey modules on political attitudes/behavior, legislative data, manifesto codings, candidate/party databases, political media content). Prefer structured, documented datasets with codebooks. Exclude datasets where political variables are incidental, incomplete, undocumented, or where 'politics' is not a primary domain (e.g., datasets focused exclusively on non-political health measures unless they include substantial political modules). Exclude raw administrative files without documentation linking them to political analysis.

variables.desc: Variables used to measure political phenomena: institutional identifiers (party, legislature), political attitudes (trust, ideology, satisfaction), behavior (turnout, protest participation), socio-political demographics, policy preferences, political knowledge and media exposure indicators.
variables.narr: Relevant variables directly measure political concepts (party ID, vote choice, left–right self-placement, political trust, trust in institutions, turnout, protest participation, policy position items, political knowledge items). Include clearly labeled variable names and detailed coding schemes. Exclude variables whose relation to politics is ambiguous or marginal (e.g., generic income or occupation variables without connection to political analysis) unless accompanied by metadata showing political use.

instruments_tools.desc: Survey instruments, questionnaires, coding manuals and measurement tools designed to capture political constructs: election study questionnaires, public opinion modules, manifestos coding schemes, scales for political trust, efficacy, ideology, and tools for political discourse/content analysis.
instruments_tools.narr: Include validated instruments and toolkits whose stated purpose is to measure political constructs (e.g., election study core questionnaires, public opinion batteries, party manifesto coding manuals, political efficacy and trust scales). Instruments must include item wording, response categories, and scoring or coding guidance. Exclude generic social science instruments with no explicit political content, single-item ad-hoc questions without documentation, or proprietary tools without accessible documentation.

publication.desc: Publications focused on political behavior: voting behavior, electoral choices, political participation (voting, protesting, civic engagement), political socialization, political mobilization, and behavioral responses to campaigns and media.
publication.narr: Include empirical and theoretical works analyzing how individuals or groups behave politically—determinants of turnout, party choice, protest participation, political engagement across contexts. Include event studies, longitudinal analyses, experimental work on behavior, and comparative studies of participation. Exclude publications that discuss political institutions or policy without examining behavioral responses, or studies that treat behavior only as background without data or behavioral measures.

research_data.desc: Datasets documenting political behavior: election studies, panel surveys, turnout records, protest event datasets, civic participation modules in general social surveys, and field experiment datasets measuring behavior changes.
research_data.narr: Include datasets that directly record behavioral outcomes (validated turnout records, self-reported participation, protest attendance, membership/activism indicators, campaign contact experiments). Prefer data with temporal or panel structure to study changes in behavior. Exclude datasets lacking behavioral measures or containing only attitudinal items without behavioral indicators, and administrative records that cannot be linked to political behavior outcomes.

variables.desc: Variables that operationalize political behavior: turnout (actual or intended), vote choice, voter registration, protest participation, membership in political organizations, campaign activity, petition signing, online political activity and civic volunteering.
variables.narr: Relevant variables explicitly measure actions (e.g., 'voted in last election', 'intention to vote', 'participated in demonstration', 'contacted politician', 'donated to campaign'). Include variables with clear temporal reference and coding. Exclude indirect proxies for behavior (e.g., general civic attitudes) unless paired with concrete behavioral items or validated behavioral indicators.

instruments_tools.desc: Measurement instruments and protocols for political behavior: validated turnout and participation survey items, behavioral experiment protocols, observational coding schemes for participation, neighborhood or social-network measurement tools for mobilization.
instruments_tools.narr: Include standardized questionnaires and experiment designs that elicit or measure political behavior (vote intention and verification modules, turnout validation methods, protest participation batteries, mobilization treatment scripts). Instruments should provide item wording, response options and, where applicable, protocols for validation (e.g., matching survey responses to official turnout records). Exclude attitudinal-only instruments or tools lacking operational details to identify behavior.

publication.desc: Research and policy publications on political education/civic education: curricula, classroom interventions, teacher training, program evaluations, theoretical work on civic competence, and comparative studies of civic education systems.
publication.narr: Include evaluations and studies of formal and non-formal political education aimed at developing civic knowledge, skills and dispositions (school curricula, extracurricular programs, teacher guides, policy analyses). Include empirical pre-post assessments and comparative education research (e.g., ICCS-related studies). Exclude general education literature that does not address civic or political learning outcomes, or publications focused solely on administrative aspects without educational content.

research_data.desc: Datasets measuring political/civic education outcomes: school and classroom assessments, program evaluation datasets, ICCS, PISA civics modules, and surveys of teachers and students about civic knowledge and engagement.
research_data.narr: Include datasets containing measures of civic knowledge, civic competence, classroom practices, teacher qualifications, and program participation used to evaluate political education. Prioritize data with item-level test scores and documentation of instruments. Exclude datasets that only list school characteristics without measures of civic education content or learning outcomes.

variables.desc: Variables capturing civic/political education constructs: civic knowledge scores, civic skills (discussion, argumentation), civic attitudes (support for democracy, tolerance), classroom activities, frequency of civics instruction, teacher qualifications, and participation in civic programs.
variables.narr: Relevant variables explicitly measure learning outcomes or educational inputs in political education (e.g., 'civic knowledge test score', 'frequency of classroom discussion on politics', 'teacher received civic training'). Include coding schemes and item wording. Exclude general academic achievement variables unless disaggregated to civic content or tied to civic learning measures.

instruments_tools.desc: Assessment tools and pedagogical instruments for political education: civic knowledge tests, competency frameworks (ICCS, PISA civics), classroom observation protocols, teacher questionnaires, curriculum mapping tools and program evaluation instruments.
instruments_tools.narr: Include validated tests and instruments designed to measure civic knowledge, skills and dispositions (item batteries, scoring rubrics, competency frameworks), as well as curriculum analysis tools and evaluation guides. Instruments should include item wording, scoring instructions and administration protocols. Exclude generic educational assessments without civic-specific content or undocumented ad-hoc quizzes.

publication.desc: Publications examining left–right ideology and political positioning: conceptual discussions of the left–right dimension, empirical studies of self-placement, party position analyses, cleavage research and ideological shifts over time and across countries.
publication.narr: Include works that theorize, measure or analyze the left–right dimension, ideological self-placement, and its relation to party competition, policy preferences or voting behavior. Include cross-national comparisons and studies using manifesto or expert coding to position parties. Exclude publications that use 'left'/'right' metaphorically outside political ideology (e.g., technical or spatial descriptors) or focus on unrelated axes without reference to ideological positioning.

research_data.desc: Datasets containing left–right measures: survey modules with left–right self-placement, party position datasets (e.g., Manifesto Project, CHES), expert surveys, and cross-national datasets linking ideology to behavior.
research_data.narr: Include datasets that contain explicit left–right items (e.g., 0–10 self-placement), party/party family positions on left–right scale, and coding schemes for ideological placement. Prefer resources with documentation on scale construction and comparability. Exclude datasets lacking any ideological measure or those that use left/right as incidental labels without methodological detail.

variables.desc: Variables operationalizing left–right ideology: self-placement scales, ideological distance to parties, party family identifiers, economic/cultural position items, and constructed left–right indices.
variables.narr: Include variables that directly measure ideological orientation (e.g., 'left_right_placement', 'ideological_distance_to_party'), with coding and value labels. Include separate variables capturing economic vs cultural dimensions when available. Exclude vague or indirect proxies for ideology (e.g., single policy preference without context) unless part of an established left–right index.

instruments_tools.desc: Measurement instruments for ideological placement: left–right self-placement items, multi-item ideology scales, party positioning tools (manifesto coding manuals, expert survey instruments), and visual analog scales for ideological mapping.
instruments_tools.narr: Include standardized items and manuals used to measure left–right positioning (item wording for self-placement scales, CHES and Manifesto Project coding instructions, multi-dimensional ideology batteries). Instruments must provide response formats and coding conventions. Exclude informal or one-off items lacking documentation or tools that only infer ideology indirectly without explicit measurement procedures.

publication.desc: Publications on political competence (political literacy, civic competence): theoretical work and empirical studies addressing political knowledge, skills for political participation, decision-making capacity, political efficacy and competencies required for democratic citizenship.
publication.narr: Include research that defines, measures or evaluates political competence/civic competence, including longitudinal and intervention studies, theoretical frameworks, and comparative analyses (e.g., ICCS-related work). Include works linking competence to behavior and democratic outcomes. Exclude publications that use 'competence' in non-political senses (professional competencies unrelated to civic capacities) or studies that only superficially mention competence without conceptual or empirical treatment.

research_data.desc: Datasets measuring political/civic competence: survey batteries and test data with political knowledge items, ICCS, PISA civics data, national assessments of civic competence, and evaluation datasets of competence-building interventions.
research_data.narr: Include datasets that contain item-level political knowledge tests, measures of civic skills (argumentation, critical thinking), efficacy scales and validated composite competence scores. Prefer datasets with documentation and scoring rules. Exclude datasets lacking competence-related items or with only general knowledge measures not tied to political/civic content.

variables.desc: Variables representing political competence: factual political knowledge scores, civic skills indicators, political efficacy, critical thinking in political contexts, problem-solving in civic scenarios, and composite civic competence indices.
variables.narr: Relevant variables explicitly quantify components of political competence (e.g., 'political_knowledge_score', 'civic_efficacy_scale', 'argumentation_skill_item'). Include variables with clear provenance and scoring instructions. Exclude variables that measure unrelated competencies (e.g., general literacy or numeracy) unless linked and validated as part of a civic competence construct.

instruments_tools.desc: Instruments to assess political competence: validated political knowledge question batteries, civic competence frameworks (ICCS, PISA civics), scoring rubrics for civic skills, vignette-based assessment tools and teacher/student questionnaires for competence evaluation.
instruments_tools.narr: Include well-documented instruments designed to measure political/civic competence, providing item wording, administration protocols and scoring rules (e.g., ICCS item banks, PISA civics instruments, political knowledge batteries used in election studies). Exclude ad-hoc quizzes without validation, or instruments that measure only peripheral skills not linked to civic competence.

publication.desc: Publications presenting empirical or theoretical research on individuals' political orientation (e.g., left–right self-placement, partisan identification, ideological location) including cross-national comparisons, longitudinal studies, and conceptual discussions.
publication.narr: Relevant publications report empirical findings or theoretical analyses about political orientation as an attribute of individuals or groups. Included are journal articles, books, reports, and reviews that define, measure, or model political orientation (left–right scales, party attachment, ideological identification), discuss its determinants (socio-demographics, socialization), or analyze consequences (voting, attitudes). Exclude works that use 'orientation' in non-political senses (e.g., policy orientation of institutions without reference to ideology), purely normative political philosophy that does not address orientation as an empirical or measured concept, and publications focusing solely on elite or party platforms without linking to individual orientation.

research_data.desc: Datasets containing measures of political orientation at the individual or group level (e.g., left–right self-placement, party ID, ideological scale items) from surveys, panel studies, or cross-national datasets.
research_data.narr: Relevant datasets include survey modules and panels that collect left–right self-placement, party identification, ideological labels, and related items (e.g., perceived ideological proximity to parties). Include national and cross-national surveys, longitudinal panels, and experimental data where political orientation is a variable or outcome. Exclude datasets that do not contain explicit measures of political orientation, datasets limited to elite manifestos without respondent data, or administrative registers lacking attitudinal indicators.

variables.desc: Variable records that capture measures of political orientation such as left–right scale, self-reported ideology, party identification, and directional/valence ideological indicators.
variables.narr: Relevant variables are those that measure respondents' ideological self-placement (numeric left–right scales, categorical ideology labels), partisan attachment, or items operationalizing orientation (e.g., 'Where would you place yourself on a scale from 1–10?'). Include derived variables (e.g., recoded left/center/right) and contextual variables linking orientation to voting behavior. Exclude variables unrelated to personal ideological placement (e.g., geographic orientation, issue-specific policy preferences unless explicitly used to construct an orientation index).

instruments_tools.desc: Questionnaires, survey modules, coding schemes, and scales designed to measure political orientation, plus documentation for left–right placement items and index construction.
instruments_tools.narr: Relevant instruments include survey questionnaires and module templates including left–right self-placement items, partisan identification questions, ideological ladder items, and validated scales for measuring ideology. Include coding manuals and scoring algorithms for deriving orientation indices. Exclude instruments that do not capture individual political orientation (e.g., party program coding schemes without linkage to voter self-placement) and measurement tools focused exclusively on policy attitudes without orientation constructs.

publication.desc: Publications on political attitudes (politische Einstellung) covering measurement, determinants, structure, and effects of attitudes toward politics, institutions, and policy issues.
publication.narr: Relevant publications empirically or theoretically examine political attitudes at individual or group levels, including attitude formation, stability, and influence on behavior (voting, participation). Include studies addressing general political attitudes (trust in institutions, support for democracy) and specific issue attitudes when tied to broader attitude constructs. Exclude purely philosophical treatments of political doctrines disconnected from empirical attitude research, and works addressing clinical 'attitude' constructs outside political contexts.

research_data.desc: Datasets collecting measures of political attitudes such as trust, support for democracy, policy preferences, institutional evaluations, and related opinion items.
research_data.narr: Relevant datasets contain items measuring respondents' political attitudes (e.g., trust in government, satisfaction with democracy, attitude scales about immigration, welfare), ideally with metadata documenting question wording and response categories. Include cross-sectional surveys, panels, and comparative studies where political attitudes are central. Exclude datasets without political attitude items or those focusing exclusively on non-attitudinal behavioral or administrative records.

variables.desc: Variables representing political attitude items and scales: trust in institutions, support for democracy, policy-specific opinions, and composite attitude indices.
variables.narr: Relevant variables are individual survey items and constructed scales that measure political attitudes, including question wording, response coding, and provenance. Include attitudinal indices aggregated from multiple items and items capturing intensity and direction of opinions. Exclude socio-demographic variables unless they are used as part of an attitude composite or directly measure political opinions.

instruments_tools.desc: Survey questionnaires, attitude batteries, validated scales, and coding guides for measuring political attitudes and indices.
instruments_tools.narr: Relevant instruments include standardized questionnaires and modules for measuring political attitudes (e.g., political trust batteries, democratic support scales, issue opinion items), methodological guides on scale validation and index construction, and translation/adaptation documentation. Exclude instruments unrelated to political opinion measurement (e.g., personality inventories unless explicitly linked to political attitude measurement).

publication.desc: Scholarly works on political participation, covering forms of participation (voting, protest, civic engagement, online participation), causes, consequences, and measurement across contexts.
publication.narr: Relevant publications analyze empirical or theoretical aspects of political participation by individuals, groups, or communities. Include studies on conventional participation (voting, party membership), nonconventional forms (protests, petitions), digital/online participation, and cross-national or longitudinal analyses. Exclude texts focusing solely on administrative processes (e.g., election mechanics) without linking to participation behavior, or normative prescriptions without empirical investigation.

research_data.desc: Datasets recording political participation behaviors and intentions (voter turnout, protest attendance, petition signing, civic engagement metrics), including survey and behavioral data.
research_data.narr: Relevant datasets document measures of political participation at the individual or aggregate level, such as turnout records, self-reported participation, engagement in civic organizations, and online political activity logs. Include longitudinal panels, voter files linked to survey responses, and experimental data on mobilization. Exclude datasets that do not record participation measures or that only include institutional data without behavioral indicators.

variables.desc: Variables that measure types and frequency of political participation: turnout, protest participation, petition signing, membership in political organizations, and online engagement indicators.
variables.narr: Relevant variables capture participation behavior and related motivations (e.g., frequency of protest attendance, past voting in specified elections, membership in civic groups, online political posting). Include variables measuring barriers to participation and mobilization exposure. Exclude variables solely about political attitudes unless they are used as predictors or correlates of participation and are documented as such.

instruments_tools.desc: Survey instruments, turnout modules, civic engagement batteries, experimental protocols, and coding schemes designed to measure political participation and mobilization.
instruments_tools.narr: Relevant instruments include validated survey modules for measuring voting and non-voting participation, protest and petition items, civic engagement indices, field experiment protocols for mobilization, and tools for coding online participation. Include documentation on question wording, sampling, and measurement reliability. Exclude tools unrelated to measuring participation (e.g., institutional procedural manuals without behavioral measures).

publication.desc: Publications on political ideologies covering conceptual frameworks, empirical measurement, ideology content (left/right, libertarian/authoritarian), party-ideology linkages, and historical or comparative analyses.
publication.narr: Relevant works examine political ideologies as coherent belief systems, their dimensions, measurement (scales, content analysis of manifestos), or impacts on politics and behavior. Include comparative studies of dominant ideologies, typologies, and research linking ideology to policy preferences and party systems. Exclude purely philosophical treatises that do not engage with ideology as an empirical or social-scientific concept, and topical studies that mention 'ideology' only tangentially without analysis.

research_data.desc: Datasets that capture ideological beliefs or content, including respondent ideology measures, party manifesto codings, text corpora of ideological materials, and cross-national indicators of ideological dimensions.
research_data.narr: Relevant datasets contain individual-level ideology measures (self-placement, policy clusters), coded party manifestos and speeches (for ideological content), or computational text datasets annotated for ideology. Include longitudinal or comparative datasets mapping ideological change. Exclude datasets lacking ideological indicators or those exclusively about organizational procedures without ideological content.

variables.desc: Variables representing ideological placement, multidimensional ideology scales, issue-based ideology indices, and coded indicators of ideological content from texts or manifestos.
variables.narr: Relevant variables include left–right placement, authoritarian–libertarian scales, constructed ideology indices from issue items, and coded manifesto indicators (e.g., economic or cultural ideology scores). Include metadata on construction and scoring. Exclude vague or incidental mentions of ideology not operationalized as a measurable variable.

instruments_tools.desc: Questionnaire modules, ideology scales, coding manuals for manifesto/text analysis, dictionaries for automated ideological content analysis, and validation studies.
instruments_tools.narr: Relevant instruments include validated scales for measuring ideological dimensions, survey items for ideological self-placement, coding schemes and manuals for party manifestos and speeches, and computational tools (dictionaries, supervised models) for detecting ideological content. Exclude instruments not designed to capture ideological content or those applicable only to non-political contexts.

publication.desc: Publications investigating political values (core normative beliefs about politics such as democratic values, egalitarianism, authority, civil liberties), their measurement, origins, and consequences.
publication.narr: Relevant publications study political values as stable normative orientations shaping political behavior and policy preferences, including cross-cultural comparisons, value change over time, and links to institutions. Include empirical analyses using survey measures (e.g., human values, civic values) and theoretical treatments that operationalize values for research. Exclude philosophical value debates without empirical linkage, or studies of non-political personal values not connected to political attitudes or behavior.

research_data.desc: Datasets containing measures of political and civic values (e.g., items on democratic norms, tolerance, egalitarianism, support for civil liberties, Schwartz values) from surveys and panel studies.
research_data.narr: Relevant datasets include those that record respondents' normative beliefs about politics and society, such as support for democratic procedures, tolerance of dissent, authority acceptance, and equality values. Include cross-national surveys (e.g., World Values Survey), panels, and modules mapping value dimensions. Exclude datasets that do not assess normative or value items or focus solely on descriptive attitudes without normative content.

variables.desc: Variables capturing political values: support for democracy, tolerance, equality preferences, authority orientation, and composite value scales (e.g., civic virtue indices).
variables.narr: Relevant variables are survey items and constructed indices representing political values, including question wording, response coding, and scale construction details. Include variables derived from standard value batteries (e.g., Schwartz, Inglehart) when linked to political outcomes. Exclude socio-demographic or factual knowledge variables unless explicitly used to measure political values.

instruments_tools.desc: Value inventories, survey modules, validated scales, and coding guides for measuring political and civic values, including translation/adaptation notes.
instruments_tools.narr: Relevant instruments include standardized question batteries for assessing political values (tolerance, democratic commitment, equality), psychometric validation studies, and coding manuals for constructing value scales. Include tools for cross-cultural harmonization of value measures. Exclude instruments that measure only personal or occupational values without political relevance.

publication.desc: Scholarly works and reports that analyse citizens' political attitudes, evaluations, and preferences specifically toward Austria's major parties ÖVP and SPÖ, including comparative studies of party support.
publication.narr: Relevant publications include empirical studies, articles, books, and reports that measure or analyse attitudes, party sympathy, favourability, trust, vote intention, or evaluations specifically referencing the Austrian People's Party (ÖVP) and the Social Democratic Party of Austria (SPÖ). Include national and regional analyses, election studies, comparative research where ÖVP or SPÖ are distinct cases, and works addressing changes over time or determinants of attitudes toward these parties. Exclude materials that only discuss abstract or generic 'political attitudes' without specific reference to ÖVP or SPÖ, studies focused on other parties unless ÖVP/SPÖ are one of the main targets, and purely theoretical treatments with no empirical connection to these parties.

research_data.desc: Datasets and survey archives that contain measures of attitudes, party sympathy, vote intention, or evaluations toward ÖVP and SPÖ (e.g., Austrian Election Studies, national surveys, panel data).
research_data.narr: Include datasets with variables that explicitly measure respondents' feelings, confidence, trust, sympathy, likelihood to vote for, or evaluations of ÖVP and/or SPÖ. Accept cross-sectional and panel datasets, election-study data, quota or probability samples, and datasets with regional breakdowns for Austria. Exclude datasets that lack party-specific items, contain only macro-level indicators without party-level measures, or datasets about other countries that do not include Austrian party items.

variables.desc: Variable fields capturing party preference, favourability, vote intention, sympathy, trust, and evaluations specifically for ÖVP and SPÖ.
variables.narr: Relevant variables are those labelled or coded to represent respondents' support, vote choice, likelihood to vote, affective ratings, trust or satisfaction with ÖVP and/or SPÖ. Include numeric and categorical variables (party closeness, feeling thermometer, vote intention, retrospective vote) and panel-derived change measures. Exclude generic ideological variables (left–right) unless they are explicitly linked to measured attitudes toward ÖVP or SPÖ.

instruments_tools.desc: Survey question wordings, interview modules, coding schemes, and experimental instruments designed to elicit attitudes toward ÖVP and SPÖ.
instruments_tools.narr: Include questionnaires, module items, standardized party-evaluation batteries, feeling-thermometer items, vignette texts, experimental manipulations, and coding manuals that explicitly ask about or code responses for ÖVP and SPÖ. Include translation notes where items are in German. Exclude instruments that do not target specific party evaluations or that only measure general political attitudes without party identification.

publication.desc: Research on political interest: conceptual discussions, empirical analyses of levels, determinants, consequences, and trends in citizens' interest in politics.
publication.narr: Relevant publications are empirical and theoretical works that define, measure, or analyze 'political interest' (interest in politics, attention to political news, curiosity about public affairs). Include cross-national comparisons, longitudinal trend studies, psychological and sociological investigations, and research linking political interest to participation, knowledge, or media use. Exclude studies that only address unrelated types of interest (e.g., interest groups) or that mention 'interest' without relation to citizens' attention or engagement with politics.

research_data.desc: Datasets containing measures of political interest, such as survey items on how often respondents follow politics or how interested they are in political affairs (e.g., ISSP, European Social Survey, national surveys).
research_data.narr: Include survey datasets with direct items on political interest (single-item scales, frequency questions, interest indexes), time-use or media-consumption datasets with political attention indicators, and panel data tracking change in interest. Accept datasets from national and international sources and those with demographic covariates. Exclude datasets lacking any measure of respondents' interest in politics or datasets focused solely on organizational interests (e.g., interest group data).

variables.desc: Variables that measure personal interest in politics: interest intensity, frequency of following politics, attention to political news, and composite interest scales.
variables.narr: Relevant variables include single-item measures (e.g., 'How interested are you in politics?'), frequency measures ('How often do you follow political news?'), scale scores combining several items, and items differentiating types of political interest (local, national, policy-specific). Exclude variables with ambiguous labels that do not clearly measure individual political interest (e.g., general curiosity) or variables that measure institutional interest (organizational lobbying).

instruments_tools.desc: Survey question wordings, validated scales and modules used to measure political interest (e.g., ISSP modules, ESS items), and coding guides for interest measures.
instruments_tools.narr: Include standardized item wordings, multi-item scales and scoring instructions, module descriptions from large surveys (ISSP, ESS, Eurobarometer), and interviewer instructions for measuring political interest. Also include experimental prompts or diary instruments that assess attention to politics. Exclude tools that measure only knowledge, efficacy, or participation unless combined with explicit political interest items.

publication.desc: Studies and reports on political engagement and civic participation, covering conventional and non-conventional forms of engagement, volunteering, activism, and mobilization.
publication.narr: Relevant publications empirically or theoretically address individual and collective political engagement: voting, party membership, campaigning, contacting officials, protest, demonstrations, online activism, civic volunteering, and community engagement with political aims. Include determinants, consequences, measurement issues, and subgroup analyses. Exclude works solely about non-political volunteering unrelated to civic or political aims, or organizational reports without empirical measurement of individuals' political engagement.

research_data.desc: Datasets documenting forms and frequency of political engagement, including election studies, participation modules in general social surveys, protest and activism surveys, and administrative records of membership/volunteering.
research_data.narr: Include datasets containing variables for voting turnout, party/union membership, campaigning activity, contacting authorities, protest participation, online political activity, and civic volunteering. Accept cross-sectional, panel, and event datasets (e.g., protest event data) that quantify engagement or track changes. Exclude datasets that only contain macro-level indicators of civic organizations without individual-level engagement measures.

variables.desc: Variables capturing types and intensity of political engagement: turnout, membership, campaigning, contacting, protest participation, volunteering, and online activism measures.
variables.narr: Relevant variables are those recording whether and how often respondents engaged in political acts (binary and frequency measures), composite participation indices, measures of intensity or sustained engagement, and items distinguishing conventional vs. non-conventional actions. Include demographic and attitudinal covariates when linked to engagement items. Exclude variables that only measure passive attitudes (e.g., support for protests) without reported behaviour.

instruments_tools.desc: Question batteries, survey modules, validated participation scales, protest/event coding protocols, and measurement tools used to assess political engagement.
instruments_tools.narr: Include standard survey instruments (participation batteries in ESS, CSES, national election studies), coding schemes for protest involvement, diaries and online-activity trackers for digital engagement, and scoring instructions for participation indices. Also include experimental instruments aimed at mobilization. Exclude tools that measure organizational capacity without individual engagement items.

publication.desc: Research that examines both political behaviour (e.g., voting, turnout, contact, protest) and political attitudes (ideology, issue positions, party evaluations) and, importantly, their interrelationship.
publication.narr: Include empirical studies, theoretical work, and meta-analyses that measure political behaviour and political attitudes and explore causal or correlational links between them (e.g., how attitudes predict vote choice, how behaviour shapes attitudes over time). Accept election studies, longitudinal panel research, experimental studies on attitude-behaviour change, and comparative analyses. Exclude works that address only behaviour or only attitudes without explicitly linking the two, or studies focused on organizational behaviour unrelated to citizen-level political attitudes.

research_data.desc: Datasets that contain both behavioural measures (vote, turnout, protest, contacting) and attitudinal measures (ideology, issue preferences, efficacy), suitable for analysing their relationship (e.g., panel election studies, ESS, CSES).
research_data.narr: Relevant datasets include those with matched measures of attitudes and reported behaviours, panel data permitting temporal ordering, and combined survey–administrative datasets (e.g., validated turnout). Include data enabling causal inferences where possible (panels, experiments). Exclude datasets that provide only attitudinal items or only behaviour measures without overlap.

variables.desc: Pairs of variables measuring political attitudes (ideology, policy positions, party evaluations, efficacy) and political behaviour (vote choice, turnout, contacting, protest participation) allowing joint analysis.
variables.narr: Include variables for ideological self-placement, issue stances, party identification, political interest, and efficacy along with behavioural measures such as past vote, intended vote, turnout, contact with officials, and protest participation. Variables should be clearly defined and temporally linked where possible (e.g., pre- and post-election). Exclude variables that are only loosely related or that cannot be validly linked across respondents (e.g., aggregate-level attitudes without individual behavioural measures).

instruments_tools.desc: Survey modules, question batteries, validated scales, experimental protocols, and coding manuals that measure both political attitudes and political behaviour and facilitate analysis of their relationship.
instruments_tools.narr: Include combined questionnaires (attitude batteries plus participation items), validated scales for ideology and efficacy, turnout measurement protocols (self-report vs validated), and experimental vignettes manipulating attitudes to observe behavioural intent. Also include longitudinal instrument designs that permit panel comparisons. Exclude instruments that capture only one domain (attitude or behaviour) without tools to link them at the respondent level.

publication.desc: Works studying the concept, measurement, causes, and effects of citizens' political interest and attention to political life.
publication.narr: Relevant publications are those that explicitly define or measure 'political interest' — including its antecedents (education, media use, social capital), consequences (participation, knowledge), and temporal or cross-national variation. Include qualitative and quantitative studies, literature reviews, and measurement-focused articles. Exclude publications that use the term 'interest' in other contexts (e.g., vested interests, interest groups) without reference to individual political attention or curiosity.

research_data.desc: Survey and observational datasets containing direct measures of political interest or attention (e.g., frequency of following politics, self-rated interest), suitable for analysis of correlates and outcomes.
research_data.narr: Include national and cross-national surveys (ESS, ISSP, Eurobarometer), longitudinal panels, and specialized media-attention datasets with explicit political-interest items. Datasets should permit linking interest to demographic, attitudinal, or behavioural variables. Exclude datasets without any measure of individual political interest or that only capture organizational or elite-level interests.

variables.desc: Variables denoting self-reported interest in politics, frequency of following political news, attention to public affairs, and composite interest indices.
variables.narr: Relevant variables are explicitly labelled as measuring 'political interest' or clearly operationalize the concept (e.g., 'How interested would you say you are in politics?' or 'How often do you follow news about politics?'). Include both single-item and multi-item measures and distinctions between local/national/global political interest. Exclude indirect proxies (e.g., knowledge) unless accompanied by explicit interest items.

instruments_tools.desc: Question wordings, validated scales, survey modules, and measurement protocols for assessing political interest and attention.
instruments_tools.narr: Include standardized items (from ISSP, ESS, national surveys), multi-item scales, interviewer instructions, diary or media-use instruments that record political attention, and experimental measures manipulating salience to measure changes in interest. Exclude instruments that only measure political knowledge, efficacy, or participation without direct items on interest.

publication.desc: Publications that analyze political knowledge (politisches Wissen) including its measurement, determinants, consequences, and cross-national comparisons in political behavior and civic education literatures.
publication.narr: Include studies, review articles, and book chapters that define or measure political knowledge (factual/cognitive knowledge about institutions, parties, policy), explore predictors (education, media use) or outcomes (political participation, vote choice), or validate political knowledge batteries; include national and comparative empirical analyses. Exclude works that only mention 'knowledge' in a non-political context (e.g., technical knowledge unrelated to politics), pedagogical materials without empirical evaluation, or purely philosophical discussions of knowledge that do not address political knowledge measurement or effects.

research_data.desc: Survey datasets and study modules that contain measures of political knowledge or cognitive factual items (e.g., national election studies, cross-national surveys and panel data with political knowledge batteries).
research_data.narr: Include datasets with item-level political knowledge questions or composite indices (factual questions about institutions, party positions, office-holders, policy facts), such as national election studies, ESS/CSES modules, ALLBUS or GLES modules, and longitudinal surveys that track political knowledge over time. Exclude datasets that only contain broad political interest/efficacy items without factual knowledge measures, administrative records unrelated to respondents' political knowledge, or datasets where 'knowledge' refers to non-political domains.

variables.desc: Variables operationalizing political knowledge: individual factual items (e.g., name the head of government), scored indices (number correct), topic-specific knowledge measures, and confidence/subjective political knowledge items.
variables.narr: Include variable names and coding for item-level political knowledge questions, composite scores (sum or percentage correct), indicators of subjective political knowledge/confidence, and metadata about question wording and correct answers. Exclude general political attitudes (interest, trust) or cognitive ability measures unless explicitly used as proxies for political knowledge.

instruments_tools.desc: Questionnaire modules, cognitive item batteries and tests used to measure political knowledge, and coding guides for scoring factual knowledge items.
instruments_tools.narr: Include validated political knowledge batteries, survey question wordings, interviewer instructions, answer keys, and methodological notes on question design (open vs. multiple-choice), item difficulty, and scoring. Exclude educational curricula, teaching guides without standardized measurement instruments, or tools that assess non-political factual knowledge only.

publication.desc: Scholarly works on populism as a political ideology, movement, or strategy including theoretical treatments, case studies, comparative analyses, and measurement debates.
publication.narr: Include theoretical articles defining populism (e.g., people-centrism, anti-elitism), empirical studies of populist parties/movements, comparative research on causes and consequences of populism, and methodological papers on measuring populism. Exclude publications that use 'populism' only as a vague rhetorical label without analytical treatment, media opinion pieces lacking scholarly analysis, or studies of unrelated political phenomena that do not engage with populism concepts or measures.

research_data.desc: Datasets that enable analysis of populism at individual, party, or media levels, including survey modules on populist attitudes and datasets coding party rhetoric or party typologies.
research_data.narr: Include survey data with populism-related items (individual attitudes, anti-elitism, people-centrism), party-level datasets classifying parties as populist, content-analysed corpora of political speeches/media, and election studies that permit populism analysis. Exclude datasets that mention protest or dissatisfaction without measures linking to populist ideology, or administrative data with no content on attitudes or party positions relevant to populism.

variables.desc: Variables measuring populism-related constructs: populist attitudes (anti-elitism, people-centrism), party classifications, indicators of populist rhetoric, and related constructs (authoritarianism, nativism) when used in populism research.
variables.narr: Include item-level variables and scales capturing core dimensions of populism (anti-elitism, people vs elite, demand for popular sovereignty), party-level flags or continuous scores for populist orientation, and content-coded indicators of populist messages. Exclude standalone variables about economic policy or voter demographics unless explicitly linked to operationalizations of populism in the dataset.

instruments_tools.desc: Measurement instruments and coding schemes for populism: survey scales (e.g., Populist Attitudes Scales), party coding manuals, and content-analysis protocols for identifying populist rhetoric.
instruments_tools.narr: Include validated scales and their questionnaires, translations, scoring rules, coding schemes for party classification, and manuals for coding speeches or media as populist. Exclude informal lists of populist parties without coding criteria, or journalistic lists of populist actors that lack a reproducible measurement instrument.

publication.desc: Empirical and theoretical publications focused specifically on populist attitudes at the individual level: development, measurement, correlates, and political consequences.
publication.narr: Include articles validating populist attitudes scales, studies linking populist attitudes to voting behavior or policy preferences, cross-national comparisons of populist attitudes, and longitudinal analyses of attitude change. Exclude works treating populism only as a party attribute, papers that discuss elite or organizational populism without measuring individual attitudes, or opinion pieces without empirical measurement.

research_data.desc: Survey datasets containing individual-level items or composite scales measuring populist attitudes (anti-elitism, people-centrism, Manicheanism), often as dedicated modules or items in comparative surveys.
research_data.narr: Include datasets with item-level populist attitudes measures (e.g., PAS items, CSES/ESS modules), data documentation with question texts and response coding, and cross-national survey batteries designed to capture populist attitudes. Exclude datasets that only provide party-level indicators or single-item measures of general distrust without items explicitly capturing core dimensions of populist attitudes.

variables.desc: Variables operationalizing populist attitudes: item-level responses for anti-elitism, people-centrism, homogeneous 'the people' constructs, Manichean worldviews, and created composite scores/indices.
variables.narr: Include variable labels, question wording, coding (response scales), and construction details for composite scores measuring populist attitudes; include information on reliability and factor structure where available. Exclude variables that measure political distrust or anti-system sentiment alone unless explicitly used as components in a validated populist attitudes construct.

instruments_tools.desc: Validated survey scales and measurement tools for individual-level populist attitudes, coding guides, and translation notes (e.g., Populist Attitudes Scale and comparable instruments).
instruments_tools.narr: Include complete instrument texts, recommended items for each populism dimension, scoring instructions, psychometric evaluations, and cross-cultural adaptation notes. Exclude ad-hoc single items lacking validation or instruments that measure unrelated constructs (e.g., general political cynicism) without mapping to populist attitudes dimensions.

publication.desc: Publications on mental health (psychische Gesundheit) covering prevalence, determinants, outcomes, treatment, and public health interventions in clinical and population contexts.
publication.narr: Include epidemiological studies, clinical research, health services research, and policy evaluations that address mental health status, risk factors, comorbidity, wellbeing, and intervention effectiveness; include German- and international-focused studies when relevant. Exclude publications that only mention mental health tangentially (e.g., as a minor control variable) or solely focus on physical health without linking to mental health outcomes.

research_data.desc: Health survey datasets and epidemiological studies containing validated measures of mental health and wellbeing (e.g., DEGS, GEDA, SOEP, SHARE, EHIS), clinical registries and cohort studies with mental health measures.
research_data.narr: Include datasets with standardized mental health instruments (PHQ, GHQ, WHO-5, CES-D, SF-12/36), diagnostic modules, longitudinal cohort data on mental health trajectories, and administrative health records with mental health diagnoses. Exclude datasets that do not contain any mental health variables or only include non-validated single-item mood questions without context.

variables.desc: Variables describing mental health status and wellbeing: symptom scales (depression, anxiety), subjective wellbeing measures, mental health diagnoses, treatment utilization, and functional impairment indicators.
variables.narr: Include item-level responses and composite scores for commonly used instruments (PHQ-9, GAD-7, GHQ-12, WHO-5, CES-D, SF mental component), coded diagnosis variables (ICD codes), service use variables (therapy, medication), onset and duration measures, and sociodemographic covariates relevant to mental health. Exclude physiological measures that do not assess mental states, or variables that only tangentially relate to mental health (e.g., general life satisfaction without mental health linkage) unless explicitly used as mental health indicators.

instruments_tools.desc: Validated screening and diagnostic instruments for mental health assessment: self-report scales (PHQ-9, GAD-7, GHQ-12, WHO-5, CES-D), diagnostic interviews (CIDI, SCID), and recommended survey modules for population studies.
instruments_tools.narr: Include full questionnaires, scoring guidelines, cut-off values, translation/validation information for German contexts, and interviewer manuals for diagnostic interviews. Exclude non-validated checklists, lay screening apps without validation, or instruments focused only on physical health without mental health subscales.

publication.desc: Scholarly and clinical publications on mental disorders (psychische Krankheiten): epidemiology, diagnosis, treatment, burden of disease, and health services research.
publication.narr: Include peer-reviewed epidemiological studies on prevalence and incidence of psychiatric disorders, clinical trials, diagnostic research, health policy analyses addressing mental disorder treatment and access, and reviews on specific disorders (depression, anxiety, psychosis, bipolar disorder).
