Exclude publications that use the term metaphorically or refer to non-clinical distress without diagnostic framing, and exclude non-scientific commentary lacking empirical data.

research_data.desc: Datasets and registries containing diagnostic information on mental disorders: epidemiological surveys with diagnostic modules (CIDI), clinical registries, hospital discharge data, insurance claims with ICD-10 F-codes, and psychiatric cohort studies.
research_data.narr: Include datasets with clinician- or instrument-assessed diagnoses (ICD/DSM codes), structured diagnostic interview data, treatment and hospitalization records, and longitudinal clinical cohorts documenting onset, course, and outcomes of psychiatric disorders. Exclude general health surveys without diagnostic measures, datasets that only record symptom levels without diagnostic mapping when diagnosis is required, or administrative data lacking reliable mental health coding.

variables.desc: Variables capturing diagnosed mental disorders, diagnostic codes (ICD-10/DSM), symptom counts, severity ratings, comorbidity, duration, age at onset, and treatment indicators.
variables.narr: Include variables for specific disorder diagnoses (F-codes), structured interview diagnoses, symptom scales mapped to diagnostic thresholds, measures of disorder severity and functional impairment, and treatment/utilization variables. Exclude non-specific distress measures unless explicitly linked to diagnostic criteria, and exclude variables that denote only family history without respondent diagnosis unless relevant to study aims.

instruments_tools.desc: Diagnostic instruments and clinical assessment tools for psychiatric disorders: structured interviews (CIDI, SCID, MINI), disorder-specific scales (MADRS, PANSS), and coding manuals for ICD/DSM diagnoses.
instruments_tools.narr: Include validated diagnostic interviews, clinician-rated and self-report disorder-specific scales, scoring rules, thresholds for caseness, and translation/validation materials for use in German-speaking populations. Exclude informal checklists, unvalidated symptom inventories, or tools designed solely for non-clinical wellbeing screening without diagnostic applicability.

publication.desc: Scholarly publications addressing human psychological needs, their theories (e.g., self-determination theory), empirical studies of need satisfaction/frustration, and interventions targeting psychological needs.
publication.narr: Relevant publications will focus on definitions, measurement, development, or effects of psychological needs (e.g., autonomy, competence, relatedness); theoretical frameworks (SDT, need theory), clinical or educational interventions to enhance needs, and population studies reporting need-related outcomes. Exclude papers that only mention 'needs' tangentially (e.g., basic needs in economics without psychological framing), non-psychological basic needs (food, shelter) unless linked to psychological need constructs, and purely physiological or neurological studies that do not relate findings to psychological need concepts.

research_data.desc: Datasets and empirical data collections measuring psychological needs, need satisfaction/frustration, or variables tied to need theories in surveys, experiments, longitudinal or intervention studies.
research_data.narr: Include datasets containing validated measures of psychological needs (e.g., Basic Psychological Need Satisfaction and Frustration Scale, autonomy/competence/relatedness items), longitudinal panels tracking need-related trajectories, experimental/intervention trial data evaluating changes in needs, and cross-cultural datasets with need measures. Exclude datasets lacking psychological-need measures, administrative data unrelated to psychological constructs, or datasets that only record generic 'needs' without psychometric anchors.

variables.desc: Variables operationalizing psychological needs and closely related constructs: autonomy, competence, relatedness, need satisfaction, need frustration, intrinsic motivation, psychological well‑being linked to needs.
variables.narr: Relevant variables include scale scores and items for autonomy, competence, relatedness; composite need satisfaction/frustration indices; motivation types (intrinsic/extrinsic) when used to test need hypotheses; and outcome variables directly tied to needs (well‑being, engagement, mental health) measured in the same study. Exclude variables that only refer to non-psychological 'needs' (e.g., material needs, food insecurity) unless explicitly tied to psychological constructs.

instruments_tools.desc: Validated instruments and assessment tools for measuring psychological needs and related constructs: questionnaires, interview guides, experimental manipulations, and coding schemes.
instruments_tools.narr: Include instruments such as the Basic Psychological Need Satisfaction and Frustration Scale (BPNSFS), Basic Psychological Needs Scale (BPNS), Need Satisfaction scales, vignettes or experimental protocols designed to manipulate autonomy/competence/relatedness, and structured interview guides for need assessment. Exclude ad hoc single-item mentions without validation, tools measuring only general well‑being without explicit need components, and physiological instruments with no linkage to psychological need measures.

publication.desc: Publications on assessment, measurement, improvement, and determinants of health care quality including safety, effectiveness, patient-centeredness, timeliness, efficiency and equity.
publication.narr: Include systematic reviews, empirical studies, policy analyses, and theoretical papers that define, measure, compare, or attempt to improve health care quality (clinical outcomes, process indicators, patient experience, safety incidents, access and equity). Exclude works that focus exclusively on basic biomedical research unrelated to delivery of care, papers only about health care financing without quality outcomes, or informal commentary lacking empirical or methodological substance.

research_data.desc: Datasets related to health care quality: clinical outcomes, hospital performance metrics, patient satisfaction surveys, quality indicators, audits, accreditation data, and administrative records used to study quality.
research_data.narr: Relevant data include patient-level clinical outcomes (mortality, readmission), process measures (guideline adherence), safety incident reports, HCAHPS or equivalent patient experience surveys, hospital/provider performance registries, and datasets enabling quality comparisons over time or between providers. Exclude data that do not include quality-related indicators (purely cost data without quality measures), or health surveys lacking health care utilization or quality variables.

variables.desc: Variables capturing dimensions of health care quality: outcome, process, patient experience, safety, access, timeliness, efficiency and equity indicators.
variables.narr: Include mortality rates, readmission rates, complication/infection rates, adherence to clinical guidelines, waiting times, patient satisfaction scores, safety incident counts, preventable admission rates, equity stratifiers (socioeconomic status, ethnicity) when used to assess quality. Exclude purely biomedical test results not interpreted as care quality, or administrative identifiers with no link to quality measurement.

instruments_tools.desc: Measurement instruments and tools for assessing health care quality: standardized surveys, clinical audit tools, quality indicators/scorecards, accreditation standards and measurement protocols.
instruments_tools.narr: Include instruments such as HCAHPS (or national equivalents), WHO quality of care frameworks and tools, clinical audit checklists, patient safety incident reporting systems, Lean/Six Sigma protocols adapted for health care, and validated quality indicator sets. Exclude non-validated checklists or opinion-based tools with no documentation, and instruments that measure only cost or utilization without quality content.

publication.desc: Scholarly and policy publications concerning refugees and forced migrants: protection, health, integration, legal status, experiences of displacement, and related social, economic, and mental health outcomes.
publication.narr: Relevant publications address refugees, asylum seekers, and forced displacement (vs. voluntary migrants), covering legal/policy analysis, epidemiology, healthcare access, psychosocial outcomes, resettlement/integration, education, and livelihoods. Exclude studies focused solely on general migration without distinguishing forced migration, internal migration without cross-border displacement unless framed as forced displacement, and non-empirical anecdotes without systematic analysis.

research_data.desc: Datasets on refugee populations: registration data, surveys, longitudinal cohorts, health assessments, service utilisation records, and qualitative data collections specific to refugees/asylum seekers.
research_data.narr: Include population registers, UNHCR/refugee agency datasets, health screening datasets for refugees, survey data on integration/employment/education, longitudinal studies tracking refugee outcomes, and qualitative interview collections describing refugee experiences. Exclude datasets on general migrants where refugee status cannot be determined, aggregated country-level migration statistics without refugee-specific variables, or purely theoretical model outputs with no empirical refugee data.

variables.desc: Variables relevant to refugee research: legal status (refugee/asylum seeker), country of origin, reason for flight, date of arrival, living conditions, housing, employment, language proficiency, health status, trauma exposure, and access to services.
variables.narr: Include variables that identify forced migration status (asylum/refugee), pre- and post-migration exposures (trauma, persecution), demographic and socioeconomic markers, health and mental health measures, service utilisation, legal outcomes (asylum decision), and integration indicators (employment, education, language). Exclude generic migration variables that do not distinguish voluntary vs forced migration, or variables unrelated to living conditions and outcomes of refugees.

instruments_tools.desc: Assessment tools and instruments used with refugees: screening instruments for physical and mental health, trauma/PTSD scales, needs assessments, resettlement questionnaires, and cultural adaptation protocols.
instruments_tools.narr: Include tools validated or widely used with refugee populations such as the Harvard Trauma Questionnaire, Refugee Health Screener (RHS-15), PTSD Checklist (PCL), WHO-5/WHOQOL modules adapted for refugees, needs assessment templates, and translated structured interview guides. Exclude general population tools without evidence of suitability or adaptation for refugees, and administrative forms that only record registration without health or psychosocial content.

publication.desc: Academic and policy works on religion: beliefs, practices, institutions, religiosity, secularization, interfaith relations, and the social, political and psychological roles of religion.
publication.narr: Include sociology, anthropology, psychology, history, and political science studies that analyze religious affiliation, practice (attendance, rituals), belief systems, church/state relations, religion's effects on behavior or well‑being, and comparative studies across faiths. Exclude purely theological exegesis not addressing empirical or social dimensions, corporate or organizational uses of 'religion' as metaphor without substantive religious content, or works that only incidentally mention religion.

research_data.desc: Datasets containing religion-related variables: surveys and studies measuring affiliation, attendance, beliefs, practices, and the social effects of religion (e.g., EVS, WVS, ESS modules).
research_data.narr: Include cross-national surveys (World Values Survey, European Values Study), national religion modules, church membership and attendance registers, longitudinal panels with religiosity measures, and qualitative interview datasets exploring religious life. Exclude datasets lacking religion/religiosity variables, or data on unrelated organizational 'religions' (e.g., workplace cultures) that do not measure faith or belief.

variables.desc: Variables that operationalize religion and religiosity: religious affiliation/denomination, frequency of attendance, private practice (prayer), belief in God, religiosity scales, religious salience, and church membership.
variables.narr: Relevant variables include denomination, frequency of religious service attendance, private prayer frequency, belief statements (existence of God), intrinsic/extrinsic religiosity scores, importance of religion, and measures of religious practice or identity. Exclude variables that nominally reference 'religion' but measure unrelated constructs (e.g., cultural festivals referenced without personal religiosity), or variables on spirituality/worldview without explicit mapping to religion unless both are included and labeled.

instruments_tools.desc: Measurement instruments for studying religion: questionnaires, validated religiosity scales, interview schedules, and coding schemes for religious content.
instruments_tools.narr: Include tools such as Religious Commitment Inventory, Duke University Religion Index (DUREL), Intrinsic/Extrinsic Religious Orientation scales, religion modules from EVS/WVS/ESS, structured interview guides on belief and practice, and coding frameworks for religious affiliation. Exclude ad hoc single-item mentions of religion without validated instrument context, and measures that conflate spirituality, secular values or political ideology without clear religious constructs.

publication.desc: Publications addressing religion and weltanschauung (worldview/life stance): comparative studies of religious and non-religious worldviews, secular philosophies, life stances, ethics, and public expressions of worldview.
publication.narr: Include studies that examine both religion and weltanschauung/life stance (Weltanschauung), comparative analyses of religious beliefs and secular worldviews, legal and institutional treatment of worldviews, and measures of worldview identity and values. Exclude works only about religion without reference to worldview concepts when the query intends both, purely theological texts not engaging with 'weltanschauung', and philosophical treatises unrelated to social or empirical aspects of worldviews.

research_data.desc: Datasets covering religion and worldviews: surveys and studies that capture religious affiliation alongside worldview/life stance variables (secularism, humanism, philosophical beliefs), church-state relations and worldview policies.
research_data.narr: Include datasets with items on religious affiliation and non-religious worldviews (humanism, secular worldview, other life stances), measures of worldview importance, legal status of worldviews, and attitudes toward religion and secularism. Exclude datasets that record only formal religious affiliation without any measures of worldview or life stance, and data from unrelated cultural or philosophical studies without empirical worldview indicators.

variables.desc: Variables representing religious and worldview constructs: denomination, belief statements, secular/non-religious life stance (e.g., humanism), importance of worldview, ethical orientation, and institutional membership (church, Weltanschauung communities).
variables.narr: Relevant variables include religious affiliation and denomination, self-identified weltanschauung or life stance (e.g., atheist, agnostic, humanist), importance of worldview in life, ritual/practice frequency, membership in worldview organizations, and attitudes toward church/state differentiation. Exclude variables that only capture cultural tradition names without respondent‑level worldview identification, or abstract philosophical variables not linked to respondents' self‑described life stance.

instruments_tools.desc: Instruments for measuring religion and worldviews: survey modules, scales and interview guides that distinguish religious belief/practice and secular/worldview positions, and coding schemes for life stance classification.
instruments_tools.narr: Include EVS/WVS/ESS modules that have religion and worldview items, bespoke questionnaires distinguishing worldview/life stance categories, validated scales for religiosity and secular orientation, and interview protocols for exploring personal weltanschauung. Exclude instruments that only measure religiosity without any option for non-religious worldviews, or philosophical inventories not adapted for empirical social research on life stances.

publication.desc: Publications (articles, books, reports) addressing religion, religiosity, beliefs, and values, especially in German-speaking contexts or comparative studies including Germany.
publication.narr: Relevant publications are scholarly works that study religious affiliation, practices, beliefs, church attendance, personal and social values (e.g. moral values, value orientations like Schwartz values), religion's role in social or political attitudes, secularization, and religion–value relations. Include empirical studies, theoretical treatments, reviews, and comparative research that explicitly focus on religion and value systems, or include quantitative or qualitative analyses of values tied to religious variables. Prefer works in German or studies that analyze German-speaking samples. Non-relevant items are publications that only mention religion or values tangentially (e.g., passing reference without empirical/theoretical focus), purely theological texts unrelated to social-scientific study, popular press pieces, or materials focused exclusively on unrelated topics (e.g., ritual studies with no value or attitudinal component).

research_data.desc: Datasets and study collections measuring religiosity, religious affiliation, belief, practice, and value orientations (including German or comparative European surveys).
research_data.narr: Relevant data are survey datasets, longitudinal studies, and cross-national data that contain variables on religious affiliation, frequency of practice, importance of religion, belief, spiritual practices, and measures of personal or social values (e.g. Schwartz value items, moral value scales). Include data from national surveys, church-research datasets, EVS/WVS, Eurobarometer modules, and German panel studies with religion/value items. Exclude datasets that do not include any religion- or value-related variables, administrative records with only institutional details, or exclusively theological source data without social-science measures.

variables.desc: Variable descriptions and codebooks for measures of religiosity, religious affiliation, belief, and value orientations (Schwartz, moral value items, civic/religious values).
variables.narr: Relevant variables are those that capture religious denomination, frequency of worship, religious belief/importance, prayer, religiosity scales, and specific value items or scales (e.g. Schwartz value dimensions, moral foundations, tradition vs. autonomy). Include variable metadata, coding schemes, and derived indices linking religion and value constructs. Non-relevant variables include administrative identifiers, unrelated demographic variables unless clearly used as controls, or variables about religion that are ambiguous or not operationalized (e.g. a single unclear text field without coding).

instruments_tools.desc: Validated questionnaires, scales and measurement instruments assessing religiosity and value orientations, including German-language translations and modules used in large surveys.
instruments_tools.narr: Relevant instruments include validated scales and questionnaires for measuring religiosity (e.g. Centrality of Religiosity Scale, church attendance items), value inventories (e.g. Schwartz Value Survey, Portrait Values Questionnaire), moral values scales, and survey modules used in EVS/WVS with German versions. Include translation documentation, reliability/validity information, and administration guidelines. Exclude instruments that are purely theological liturgy tools, clinical diagnostic instruments unrelated to values, or unvalidated ad-hoc items without measurement information.

publication.desc: Scholarly publications about schools, schooling, educational processes and outcomes at primary and secondary levels, with emphasis on German educational contexts.
publication.narr: Relevant publications examine school systems, teaching and learning, classroom practices, school organization, school effectiveness, student outcomes (achievement, attainment), school transition, tracking, inclusive education, and policy studies focused on primary and secondary schools. Include empirical studies, program evaluations, comparative education research, and reports on German schools or German-speaking regions. Exclude items focused exclusively on higher education/university, early childhood (unless explicitly linked to school entry), vocational training outside the school context, or non-educational uses of the word 'school' (e.g. schools of thought) without relation to formal schooling.

research_data.desc: Datasets pertaining to schooling: student assessments, school surveys, administrative school records, and panel studies tracking pupils in primary/secondary education.
research_data.narr: Relevant data include large-scale assessments (PISA, TIMSS, PIRLS), national student assessments, school-level administrative data (enrollment, attainment, class size), teacher and school leader surveys, longitudinal cohort data following students through school, and intervention evaluation datasets. Include data describing school type, curricula, SES composition, teacher qualifications, and student achievement. Exclude datasets limited to tertiary education, workplace training, or datasets lacking any school-related variables.

variables.desc: Variables and codebooks capturing school-related constructs: school type, grade level, achievement scores, attendance, tracking, teacher characteristics, and school climate indicators.
variables.narr: Relevant variables measure school enrollment, grade/age, school sector/type (public/private/tracking streams), standardized test scores, class size, teacher qualifications, pupil–teacher ratio, absenteeism, disciplinary incidents, school climate and resources. Include variables used as outcomes (achievement) and predictors (school SES, school policies). Exclude variables unrelated to schooling (e.g. adult workplace variables) or those that cannot be mapped to school contexts (e.g. generic organization codes without school labeling).

instruments_tools.desc: Assessment instruments, teacher questionnaires, school climate scales, and survey modules designed for school research and evaluations (including German versions).
instruments_tools.narr: Relevant instruments include standardized achievement tests, classroom observation protocols, teacher self-report scales, school climate instruments, student engagement and motivation questionnaires, and validated measurement tools used in PISA/TIMSS/PIRLS. Include administration manuals, scoring rules, and translated German instruments. Exclude instruments intended solely for higher education, clinical diagnostic tools not adapted to school settings, or informal checklists lacking validation.

publication.desc: Publications about self-esteem that are written in German or focus on German-speaking samples, addressing theory, measurement, development, correlates, and outcomes of self-esteem.
publication.narr: Relevant publications are empirical studies, reviews, and theoretical pieces examining global and domain-specific self-esteem, its antecedents and consequences, and validation of German translations of self-esteem scales. Include work on adolescent and adult self-esteem in German samples, cross-cultural comparisons involving German versions, and psychometric analyses of German instruments. Exclude publications that only mention self-esteem peripherally, non-scientific articles, or studies focusing on unrelated constructs without reference to self-esteem.

research_data.desc: Datasets measuring self-esteem in German-speaking populations, including surveys and longitudinal studies that include validated German self-esteem scales.
research_data.narr: Relevant data contain self-esteem measures (e.g. Rosenberg Self-Esteem Scale German translation, domain-specific self-worth scales) collected in Germany, Austria, Switzerland, or German-speaking subsamples of international studies. Include datasets with item-level responses, scale scores, and metadata on translation and psychometrics. Exclude datasets lacking any self-esteem variables, or datasets where 'self esteem' is not clearly operationalized or measured in German.

variables.desc: Variables and codebooks for self-esteem measures in German, including item-level responses, composite scores, and scoring instructions for German translations of standard scales.
variables.narr: Relevant variables are item responses and computed scores from validated German self-esteem instruments (e.g. German Rosenberg items, single-item self-esteem measures labeled in German, domain-specific self-concept scales), and metadata on reverse-scoring and reliability. Include variables indicating scale version, language, and sample. Exclude ambiguous items not clearly labeled as self-esteem, or variables from non-German instruments without translated equivalents.

instruments_tools.desc: Validated self-esteem instruments and measurement tools in German, including translations (Rosenberg Self-Esteem Scale German version), manuals, and psychometric documentation.
instruments_tools.narr: Relevant instruments include established self-esteem scales available in German (e.g. Rosenberg Self-Esteem Scale German translation, Multidimensional Self-Esteem Inventory adaptations, single-item measures where validated), administration instructions, scoring keys, and validation studies in German samples. Include psychometric properties and translation/back-translation documentation. Exclude unvalidated ad-hoc self-worth items, instruments in other languages without documented German translation, or clinical assessments not intended to measure general self-esteem.

publication.desc: Scholarly works on self-determination, autonomy, and Self-Determination Theory (SDT), including theoretical, empirical, and applied research across contexts.
publication.narr: Relevant publications discuss self-determination as a psychological construct (autonomy, competence, relatedness), Self-Determination Theory research, motivation, volition, self-regulation, and autonomy-supportive contexts in education, work, health, or social domains. Include validation studies of SDT constructs, interventions to enhance autonomy, and cross-cultural examinations. Exclude papers using 'self-determination' in unrelated legal/medical contexts (e.g. advance directives) unless they address psychological autonomy or motivation explicitly.

research_data.desc: Datasets containing measures of self-determination, autonomy, basic psychological needs, and related motivational constructs from experimental, longitudinal, or survey studies.
research_data.narr: Relevant datasets include those with scales for autonomy, competence, relatedness, causality orientations, intrinsic/extrinsic motivation measures, or SDT-based intervention outcomes. Include data from educational, occupational, clinical, and community samples where self-determination constructs are measured. Exclude datasets that only contain legal, administrative records of 'self-determination' (e.g. guardianship decisions) without psychological measures.

variables.desc: Variables capturing autonomy, basic psychological needs (autonomy, competence, relatedness), motivational regulations, and self-determination indices used in SDT research.
variables.narr: Relevant variables are item-level responses and computed scores for instruments such as the Basic Psychological Need Satisfaction scales, Self-Regulation Questionnaires, Intrinsic/Extrinsic Motivation scales, and autonomy-support measures. Include coding details, scales, and version/language information. Exclude variables that refer to legal self-determination status, capacity assessments unrelated to motivational constructs, or vague indicators without clear operationalization.

instruments_tools.desc: Measurement instruments and tools for assessing self-determination and SDT constructs (Basic Psychological Needs scales, Self-Regulation Questionnaires, autonomy-support measures) and their manuals or validation studies.
instruments_tools.narr: Relevant instruments include validated questionnaires for autonomy, competence, relatedness (e.g. Basic Psychological Need Satisfaction scales), General Causality Orientations Scale, Self-Regulation Questionnaires, and context-specific SDT measures (education, work, health). Include translations, psychometric evidence, administration and scoring guidelines. Exclude tools that measure unrelated legal or medical decision-making capacity without psychological autonomy/motivation content, and unvalidated ad-hoc items.

publication.desc: Academic publications on sexual orientation, including identity, attraction, behavior, social attitudes, discrimination, and health, especially in German-language research or German-speaking samples.
publication.narr: Relevant publications investigate sexual orientation (heterosexual, homosexual, bisexual, asexual, and other orientations), identity development, attraction and behavioral measures, minority stress, discrimination, legal and social status, and health disparities. Include empirical studies, policy reports, and theoretical work focused on German-speaking populations or comparative research including Germany/Austria/Switzerland. Exclude materials that conflate sexual orientation solely with gender identity without clear focus on orientation, or publications that only mention orientation peripherally without substantive analysis.

research_data.desc: Datasets containing measures of sexual orientation (identity, attraction, behavior), experiences of discrimination, and related health or social variables in German-speaking or comparative contexts.
research_data.narr: Relevant data include surveys and cohort studies with items on sexual identity, romantic/sexual attraction, sexual behavior, coming-out history, experiences of stigma or discrimination, mental and physical health indicators by orientation, and policy-related variables. Include datasets that provide clear variable coding for orientation and allow subgroup analyses. Exclude datasets without any sexual-orientation measures or with ambiguous/non-disaggregated sexual behavior items that cannot be linked to orientation.

variables.desc: Variables and codebooks for sexual orientation: self-identified orientation, attraction measures, sexual behavior items, and discrimination or minority stress indicators.
variables.narr: Relevant variables explicitly measure sexual orientation (self-identification categories), indices of attraction (who one is attracted to), sexual behavior variables (partners' sex/gender), and variables capturing experiences of prejudice, victimization, or social support by orientation. Include coding schemes, multi-response categories, and notes on how orientation categories were constructed. Exclude variables that only record partner sex without context for orientation and those conflating orientation with gender identity unless both are clearly distinguished.

instruments_tools.desc: Validated questionnaires and measurement modules for assessing sexual orientation, attraction, sexual behavior, minority stress, and related psychosocial constructs, including German-language instruments.
instruments_tools.narr: Relevant instruments include survey modules and scales for sexual identity labels, Kinsey-type attraction/behavior measures, the Lesbian, Gay, Bisexual Identity Scale adaptations, minority stress scales, and standardized health questionnaires that report outcomes by orientation, with German translations and validation where available. Include administration notes, ethical guidance for sensitive topics, and translation/back-translation documentation. Exclude clinical diagnostic tools unrelated to orientation, and unvalidated items lacking documentation on wording or ethical procedures for sensitive data collection.

publication.desc: Publications (articles, books, reports) that study the concept of 'meaning of work' (Sinn der Arbeit) including theoretical frameworks, empirical studies, cross-cultural comparisons, and policy implications.
publication.narr: Relevant publications are empirical and theoretical works explicitly addressing the meaning, purpose, sense, or meaningfulness of work or employment (including vocational calling, work values, and existential/work identity). Include studies in German or English that develop or apply measures of work meaningfulness, qualitative interview studies about workers' experiences, longitudinal or comparative research on changes in meaning of work, and policy or organizational analyses that discuss implications for wellbeing or HR practice. Exclude works that only mention 'work' in passing without addressing meaning (e.g., purely economic productivity studies), publications focused solely on job satisfaction or pay where meaningfulness is not a focus, and materials about volunteer work if they do not relate to perceived meaning of occupational activities.

research_data.desc: Datasets and study data that contain survey, interview, or administrative measures related to workers' perceptions of meaning, purpose, or meaningfulness in their work.
research_data.narr: Relevant datasets are quantitative surveys or qualitative interview corpora with variables or items capturing meaning of work, work values, sense of calling, meaningfulness scales (e.g., Work and Meaning Inventory), or open-ended responses about why work matters. Include cross-sectional, panel, or life-course datasets covering occupational groups, employees, or unemployed persons where questions target the psychological or social meaning of work. Exclude datasets solely about labor market status, wages, or performance metrics without attitudinal items about meaning; exclude datasets on leisure or volunteering unless they explicitly measure perceived meaning as part of work identity.

variables.desc: Variable descriptions and codebooks that measure constructs related to the meaning of work (e.g., meaningfulness scales, items on calling, work centrality, purpose).
variables.narr: Relevant variables are items or scales labeled as 'meaningful work', 'sense of purpose at work', 'calling', 'work centrality', or similar constructs, including their coding, response scales, and psychometric properties. Include derived scores, subscales, and show how missing values are coded. Exclude demographic or employment variables (occupation, hours) unless they explicitly operationalize meaning; exclude generic wellbeing indices that do not specifically target meaning in work contexts.

instruments_tools.desc: Survey instruments, questionnaires, interview guides, and validated scales used to assess the meaning of work and related constructs.
instruments_tools.narr: Include instruments such as the Work and Meaning Inventory (WAMI), Meaningful Work Scale, Calling and Vocation questionnaires, interview protocols for exploring work purpose, and translated/adapted German versions. Include manuals, validation studies, administration instructions, and scoring keys. Exclude general job satisfaction questionnaires or organizational climate tools that lack items on meaningfulness; exclude productivity measurement tools not intended to assess subjective meaning.

publication.desc: Publications on social media as a phenomenon, platform studies, user behavior, effects of social media, policy, and methodological approaches to studying social media.
publication.narr: Relevant publications explicitly focus on social media platforms, usage patterns, effects on communication/health/politics/economy, platform governance, content moderation, algorithmic impacts, social network analysis of social media, or methods for collecting/analyzing social media data. Include empirical studies, theoretical treatments, reviews, and comparative platform analyses. Exclude works that use 'social media' as a cursory example without substantive analysis, or publications solely about traditional media with no link to social media platforms.

research_data.desc: Datasets containing social media data or data about social media use (e.g., survey responses, harvested posts, network data, API-derived datasets).
research_data.narr: Include datasets of user-generated content from platforms (Twitter/X, Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, Reddit, etc.), social network graphs, topic-labeled corpora, survey data on social media use and attitudes, and observational datasets derived via APIs or scraping (with ethical documentation). Also include datasets combining social media behavior with survey or administrative variables. Exclude datasets that only mention 'social media' but contain no platform-specific measures, and exclude raw web crawl data unrelated to social platforms.

variables.desc: Variables and codebook entries that measure social media use, behaviors, attitudes, network metrics, and content characteristics.
variables.narr: Relevant variables include frequency and duration of platform use, platform-specific usage indicators, types of activities (posting, sharing, commenting), network measures (followers, degree centrality), engagement metrics (likes, shares), sentiment or topic labels, and self-reported attitudes toward social media. Include variable definitions, coding schemes, and derivations. Exclude variables unrelated to social media (e.g., general internet use without platform detail) or ambiguous variables with no documentation linking them to social media concepts.

instruments_tools.desc: Tools, software, coding schemes, and survey instruments designed to collect or analyze social media data, including APIs, scraping tools, content analysis codebooks, and validated questionnaires on social media use.
instruments_tools.narr: Include technical tools for harvesting and analyzing social media data (APIs, R/Python packages), codebooks for manual content analysis of social media posts, questionnaires measuring social media behavior or impacts, sentiment analysis models tailored to social platforms, and network analysis workflows for social media networks. Exclude general-purpose web tools not applied to social media contexts, and proprietary tools with no methodological documentation.

publication.desc: Publications reporting on surveys about social media use, attitudes toward social media, effects of social media, or methodology of surveying social media users.
publication.narr: Include empirical reports, articles, and technical notes that present survey results specifically about social media (frequency, motives, platform comparison), methodological discussions on surveying social media users (sampling, representativeness), and evaluations of survey modes for capturing social media behavior. Exclude general surveys that incidentally include a single unrelated question about social media without analysis, and qualitative studies without a survey component unless they present mixed-method survey findings.

research_data.desc: Survey datasets where the survey instrument is specifically about social media usage, attitudes, platform comparison, or related behaviors.
research_data.narr: Include cross-sectional and panel survey datasets focused on social media topics (e.g., digital media use surveys, national media panels with social media modules), with documentation of sampling, questionnaire, and variables. Datasets combining survey responses with social media trace data (linkage to profiles or posts) are relevant. Exclude datasets where social media is only a peripheral variable with no dedicated module, and exclude non-survey social media datasets (e.g., scraped posts) unless merged with survey data.

variables.desc: Survey variables measuring aspects of social media behavior, attitudes, motives, platform-specific use, and demographic correlates from social media-focused surveys.
variables.narr: Relevant variables capture self-reported frequency and intensity of platform use, purposes for use (information, socializing, news), trust in platforms, privacy concerns, multi-platform use, and willingness to engage. Include coding details, response options, and scales used for typical social media survey items. Exclude administrative or outcome variables unrelated to social media content or behavior.

instruments_tools.desc: Survey instruments, questionnaires, modules, and methodological guides tailored for surveying social media use and attitudes.
instruments_tools.narr: Include full questionnaires and modules measuring social media behavior (question wording, response categories), interviewer instructions for social media items, survey experiments on question wording for social media, and best-practice documentation for linking surveys to social media traces. Also include validated scales specific to social media research (e.g., scales for social media addiction, privacy concern). Exclude generic media use modules that do not differentiate social media platforms or lack methodological detail.

publication.desc: Publications in German or English studying social media use (Nutzung), including patterns, motives, demographics, effects, and cross-cultural comparisons of platform usage.
publication.narr: Relevant publications explicitly investigate 'social media use' (Nutzung), such as empirical analyses of usage frequency, platform preferences, usage contexts, age/gender differences in use, motivations for use, and consequences of use. Include national studies, panel analyses, and qualitative work focused on how people use social media. Exclude studies that discuss social media platforms theoretically without empirical focus on usage behavior, or those solely about technical platform features without linking to user behavior.

research_data.desc: Datasets documenting social media usage (Nutzung) via surveys, logs, or linked trace data, preferably with German-language instruments or samples from German-speaking populations.
research_data.narr: Include datasets capturing usage frequency, duration, platform-specific activities, motives, and demographic correlates. Particularly include German national media surveys, European media panels with social media modules, and datasets combining survey self-reports with platform log data. Exclude datasets that mention social media only as a control variable or lack substantive usage measures; exclude purely technical platform metrics without user context.

variables.desc: Variables that operationalize social media use (Nutzung): frequency, duration, platform-specific indicators, activity types, motives, and related demographic variables.
variables.narr: Relevant variables include self-reported frequency (daily/weekly), time spent, types of activities (posting, messaging, browsing), platform identifiers, motives for use, and cross-tabulations with age, education, and occupation. Include coding schemes and question wording, especially for German-language items. Exclude variables that measure only internet use without social media detail, or variables that are proxies for usage without clear operationalization.

instruments_tools.desc: Survey modules, questionnaires, coding schemes, and tools designed to measure social media use (Nutzung), including German-language instruments and cross-national modules.
instruments_tools.narr: Include validated questionnaire modules with item wording and response categories in German or translated versions that measure social media usage patterns and motives, as well as guidelines for administering social media usage items, diary tools for recording use, and tools for linking self-reports to digital trace data. Exclude generic internet-use instruments lacking social media specificity and technical scraping tools without user-focused measurement guidance.

publication.desc: Publications addressing the concept of social presence in communication, online learning, virtual teams, and computer-mediated environments, including theoretical development and empirical measurement.
publication.narr: Include theoretical and empirical studies that define, operationalize, or measure social presence (the sense of being with others) in online contexts such as e-learning, virtual collaboration, social media, and telecommunication. Include scale development/validation, experimental studies manipulating social presence, and meta-analyses. Exclude uses of the term 'presence' that refer only to physical presence, presence in public spaces without mediated interaction, or unrelated psychological constructs unless explicitly tied to social presence.

research_data.desc: Datasets containing measures of social presence from surveys, experiments, classroom studies, or platform evaluations, including psychometric data from scale validations.
research_data.narr: Relevant datasets include experimental data where social presence is manipulated or measured, survey data from online learners or remote workers including social presence scales, and datasets with repeated measures of perceived social presence. Include datasets from studies validating social presence instruments and linking presence scores to outcomes (engagement, learning, collaboration). Exclude datasets without explicit social presence items or those measuring only technological features (bandwidth) without subjective presence measures.

variables.desc: Variables that capture perceived social presence, social presence scale items, subscales (affective, co-presence, immediacy), and related constructs such as perceived intimacy or immediacy.
variables.narr: Include items and aggregated scores from established social presence measures (e.g., Short et al. social presence scale, Community of Inquiry presence indicators), coding, response scales, reliability statistics, and derived indices. Also include related constructs only if clearly linked theoretically (e.g., social intimacy in computer-mediated communication). Exclude generic engagement or satisfaction variables that do not specifically measure the subjective sense of others' presence.

instruments_tools.desc: Measurement instruments, validated scales, questionnaire modules, and experimental protocols for assessing or manipulating social presence in mediated environments.
instruments_tools.narr: Include full instruments and administration guides for social presence scales, coding manuals, experimental protocols for inducing social presence (e.g., avatar cues, video vs. text), and software tools that implement presence manipulations. Include psychometric validation reports and translation/adaptation documents. Exclude measurement tools unrelated to social presence (e.g., general usability tests) or tools that measure only technical connectivity without subjective presence assessment.

publication.desc: Publications (articles, books, reports, conference papers) addressing social phenomena, social policy, social welfare, social services, social behavior, or uses of the adjective 'sozial' in social-science contexts.
publication.narr: Include works whose primary focus is on social issues, social policy, social welfare, social behavior, social institutions or social theory; include empirical studies, theoretical analyses, reviews, and policy reports where 'sozial' denotes social aspects. Exclude records where 'sozial' appears only in organizational names, commercial product names, or as an incidental word without connection to social science topics; exclude purely medical uses unrelated to social dimensions unless they explicitly address social determinants or social aspects of health.

research_data.desc: Datasets and study collections that capture social variables or are described as social surveys, social statistics, administrative data on social policy, or other data used to study social phenomena.
research_data.narr: Include datasets labeled as social surveys, household surveys, social policy evaluations, social service administrative files, or any empirical data whose variables operationalize social constructs (e.g., welfare receipt, social participation, attitudes); include longitudinal and cross-sectional data relevant to social research. Exclude datasets that do not contain social variables (e.g., purely biological lab data) or where 'sozial' is only present in metadata without substantive social content.

variables.desc: Variables measuring social constructs such as social status, welfare receipt, social participation, social attitudes, social integration, and related demographic indicators.
variables.narr: Include variable names and descriptions that measure social constructs (e.g., social support, civic participation, welfare benefits, social capital, social inclusion/exclusion, social attitudes); include standard demographic covariates used in social analyses (age, gender, household composition) when presented as part of social-variable sets. Exclude variables unrelated to social constructs (technical or laboratory measures) or variables that only incidentally include the term 'sozial' without measuring a social concept.

instruments_tools.desc: Questionnaires, scales, coding manuals, and tools used to measure social phenomena (e.g., social attitudes scales, social capital instruments, survey modules on social policy) and software/methods for social-science analysis.
instruments_tools.narr: Include validated questionnaires, survey modules, coding schemes, measurement protocols, and methodological guides explicitly designed to assess social constructs (e.g., social support scales, social capital indices, social policy evaluation instruments) and analytic tools commonly used in social research. Exclude instruments whose use of 'social' is nominal or administrative only, and exclude technical tools unrelated to measuring social phenomena.

publication.desc: Publications on social competence (sozialkompetenz) including theory, measurement, development, interventions, education, and outcomes in children, adolescents, adults, and occupational contexts.
publication.narr: Include empirical studies, theoretical papers, reviews, and program evaluations that define, measure, or intervene on social competence (e.g., prosocial behavior, social skills, interpersonal competence, emotional regulation as part of social functioning) across settings (school, workplace, clinical). Include psychometric studies of social competence scales and cross-cultural comparisons. Exclude works that use the phrase only tangentially (e.g., listing 'social competence' among many unrelated factors without substantive focus), and exclude publications focused solely on unrelated competencies (technical, cognitive) unless linked to social competence.

research_data.desc: Datasets that contain measures of social competence or related constructs (peer ratings, teacher reports, self-reports of social skills, observational coding) often from educational, developmental, clinical, or workplace studies.
research_data.narr: Include datasets with variables explicitly labeled as measures of social competence, social skills, peer relations, prosocial behavior, or validated scales (e.g., Social Skills Rating System, Strengths and Difficulties Questionnaire subscales) and intervention trial data assessing effects on social competence. Exclude datasets lacking direct measures of social competence or that only include generic behavioral measures without mapping to social competence constructs.

variables.desc: Variables that operationalize social competence: standardized scale scores, items on social skills, peer/teacher ratings, emotion-regulation indices, prosocial behavior counts, and related behavioral observations.
variables.narr: Include variables labeled as social competence, social skills, interpersonal competence, peer acceptance/rejection, empathy, conflict resolution, cooperation, prosocial actions, and teacher/parent/peer ratings or observational coding schemes designed to measure social competence. Exclude variables that do not capture interpersonal or socio-emotional functioning or that measure only academic/cognitive abilities unless clearly linked to social competence constructs.

instruments_tools.desc: Measurement instruments and tools for assessing social competence: standardized questionnaires, observational coding manuals, teacher/parent rating scales, intervention manuals, and assessment batteries.
instruments_tools.narr: Include validated instruments (e.g., Social Skills Rating System, SSRS; Social Competence Inventory; SDQ subscales when used for social skills), coding protocols for social interactions, program manuals for social-skills training, and psychometric documentation. Include tools for scoring and interpreting social competence measures. Exclude generic personality inventories or competence instruments that do not assess interpersonal/social domains unless a specific subscale measures social competence.

publication.desc: Scholarly and policy publications on social inequality (soziale Ungleichheit): causes, patterns, measurement, consequences across income, education, health, gender, race/ethnicity, region, and life course.
publication.narr: Include empirical analyses, theoretical treatments, comparative studies, and policy evaluations that focus on social inequality, social stratification, distributive outcomes, mobility, poverty, or disparities in well-being. Include cross-national, longitudinal, and cohort studies and works that operationalize inequality (Gini, percentiles, gradients). Exclude publications where inequality is mentioned only peripherally, or studies of purely technical inequality measures in non-social domains (e.g., algorithmic inequality) unless explicitly linked to social inequality.

research_data.desc: Datasets relevant to studying social inequality: household surveys, income/expenditure data, longitudinal cohort studies, administrative registers, social mobility data, and inequality-focused cross-national datasets.
research_data.narr: Include datasets that provide measures of income, wealth, education, occupation, employment, health outcomes, social mobility, poverty indicators, and demographic covariates necessary for inequality research. Include administrative and register data used for distributional analysis. Exclude datasets that lack information on socio-economic position or outcomes of interest for inequality research, or datasets focused solely on non-social technical measures.

variables.desc: Variables used to measure social inequality: income, wages, wealth, consumption/expenditure, education level, occupational status, social class, poverty status, Gini coefficient and inequality indices, and health/social outcome gradients.
variables.narr: Include individual- and household-level socioeconomic variables (gross/net income, assets, educational attainment, occupational codes, employment status), constructed inequality metrics (Gini, Theil, percentiles, decile ratios), poverty thresholds, and outcome variables commonly analyzed for inequality (mortality, morbidity, educational achievement). Exclude variables unrelated to socio-economic position or distributional outcomes.

instruments_tools.desc: Measurement tools and methods for inequality research: survey modules, coding schemes for SES, wealth indexing methods, poverty measurement guidelines, decomposition techniques, and software packages for inequality analysis.
instruments_tools.narr: Include instruments such as standardized income/consumption questionnaires, occupational coding manuals (ISCO, EGP), wealth imputation protocols, poverty and deprivation indices, analytic guides on inequality measures and decomposition, and software tools (e.g., Stata/R packages) for computing inequality statistics. Exclude tools that do not pertain to social or economic distributional analysis.

publication.desc: Publications addressing social class (soziale Schicht), class stratification, class identity, class mobility, and class-related measurement and theory in sociology and related fields.
publication.narr: Include empirical and theoretical works that define, measure, or analyze social class/stratum, class effects on life chances, class consciousness, and class-based inequalities; include comparative and historical studies and research using class schemas (e.g., EGP, Goldthorpe). Exclude uses of 'Schicht' in geological or technical contexts or studies that use occupational labels without interpreting them as class or stratification variables.

research_data.desc: Datasets containing measures of social class: surveys with occupational codes, education and income measures, class categorizations, social mobility panels, and life-course studies suitable for class analysis.
research_data.narr: Include datasets that allow derivation of class positions (detailed occupation codes, employment status, education, income) and that are used for class-stratification or mobility research (e.g., cross-sectional surveys, mobility matrices, longitudinal cohorts). Exclude datasets lacking occupational detail or socio-economic indicators necessary to assign class categories.

variables.desc: Variables relevant to social class: occupational codes (ISCO, national classifications), class schema assignments (EGP, NS-SEC), education, income, status/prestige scores, parental class/origin variables, and subjective social class measures.
variables.narr: Include variables that record occupation, industry, employment status, education level, income/wealth, measures of social status/prestige, parental occupation/education for origin, and subjective class identification items. Exclude variables that cannot be mapped to class positions (vague job titles without coding) or that pertain to non-social 'layers' (e.g., geological strata).

instruments_tools.desc: Instruments and tools for measuring and analysing social class: occupational coding manuals, class schema conversion tools, social status scales, mobility tables, and methodology guides for class assignment.
instruments_tools.narr: Include coding manuals (ISCO, national occupational codes), conversion tables to class schemes (EGP, NS-SEC), guides for constructing class variables, status/prestige scales (e.g., SIOPS), and software or scripts for assigning class categories and analysing mobility. Exclude tools unrelated to social-stratification measurement.

publication.desc: Publications on social networks (soziale Netzwerke), including theory, empirical network studies, social network analysis (SNA), online/offline networks, social capital, and diffusion processes.
publication.narr: Include theoretical and empirical studies that investigate social ties, network structures, social capital, diffusion, influence, and methodological work on SNA; include applications across sociology, communication, public health, organizations, and political science. Exclude studies using 'network' in purely technical or computer-networking contexts unless they explicitly study social relations or human-centered networks.

research_data.desc: Network datasets: ego-network and whole-network surveys, communication logs mapped to social ties, collaboration/co-authorship networks, organizational network data, and longitudinal network panels.
research_data.narr: Include data that represent interpersonal ties (friendship, advice, support), affiliation networks, communication/contact records used as proxies for social ties, and time-series or panel network data suitable for SNA. Include datasets with node and edge attributes enabling network analysis. Exclude datasets representing non-social technical networks (e.g., computer topology) or lacking relational information.

variables.desc: Variables and indicators used in social network research: ties (presence/strength/type), degree, centrality measures, density, betweenness, reciprocity, network size, multiplexity, homophily indicators, and tie-strength proxies.
variables.narr: Include variables describing relational data (edge lists, adjacency matrices), tie attributes (frequency, duration, type), node attributes relevant to network positioning (role, attributes used for homophily), and computed network metrics (degree, centrality, clustering). Exclude variables that describe only individual attributes without any relational component unless used to model network formation or influence.

instruments_tools.desc: Instruments, questionnaires, and software for measuring and analysing social networks: name-generator modules, roster-based network instruments, coding manuals, SNA software (e.g., UCINET, Gephi, igraph), and methodological guides for network data collection and analysis.
instruments_tools.narr: Include validated network survey instruments (name generators, interpreters), protocols for observational/social-sensing data collection, documentation for coding ties, tutorials and software packages for network analysis, and methodological literature on network inference and visualization. Exclude general survey instruments that do not include relational modules and tools focused solely on non-social network technologies.

publication.desc: Publications that study interpersonal social contacts, networks and contact frequency/quality across populations (e.g., social network studies, loneliness/contact deprivation, contact patterns during COVID-19, time-use/contact-diary research).
publication.narr: Include empirical articles, reviews, books and reports that explicitly address social contacts, ties or contact patterns (keywords: social contacts, contact frequency, social ties, social network, contact diary, social isolation, social support). Relevant populations: children, adolescents, adults, elderly, and specific groups (immigrants, patients). Include cross-sectional and longitudinal research, comparative and country-specific studies. Exclude items that use the word 'contact' only in unrelated senses (e.g., business contacts with no interpersonal/social content) or purely theoretical works that do not address measurable social contact constructs.

research_data.desc: Datasets containing measures of social contact or networks (e.g., contact diaries, egocentric network modules, time-use surveys, longitudinal panel data with contact items such as SOEP, SHARE, network modules, COVID contact studies).
research_data.narr: Include microdata and aggregate datasets that capture number, frequency, type (face-to-face, phone, online), or quality of social contacts and networks. Accept diary/contact-matrix data, sociometric/network datasets, and modules within large surveys measuring social ties or isolation. Exclude datasets that do not include any measure of interpersonal contact (e.g., only economic indicators) or that mention 'contact' in administrative/business contexts.

variables.desc: Variables that measure number/size of contacts, contact frequency, contact type, network composition, perceived social support and measures of social isolation/loneliness related to social contacts.
variables.narr: Include variable names and codes for: network size, number of close friends, frequency of meeting family/friends, daily/weekly contact counts, contact diary entries, types of contact (in-person/telephone/online), perceived availability of support, and indices of social integration/isolation. Also include derived measures (e.g., average daily contacts, proportion of weak/strong ties). Exclude demographic variables that are not used to indicate social contact (unless they are combined to form contact measures).

instruments_tools.desc: Validated instruments and tools for measuring social contacts and networks (e.g., contact diaries, name-generator/name-interpreter questionnaires, Lubben Social Network Scale, Berkman–Syme Social Network Index, network analysis software/tools).
instruments_tools.narr: Include paper/electronic contact-diary protocols, structured social network questionnaires (egocentric and sociometric), standardized scales addressing network size/support, and methodological guides for collecting/processing contact data. Include validation studies and translations. Exclude instruments unrelated to interpersonal contacts (e.g., general survey modules without contact measures).

publication.desc: Publications on social interaction processes and behaviours at micro- and meso-levels (e.g., conversational analysis, face-to-face interaction, group interaction, interaction patterns in organizations, observational and experimental studies).
publication.narr: Include empirical and theoretical works that explicitly examine social interaction, interactional dynamics, communication behaviors, and situational/interpersonal processes (keywords: social interaction, interactional patterns, conversation analysis, nonverbal behavior, microinteraction). Include laboratory experiments, field observations, ethnographies, and interaction coding studies. Exclude broad papers that mention social interaction only tangentially or use the term metaphorically without studying interactional processes.

research_data.desc: Datasets derived from observational coding, conversation transcripts, interaction experiments, sensor-based interaction logs, and video/audio corpora capturing social interactions.
research_data.narr: Include annotated transcripts, coded observational datasets (with interaction categories, turn-taking, gesture codes), wearable sensor datasets measuring proximity/interactions, and lab experiment data on interactive tasks. Accept datasets that permit analysis of micro-level behavior (timing, sequencing) and group interaction structures. Exclude datasets that only include high-level social indicators without direct interaction measures.

variables.desc: Variables capturing interaction frequency, turn-taking counts, speech acts, nonverbal behaviors, synchronization, conversational dominance, cooperative/competitive interaction measures, and situational context of interactions.
variables.narr: Include variables such as number of interactions, duration, initiator/respondent roles, number of speaking turns, interruption counts, gesture occurrences, gaze, proxemic measures, codings of interaction quality (e.g., cooperation, conflict), and timestamps for sequence analysis. Also include contextual variables (setting, group size). Exclude generic attitudinal items that do not directly measure interaction behavior.

instruments_tools.desc: Tools and instruments for studying social interaction: observational coding schemes, conversation-analysis frameworks, behavioral coding manuals, sensor/toolkits (Bluetooth proximity, sociometric badges), video annotation software, and validated interaction scales.
instruments_tools.narr: Include standardized coding schemes and manuals, instruments for measuring nonverbal and verbal interaction (e.g., Roter Interaction Analysis System, conversation-analysis methods), software for annotation and sequence analysis (e.g., ELAN, NVivo, BORIS), and details about sensor devices and preprocessing pipelines. Exclude general survey instruments not designed to capture moment-to-moment interaction.

publication.desc: Publications addressing the social validity of vocational programs, workplace interventions and employment-related measures — i.e., acceptability, relevance and social importance of interventions in occupational contexts.
publication.narr: Include empirical evaluations, program reports and theoretical discussions that assess social validity in employment/vocational settings (keywords: social validity, acceptability, vocational training, workplace intervention, job coaching, employment programs). Include stakeholder perspectives (participants, employers), feasibility/acceptability studies, and outcome evaluations that report social validity indicators. Exclude generic validity literature (psychometric validity) unless explicitly about social validity in vocational contexts.

research_data.desc: Datasets from program evaluations and surveys that include measures of social validity, stakeholder satisfaction, perceived relevance/acceptability of work interventions, and employment outcomes linked to social validity assessments.
research_data.narr: Include quantitative and qualitative datasets from vocational training evaluations, job-placement programs, disability employment services, and workplace accommodation studies that record participant/employer ratings of acceptability, goals' importance, feasibility, implementation fidelity, and subsequent employment outcomes. Exclude administrative employment data without measures of perceived acceptability or social relevance.

variables.desc: Variables measuring perceived acceptability, relevance, satisfaction, feasibility, goal importance, stakeholder endorsement, and employment outcomes used to assess social validity in work settings.
variables.narr: Include items/scales for acceptability (e.g., treatment acceptability ratings), satisfaction with training/program, perceived usefulness/relevance to job goals, willingness-to-participate, employer acceptance, and linked objective outcomes (job attainment, retention). Also include qualitative codes for stakeholder comments about acceptability. Exclude unrelated psychometric validity indicators (construct validity) unless linked to social validity constructs.

instruments_tools.desc: Instruments and tools for assessing social validity in vocational and workplace contexts: social validity scales, acceptability questionnaires, qualitative interview guides, stakeholder feedback protocols and program-fidelity checklists adapted for employment interventions.
instruments_tools.narr: Include validated social validity measures and structured interview guides used in vocational rehabilitation and workplace intervention research, instruments for measuring feasibility/acceptability, and templates for stakeholder evaluation. Include translations and context-specific adaptations. Exclude clinical psychometric instruments that do not assess social relevance/acceptability.

publication.desc: Publications on social origin/background and its effects — parental socioeconomic status, education, occupation, cultural capital and intergenerational mobility across education, income and occupations.
publication.narr: Include empirical studies, reviews and theoretical works that explicitly address social origin, social background, or parental SES as determinants of life-course outcomes (keywords: social origin, parental background, intergenerational mobility, social class, family background). Cover education, labor-market outcomes, health and inequality research linking parental circumstances to offspring outcomes. Exclude works focusing only on individual adult SES without reference to family origin.

research_data.desc: Datasets that record parental/household background: cohort studies, longitudinal panels and surveys with parental education, occupation and income (e.g., SOEP, PISA, cohort studies, microcensus, SHARE).
research_data.narr: Include datasets enabling analysis of social origin and intergenerational transmission: birth cohorts, school-leaver panels, household surveys with retrospective parental information, and administrative matched parent-child records. Accept data with parental occupation codes, education levels, household income and indicators of cultural resources. Exclude datasets lacking any parental/background measures.

variables.desc: Variables characterizing social origin: parental education, parental occupation (ISCO/EGP/ISEI), parental income/wealth, family class indicators, childhood socioeconomic status, and cultural capital measures (books at home, parental cultural participation).
variables.narr: Include variable names and codes for mother/father education, highest parental qualification, parental occupational status indices (ISEI, EGP, ISEI scores), household income during childhood, social class categories, and proxies for cultural capital. Also include derived measures of intergenerational mobility (e.g., status transmission matrices). Exclude adult-only SES indicators that do not reference parental/background status.

instruments_tools.desc: Classification schemes and tools for measuring social origin: occupational classifications (ISCO, EGP), status indices (ISEI, SIOPS), education classification systems (ISCED, CASMIN), and survey modules for childhood background.
instruments_tools.narr: Include manuals and coding schemes for occupation-to-status conversion, education classification crosswalks, questionnaire modules for collecting parental background, and tools to construct composite social origin indices. Include guidance on harmonizing parental indicators across waves/countries. Exclude tools unrelated to measuring family background (e.g., adult job-satisfaction scales).

publication.desc: Publications on social inequality and stratification across domains (income, wealth, education, health, gender, ethnicity), including causes, consequences, trends and policy responses.
publication.narr: Include empirical analyses, theoretical treatments and policy studies that address patterns and drivers of social inequality (keywords: social inequality, inequality, social stratification, income inequality, health disparities, educational inequality). Cover cross-country comparisons, longitudinal trend studies, and evaluations of redistributive policies. Exclude narrowly technical econometric papers that mention inequality only as a secondary topic without substantive analysis.

research_data.desc: Datasets relevant to studying social inequality: household/individual surveys, income and wealth panels, labor-force surveys, EU-SILC, SOEP, LIS, OECD datasets, administrative tax/earnings records and health disparity datasets.
research_data.narr: Include microdata and aggregate data that permit measurement of distributional outcomes (income, consumption, wealth), social gradients (health, education), and subgroup disparities (gender, migrant status). Include longitudinal panels for mobility analysis and international harmonized datasets used in comparative inequality research. Exclude datasets that lack distributional or subgroup indicators.

variables.desc: Variables used in inequality research: income, wages, household consumption, wealth, educational attainment, occupational status, health indicators, poverty status, Gini, percentiles, and measures of social mobility and group membership (gender, ethnicity).
variables.narr: Include raw and derived variables for inequality analysis (gross/net income, equivalised household income, wealth measures), summary inequality statistics (Gini coefficient, decile ratios, concentration index), poverty measures, and indicators of socio-demographic groups. Also include mobility transition variables. Exclude variables that cannot be linked to distributional analysis (e.g., single-item non-comparable administrative codes).

instruments_tools.desc: Analytical tools and instruments for inequality research: measures and indices (Gini, Theil, Atkinson), decomposition methods, poverty measurement tools, inequality decomposition software, and survey modules commonly used to measure income/wealth/consumption.
instruments_tools.narr: Include methodological manuals and software implementations for inequality metrics, decomposition techniques (Oaxaca, Shapley), poverty measurement toolkits, and harmonization guides for cross-national comparison. Also include survey instruments for collecting income, consumption and wealth data. Exclude tools focused on unrelated statistical domains without application to distributional analysis.

publication.desc: Publications (articles, reports, books, theses) that study or review 'social competence' (soziale Kompetenz) as an individual-level construct: definitions, development, determinants, correlates, interventions and outcomes across age groups and contexts (children, adolescents, adults, workplace, schools, clinical settings). Includes empirical studies, systematic reviews and theoretical papers in German or English that explicitly operationalize or measure social competence or closely related constructs (social skills, interpersonal competence, prosocial behavior, emotional competence).
publication.narr: Relevant: empirical or theoretical works whose main focus is individual social competence or directly comparable constructs (e.g., interpersonal skills, social-emotional competence), including intervention evaluations and developmental studies. Include works in educational, clinical, organizational or community contexts. Not relevant: publications that use 'competence' only in organizational/occupational senses (e.g., institutional competence), broad constructs like social capital or social inclusion unless they explicitly measure individual social competence, or purely technological descriptions without human social-skill content.

research_data.desc: Datasets and study data that measure social competence or closely related indicators: standardized scale scores, observational coding of social interaction, teacher/parent/peer ratings, longitudinal panel data with social-skill measures, intervention trial data with pre/post social competence outcomes. Includes raw/processed survey data, observational video/audio files with coding schemes, and dataset documentation.
research_data.narr: Relevant: datasets containing explicit measures of social competence (e.g., validated scale scores, social skill ratings, observational codes) or items clearly mapped to the construct across age groups and settings. Include datasets from field trials, longitudinal cohorts, school assessments and clinical studies. Not relevant: datasets that only include general social-demographic variables, datasets about organizational performance, or datasets mentioning 'social' in other contexts (e.g., social media metrics) without individual social competence measures.

variables.desc: Variables and variable descriptions that operationalize social competence and related dimensions: social skills scores, empathy measures, prosocial behavior frequency, peer acceptance/rejection, conflict resolution ability, communication skills, emotional regulation, teacher/parent/peer ratings, observational interaction codes and composite indices of social competence.
variables.narr: Relevant: variable names and metadata that clearly measure individual-level social competence or subcomponents (e.g., 'Social Skills Total Score', 'Empathy Scale', 'Peer Nomination: liked most', 'Observed prosocial acts per hour'). Include variables from psychometric instruments and observational protocols. Not relevant: variables labelled only 'social' without relation to interpersonal competence (e.g., social class, social support) or variables measuring macro-level social phenomena (e.g., community cohesion) unless explicitly linked to individual social competence.
